F401.role: Ward discharge coordinator (senior nurse) reviewing one inpatient's discharge readiness record on the day of planned discharge
F401.setting: An acute medical ward's discharge planning system assembles a readiness record for each patient listed for discharge. The record combines admission details, the last 24 hours of observations and pending investigations, the medicines reconciliation against the discharge prescription, therapy and social assessments with any care arrangements, and the discharge checklist with transport and pharmacy timings. The coordinator reviews each record and decides whether the patient can go, where to, how prepared the discharge is, and how far it will slip from the planned time.

rx_matches.instructions: Discharge prescription matches the reconciled inpatient medication list.

next_step.instructions: What should happen with this discharge now?

criteria.discharge_now: Everything is in place; patient leaves as planned without further action.
criteria.request_item: One required section or item is missing; obtain it before deciding.
criteria.conditional_discharge: Discharge proceeds once named outstanding tasks are completed on the day.
criteria.escalate_senior: A clinical, capacity or identity concern needs a senior clinician's decision.

destination.instructions: Which discharge destination does the current evidence support?

criteria.home_independent: Home with no new care, equipment or rehabilitation needed.
criteria.home_with_package: Home with new care visits or equipment, start date confirmed.
criteria.intermediate_care: Short-term reablement or step-down bed for ongoing rehabilitation.
criteria.care_home: Permanent residential or nursing placement for continuous care needs.
criteria.remain_inpatient: No safe destination arranged yet, so patient stays on ward.

outstanding_tasks.instructions: How many discharge checklist tasks remain genuinely outstanding?
criteria: Complete: no checklist tasks outstanding
Minor gap: exactly one checklist task outstanding
Partial: two or three checklist tasks outstanding
Unprepared: four or more checklist tasks outstanding

discharge_delay.instructions: How long after the planned discharge time can the patient leave?
criteria: Ready by the planned discharge date and time
Same day, but after the planned discharge time
One or two days after the planned date
Three or more days after the planned date

factors.name: rx_discrepancy
factors.description: Difference between the reconciled inpatient medication list and the discharge prescription: none, a mere unit expression difference (1 g vs 1000 mg, brand vs generic name), a dose or frequency difference, a drug omitted, or a drug added.

factors.name: rx_change_documented
factors.description: Whether a real discrepancy is covered by a matching entry in the medication change log (drug, action, reason, prescriber, dated before the prescription was signed), making it an intentional, reconciled change.

factors.name: obs_pattern
factors.description: Pattern of vital signs over the last 24 hours: all within normal ranges, one isolated abnormal set, or repeated abnormal sets (e.g. low SpO2, raised respiratory rate, tachycardia).

factors.name: obs_baseline_documented
factors.description: Whether the clinical section records a patient-specific baseline or adjusted target (e.g. SpO2 target 88-92% for chronic lung disease, chronic rate-controlled AF) that explains the abnormal readings.

factors.name: senior_fit_review
factors.description: Whether a consultant or registrar recorded a fit-for-discharge review; it mitigates abnormal observations only if timestamped after the latest abnormal set, and is sometimes timestamped before it.

factors.name: pending_result
factors.description: State of investigations at review: none pending, awaited but flagged as not needed before discharge with a named follow-up owner, awaited and flagged as required before discharge, or resulted abnormal with no acknowledgement recorded.

factors.name: missing_section
factors.description: A required part of the record that is null or absent: none, the therapy functional assessment, the social history, or the discharge prescription itself.

factors.name: outstanding_task_count
factors.description: Number of discharge checklist tasks (e.g. TTO dispensed, discharge letter sent, cannula removed, district nurse referral, equipment delivered) whose status is not done, including tasks only falsely marked done.

factors.name: false_completion
factors.description: Whether one checklist task is marked done but has completed_at null, no signed_by, or a completion time earlier than its prerequisite (e.g. TTO dispensed before the prescription was signed), so it actually counts as outstanding.

factors.name: care_need
factors.description: Level of support the patient needs on leaving, inferred from therapy fields (mobility aid, transfer assistance count, ADL score) against social fields (lives alone, carer availability, prior package): none, a new home package or equipment, short-term rehabilitation, or permanent 24-hour care.

factors.name: care_arrangement_status
factors.description: State of the care arrangement matching the need: not required, confirmed with start on or before planned discharge, confirmed with a later start date, requested with no start date, or declined by the provider or patient.

factors.name: logistics_delay
factors.description: Timing of transport and pharmacy readiness relative to the planned discharge time: both before it, one later the same day, one on the next day, or transport booked with the date but a null pickup time.

factors.name: identifier_consistency
factors.description: Whether the patient identifier is consistent across sections: identical, differing only in formatting (spaces or leading zeros), or a genuinely different number in the medications section.

factors.name: capacity_safeguarding_open
factors.description: Whether a mental capacity assessment about the discharge decision is pending or a safeguarding referral is open without an outcome.

sections.name: patient
sections.description: Identifier, ward, admission date, admitting condition code, planned_discharge_at datetime, and flags for capacity or safeguarding status.

sections.name: clinical
sections.description: List of observation sets from the last 24 hours, documented baselines or targets, senior review entries, and investigations with status.

sections.name: medications
sections.description: Patient identifier, reconciled inpatient list, change log entries, discharge prescription items with signed_at, and pharmacy ready time.

sections.name: function_social
sections.description: Therapy assessment (mobility aid, transfer assistance, ADL score), social history, and care arrangement with provider status and start date.

sections.name: discharge_tasks
sections.description: Checklist items with status, completed_at and signed_by, plus transport booking date, pickup time and destination address type.

F401.rendering_notes: patient.planned_discharge_at is the reference for all timing. rx_discrepancy appears only by comparing medications.reconciled[] (drug, dose, unit, frequency) with medications.discharge_rx[]; unit_expression_only is a decoy (1 g vs 1000 mg, brand vs generic) and still counts as matching. rx_change_documented is an entry in medications.changes[] naming the drug, action and reason with a prescriber and changed_at before discharge_rx signed_at; when present the discrepancy is reconciled and rx_matches is true, but an entry dated after signing or naming a different drug does not cover it. If missing_section is discharge_rx_absent, medications.discharge_rx is null and rx_matches is false. obs_pattern is shown only as raw parameters in clinical.obs[] (resp_rate, spo2, systolic_bp, heart_rate, temp, consciousness, recorded_at); no aggregate early warning score or stability label is ever given. obs_baseline_documented is clinical.targets with an adjusted spo2_target or rate note; senior_fit_review is clinical.reviews[] with role, outcome fit_for_discharge and reviewed_at, which only mitigates if reviewed_at is after the last abnormal obs. pending_result is clinical.investigations[] with status, required_before_discharge boolean, follow_up_owner and acknowledged_at (null when unactioned). missing_section renders the relevant object as null or omits it. outstanding_task_count and false_completion appear in discharge_tasks.items[] statuses; there is no count field, and a done item with null completed_at, null signed_by, or completed_at before its prerequisite counts as outstanding. care_need is inferred from function_social.therapy (mobility_aid, transfer_assist_count, adl_score) against social (lives_alone, carer_available, existing_package) and is never stated; care_arrangement_status is function_social.care_arrangement with type, status and start_date (null when requested_no_date). logistics_delay is discharge_tasks.transport (booked_date, pickup_time, null when unknown) and medications.pharmacy_ready_at. identifier_consistency compares patient.id with medications.patient_id; format_only is a decoy. capacity_safeguarding_open shows as patient.capacity_assessment status pending or patient.safeguarding_referral open with null outcome. Answer logic: next_step is escalate_senior for repeated or unmitigated abnormal obs without a later senior review, abnormal_unactioned results, a true identifier mismatch or an open capacity/safeguarding item; otherwise request_item when exactly one required section is null or a blocking result is awaited; otherwise conditional_discharge when tasks are outstanding or the delay is same-day; otherwise discharge_now. discharge_delay takes the latest of care start date, transport and pharmacy times; requested_no_date or declined count as three or more days; a null pickup time on the planned date is the deliberately contested boundary between the first two levels. destination is remain_inpatient when a needed arrangement has no confirmed start date. No field states readiness, destination, delay, task count or match result.

F402.role: Community physiotherapy triage clinician reviewing incoming referrals one at a time
F402.setting: A community physiotherapy service receives referrals from GPs, hospital wards and first-contact practitioners. Each referral arrives as a structured record that joins the referral form, patient demographics, coded clinical findings, an extract from the GP record, attachments and service history. The triage clinician checks the record against itself and decides on the next step, the service pathway, whether red flags remain open, and how soon the patient must be seen. Codes and flags only; there are no free-text notes.

red_flag_unresolved.instructions: The referral contains a red-flag finding with no documented benign explanation.

criteria.true: Red flag recorded and nothing in record explains it.
criteria.false: No red flag, or one explained by documented review.

next_step.instructions: What should the triage clinician do with this referral now?

criteria.accept_as_referred: Add to waiting list at stated priority without any queries.
criteria.request_info: Ask referrer for one named missing item before triaging.
criteria.book_amended: Book now with corrected priority, side or stated precautions.
criteria.escalate_lead: Pass to clinical lead or GP for urgent medical review.

pathway.instructions: Which service pathway best fits this patient's confirmed presentation?

criteria.self_management: Stable, low-impact symptoms suited to advice and exercise resources.
criteria.community_msk: Musculoskeletal problem needing face-to-face physiotherapy in community clinic.
criteria.specialist_rehab: Neurological, frailty or post-operative needs requiring specialist rehabilitation team.
criteria.redirect_out: Problem outside physiotherapy scope; needs medical or surgical service.

reversal_time.instructions: How long would it take to fully undo this outcome?
criteria: Could be fully undone within one day
Needs one to seven days to undo
Needs eight days to three months to undo
Cannot be undone within three months

clinical_urgency.instructions: How soon must this patient have first clinical contact?
criteria: Can safely wait more than six weeks
First contact needed within six weeks
First contact needed within two weeks
Medical review needed within 48 hours

factors.name: red_flag_type
factors.description: Which serious-pathology indicator, if any, is coded in the clinical findings

factors.name: red_flag_mitigated
factors.description: Whether a benign explanation is documented for the red flag, such as a recent normal MRI, a dated GP or emergency review, or an oncology discharge with clear surveillance

factors.name: mismatch_field
factors.description: Which corresponding value disagrees between sections, if any

factors.name: mismatch_magnitude
factors.description: Size of the disagreement: trivial (typo-level, e.g. one day, matching NHS number), moderate (weeks of onset, wrong side on one of two documents), major (wrong patient identifiers, anticoagulant omitted, months apart)

factors.name: missing_item
factors.description: One item the service needs that is absent or null

factors.name: condition_group
factors.description: Underlying presentation category as shown by coded diagnosis and findings

factors.name: symptom_duration_weeks
factors.description: Weeks since symptom onset per referral; values near 6 and 12 sit on service boundaries

factors.name: function_index
factors.description: Patient-reported disability index, 0 best to 100 worst; values around 40 and 60 are borderline

factors.name: prior_episodes_12m
factors.description: Number of previous physiotherapy episodes for the same problem in the last 12 months

factors.name: referrer_priority
factors.description: Priority ticked by referrer; a decoy that often disagrees with the clinical picture

factors.name: falls_last_3m
factors.description: Number of falls in last three months recorded in the GP extract

factors.name: post_op_days
factors.description: Days since surgery when condition is post-operative; drives protocol timing

factors.name: self_mgmt_tried
factors.description: Whether a documented trial of advice or exercise resources has already been completed

sections.name: referral
sections.description: Referral id, source, received date, referrer priority, body site and side, onset date

sections.name: patient
sections.description: Pseudonymous id, NHS number, date of birth, mobility aid, consent flag

sections.name: clinical
sections.description: Coded diagnosis, red-flag codes, neuro signs, function index, anticoagulant boolean, surgery date, weight-bearing status

sections.name: gp_record
sections.description: GP extract: DOB, medication codes, first-presented date, falls count, recent review dates

sections.name: attachments
sections.description: List of documents with type, date, side and result code, e.g. imaging or op protocol

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior physiotherapy episodes with dates, discharge reason codes and self-management trial flag

F402.rendering_notes: red_flag_type appears only as codes in clinical.red_flags (list, empty when none) and clinical.neuro_signs (e.g. {"progression":"worsening"}); gp_record.weight_change_kg may support night_pain_weight_loss. red_flag_mitigated shows indirectly: an attachments entry of type MRI dated within 8 weeks with result "no_sinister", gp_record.reviews containing a dated urgent review after the flag's onset, or history containing an oncology_discharge code; when false these are absent, dated before onset, or show result "pending". mismatch_field renders as disagreeing corresponding values: referral.site.side vs attachments[].side (laterality); patient.dob vs gp_record.dob (date_of_birth); referral.onset_date vs gp_record.first_presented (symptom_onset); clinical.anticoagulant=false while gp_record.meds lists an anticoagulant code (anticoagulant_status); clinical.surgery_date vs attachments op_protocol date (surgery_date). mismatch_magnitude sets the gap size; trivial mismatches are decoys that should not change the decision. Mismatches are never flagged by any field. missing_item renders as null or absent: attachments lacks the imaging or op_protocol entry, clinical.weight_bearing is null, patient.consent_to_refer is null. condition_group is inferred from clinical.diagnosis_code plus neuro signs, surgery date and falls; non_physio_surgical shows as e.g. a diagnosis code with an attachment recommending surgical opinion. symptom_duration_weeks is derived from referral.onset_date relative to referral.received; function_index sits in clinical.function_index; prior_episodes_12m is the count of history.episodes within 12 months; self_mgmt_tried is history.self_mgmt_trial (true/false/null). referrer_priority sits in referral.priority and is a decoy, often contradicted by findings or mitigation. falls_last_3m sits in gp_record.falls_3m; post_op_days derived from clinical.surgery_date. No field ever states triage outcome, pathway, urgency band, red-flag status or a recommended action; there is no free-text note anywhere. Balance roughly half of red-flag records with mitigation, and place some values on boundaries (onset near 6 weeks, function index near 40 or 60, one fall) so judges may split.

F403.role: School catering allergen plan reviewer, who checks each pupil's individual allergen meal plan before and during its use in a school kitchen
F403.setting: A local authority school catering service keeps one allergen meal plan per pupil with a diagnosed food allergy. Each plan links the pupil's declared allergens and medical evidence to a mapped menu cycle and to the serving kitchen's controls, with a short history of reviews and incidents. The reviewer opens one plan at a time. For each plan they decide whether it can be released, how exposed the pupil is, where the plan first falls short, and how soon it matters.

evidence_allergens_covered.instructions: Every allergen in the medical evidence has a mapped menu substitution.

next_step.instructions: What should the reviewer do with this allergen plan now?

criteria.approve_plan: Plan complete and safe; release to kitchen unchanged.
criteria.request_evidence: Ask family for current clinician-signed allergy evidence before deciding.
criteria.approve_restricted: Release now with the single affected dish withheld.
criteria.return_for_rework: Hold release; two or more dishes need remapping first.
criteria.escalate_to_lead: Refer to catering safety lead after a served allergen exposure.

first_gap_stage.instructions: At which stage does the plan first fall short?

criteria.no_gap: Evidence current, every dish mapped, kitchen controls all verified.
criteria.evidence_gap: Medical evidence missing, expired or lacking clinician confirmation.
criteria.menu_gap: Evidence sound, but a dish or recipe is unmapped.
criteria.kitchen_gap: Evidence and menu sound, but a kitchen control is unverified.

exposure_proximity.instructions: How close has a declared allergen come to the pupil's plate?
criteria: Blocked: every allergen dish substituted, all controls verified
Guarded: dishes all substituted; at least one control unverified
Open: one or more allergen dishes lack substitution
Reached: pupil served a declared allergen since plan start

meal_urgency.instructions: How soon will the pupil next eat a school meal under this plan?
criteria: First school meal more than 20 school days away
First school meal 6 to 20 school days away
First school meal 2 to 5 school days away
First school meal is the next school day
Pupil already eating school meals under this plan

factors.name: evidence_status
factors.description: State of the medical evidence: current clinician letter, expired letter, section null because nothing was supplied, or a parent letter with no clinician signature.

factors.name: allergen_count
factors.description: Number of allergens declared for the pupil, which sets how many substitution chains the menu mapping must carry.

factors.name: anaphylaxis_risk
factors.description: Whether an adrenaline auto-injector is prescribed. It raises concern but does not on its own change exposure or next step.

factors.name: unsubstituted_dishes
factors.description: Count of menu-cycle dishes containing a declared allergen with no substitution mapped. Zero, one or several.

factors.name: allergen_list_mismatch
factors.description: The medical evidence names an allergen that is missing from the pupil's declared list, which the menu mapping was built from.

factors.name: recipe_change_after_mapping
factors.description: A dish's recipe version is dated after the plan's mapping date, so the mapping happened before the current recipe existed.

factors.name: supplier_spec_confirmed
factors.description: A supplier specification sheet, checked after the recipe change, confirms the changed dish is free of the declared allergens. Mitigates a recipe change.

factors.name: kitchen_control_state
factors.description: Kitchen-side control condition: all verified, allergen training lapsed for some staff, shared equipment for allergen-free prep, or the cleaning and segregation log not completed.

factors.name: control_exception_approved
factors.description: An approved, in-date exception covers the kitchen weakness, such as a signed deep-clean protocol for shared equipment or a booked training refresher with a supervising trained cook. Mitigates the weakness.

factors.name: served_allergen_incident
factors.description: Since the plan started, the incident history logs that the pupil was served a dish containing a declared allergen. This is decisive: exposure_proximity goes to Reached whatever else holds, even when the note says there was no reaction.

factors.name: days_to_first_meal
factors.description: School days from the review date to the pupil's first school meal under the plan. Zero or negative means the pupil is already eating under it.

factors.name: packed_lunch_interim
factors.description: The family has agreed packed lunches until a set date, which pushes back the first school meal even though the plan start date is earlier. Mitigates urgency.

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Tone of the free-text messages in the history, independent of the facts: reassuring, alarmed or neutral. Acts as a decoy.

sections.name: pupil
sections.description: Pupil reference, year group, school code, declared allergens, auto-injector flag, plan start date.

sections.name: medical_evidence
sections.description: Evidence document type, issuer role, issue and expiry dates, allergens listed; null if none supplied.

sections.name: menu_mapping
sections.description: Mapping date, cycle weeks and a list of allergen-bearing dishes, each with recipe version date, substitution and supplier spec check.

sections.name: kitchen_controls
sections.description: Prep area, segregated equipment flag, trained staff count and dates, cleaning log status, approved exceptions.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Review date, packed-lunch arrangement, incident list and one to three short free-text messages.

F403.rendering_notes: pupil.declared_allergens lists allergen_count items. pupil.auto_injector carries anaphylaxis_risk. pupil.plan_start is a date. evidence_status appears as medical_evidence.doc_type ('clinician_letter' or 'parent_letter') with issued and expires dates. When expires falls before history.review_date, the evidence is expired. A missing status renders the whole medical_evidence section as null. allergen_list_mismatch shows only as medical_evidence.allergens containing one item absent from pupil.declared_allergens, and therefore absent from the mapping. menu_mapping.dishes holds entries {dish, contains, recipe_version_date, substitute, spec_checked_on}. unsubstituted_dishes renders as that many entries with substitute: null. recipe_change_after_mapping renders as recipe_version_date later than menu_mapping.mapped_on. supplier_spec_confirmed renders as spec_checked_on later than recipe_version_date; otherwise spec_checked_on is null or earlier. A recipe change without a later spec check counts as an unsubstituted dish. kitchen_control_state renders as staff training dates past their 12-month refresh, or segregated_equipment: false, or cleaning_log_complete: false. control_exception_approved renders as kitchen_controls.exceptions containing a dated, signed entry that covers that weakness; a covered weakness counts as verified. served_allergen_incident renders as a history.incidents entry dated on or after plan_start whose dish contains a declared allergen. Its note may say 'no reaction observed' as a decoy, and the incident still sets exposure to Reached and next step to escalate. Earlier near-miss incidents before plan_start may appear as decoys. history.packed_lunch_until, when non-null, defers the first school meal to the next school day after that date. Otherwise the first meal is plan_start. Urgency is counted in school days from history.review_date. history.messages holds one to three one-sentence notes from the cook, parent or reviewer, written in note_tone. Their tone must not track the facts: alarmed notes can sit on a sound plan and reassuring ones on a flawed plan. For next_step, an evidence gap leads to request_evidence unless an incident forces escalation. Exactly one unsubstituted or unconfirmed dish leads to approve_restricted, and two or more lead to return_for_rework. A record must never contain fields such as risk level, approval status, gap stage, urgency or 'covered: true'. Every answer must be derived by comparing dates, lists and counts across sections.

F404.role: Ratio compliance auditor in a nursery group's central quality team, reviewing one room-day staffing record at a time
F404.setting: A group of day nurseries sends each room's daily records to a central quality team. These cover bookings, child sign-in counts per 15-minute slot, the planned staff rota, actual staff sign-in and sign-out times, floater cover entries and recent audit history. The auditor rebuilds the eligible staff count for each slot and compares it with the room's ratio rule. They decide whether the room met ratio, what caused any gap, how long and how serious the gap was, and what to do with the record.

below_ratio.instructions: The room ran below its required staff ratio during the session.

criteria.true: An uncovered slot had fewer eligible staff than required.
criteria.false: Every slot met ratio once logged cover is counted.

disposition.instructions: What should the auditor do with this room-day record?

criteria.file_no_action: Ratio met in every slot; nothing further is needed.
criteria.hold_confirm: Outcome depends on one missing confirmation, such as unsigned cover.
criteria.corrective_plan: Confirmed breach below notifiable threshold; room manager agrees an action plan.
criteria.escalate_notify: Breach is critical or exceeds sixty minutes; refer to safeguarding lead.

primary_cause.instructions: Which single cause best explains the record's ratio position?

criteria.none_found: Sections agree and every slot met the required ratio.
criteria.paperwork_only: Sections disagree, yet recomputed cover met ratio in every slot.
criteria.staff_shortfall: Ratio missed and eligible staff on duty fell below rota.
criteria.child_overrun: Ratio missed with staff at rota but children above bookings.

shortfall_duration.instructions: How long did the room run below its required ratio?
criteria: Never below ratio in any logged slot
Below ratio for fifteen minutes or less in total
Below ratio for sixteen to sixty minutes in total
Below ratio for more than sixty minutes in total

breach_severity.instructions: How many children were left beyond eligible staff cover at worst?
criteria: None: no child beyond cover in any slot
Minor: one child beyond cover at worst slot
Significant: two or three children beyond cover
Critical: four or more beyond cover, or none covered

factors.name: age_band
factors.description: Age band of the room, which sets the ratio rule: under_2 is 1:3, two_year is 1:4, three_plus is 1:8 (1:13 when a level 6 practitioner is on duty).

factors.name: children_peak
factors.description: Highest number of children signed in during any single slot.

factors.name: staff_signin_variance
factors.description: How actual staff sign-in and sign-out times differ from the rota: none, trivial (id format or a few minutes), late_arrival, early_departure, or an absent staff member with no sign-in.

factors.name: attendance_overrun
factors.description: Number of children signed in above bookings at the peak slot, for example from extra sessions not added to bookings.

factors.name: shortfall_minutes
factors.description: Underlying minutes during which eligible signed-in staff were below the requirement before any cover is counted. Zero where no gap arises.

factors.name: floater_cover_logged
factors.description: A floating practitioner is logged in the cover log as present in the room across the gap window. This mitigates the alarming sign-in gap and appears about equally often with and without one.

factors.name: cover_log_unsigned
factors.description: The floater cover entry has no countersignature from the room lead, so the mitigation needs one confirmation before it can be relied on.

factors.name: ineligible_counted
factors.description: The rota counts someone who cannot count toward ratio: a student under 17, a staff member whose suitability check is pending, or a level 2 practitioner filling a level 3 requirement shown in the staff register.

factors.name: qualified_teacher_mismatch
factors.description: For three_plus rooms, the rota claims a level 6 practitioner on duty (allowing 1:13) but staff sign-in shows them absent or out for part of the day. Values: none, partial_day, absent.

factors.name: zero_eligible_adult_slot
factors.description: Aggravating fact: in at least one slot with four or more children present, no adult eligible to count was signed in, for example only a student or an unchecked staff member. Whenever present this alone sets breach_severity to Critical.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: The gap total lands exactly on 15 or 60 minutes, or the cover log window only partly overlaps the gap, leaving judges split between neighbouring answers.

factors.name: prior_breaches_90d
factors.description: Count of breaches recorded for this room in the last 90 days. Shown as context and decoy; it does not change the ratio arithmetic.

sections.name: session
sections.description: Room id, date, age_band, ratio_rule string, registered_places, opening and closing times.

sections.name: children
sections.description: Bookings count and a list of 15-minute slots with children signed in.

sections.name: rota
sections.description: Planned staff list: staff_id, role, qual_level, counts_in_ratio flag, planned start and end.

sections.name: staff_signin
sections.description: Actual staff records: staff_id, time_in, time_out, check_status, qual_level from the register.

sections.name: cover_log
sections.description: Floater entries: staff_id, from, to, room_id, countersigned_by (null if unsigned).

sections.name: history
sections.description: prior_breaches_90d, last_audit_date and last_audit_outcome for the room.

F404.rendering_notes: The record never states a breach, minutes below ratio, children beyond cover, cause or required action. The auditor must work out the required staff for each slot from session.ratio_rule and children.slots[].signed_in, then compare it with eligible staff present according to staff_signin (not the rota). age_band appears as session.age_band and session.ratio_rule. For three_plus rooms the rule reads "1:8; 1:13 with L6 on duty". children_peak is the largest signed_in value in the slots. attendance_overrun shows as signed_in exceeding children.booked in the peak slots. staff_signin_variance shows through time_in/time_out against rota planned times: absent staff have no staff_signin entry, and trivial variance is a staff_id format difference (e.g. "S-041" against "S041") or a gap of 1 to 5 minutes. shortfall_minutes is implicit in the slots where eligible staff fall short, and the gap window is built from staff_signin times. floater_cover_logged adds a cover_log entry whose from/to spans the gap window and whose room_id matches the session. When absent, cover_log is an empty list or holds an entry for a different room as a decoy. cover_log_unsigned sets countersigned_by to null. ineligible_counted shows as rota counts_in_ratio true while staff_signin shows check_status "pending", an age under 17, or a qual_level lower than the rota claims. qualified_teacher_mismatch shows as the rota listing qual_level 6 while staff_signin is missing or has a midday time_out. zero_eligible_adult_slot shows as a slot with four or more children where only ineligible staff are signed in. boundary_case places gap totals at exactly 15 or 60 minutes, or makes cover from/to overlap only part of the gap. Decoys include registered_places (always at or above the peak and irrelevant to ratio), history.last_audit_outcome "satisfactory" alongside a current breach, prior_breaches_90d, and trivial id or time differences that do not change any count. Mismatches are never flagged by any field. Some records reconcile completely.

F405.role: Central timetabling officer reviewing room clash reports
F405.setting: A university timetabling office receives automatically detected room clash reports during term planning and live teaching weeks. For each report the officer reconciles the two bookings against the room record, any listed free rooms and the change history, then decides whether the clash is real, what to do with it and how soon it bites.

genuine_clash.instructions: Both bookings occupy the same physical room at overlapping times.

criteria.true: Room, teaching weeks and times overlap after reconciliation.
criteria.false: Reconciled weeks, times or rooms show no overlap.

alt_room_fits.instructions: A listed free room meets the displaced booking's capacity and features.

resolution.instructions: What should the officer do with this clash report?

criteria.dismiss: No overlap remains once weeks, times and room codes reconciled.
criteria.hold_confirm: Overlap exists but one booking's status or pending change unconfirmed.
criteria.relocate: Both bookings confirmed and a listed free room fits one.
criteria.reschedule: Both confirmed, no listed room fits; a teaching time must move.

urgency.instructions: How soon does the first clashing occurrence fall after the report?
criteria: Distant: first clashing occurrence more than 28 days away
Upcoming: first clashing occurrence 8 to 28 days away
Imminent: first clashing occurrence 1 to 7 days away
Live: first clashing occurrence today or already passed

parties_needed.instructions: How many separate people or teams must act to resolve this?
criteria: One person can resolve it alone
Two people or teams must act
Three or four people or teams must act
Five or more people or teams must act

factors.name: overlap_type
factors.description: True relationship between the two bookings once times and teaching weeks are compared; only full and partial_time are genuine clashes.

factors.name: room_code_alias
factors.description: Booking B cites the room by an alternative code (building-floor-number versus short name) that maps to the same room via the room section; a decoy mismatch that is not a real difference.

factors.name: wrong_room_variant
factors.description: Booking B actually references a neighbouring room whose code differs by one character and is not listed among the room's aliases, meaning no genuine clash.

factors.name: booking_b_status
factors.description: Approval state of the second booking; anything other than confirmed points towards holding.

factors.name: approval_out_of_order
factors.description: Booking B's approved_at timestamp falls after its first scheduled occurrence or its approver field is null while status reads confirmed, so confirmation is effectively incomplete.

factors.name: pending_change_request
factors.description: Mitigation: one booking already has an open change request in history moving it to another slot or room, not yet actioned; same alarming overlap appears with and without it.

factors.name: days_to_first_occurrence
factors.description: Days between report date and first clashing occurrence, derived from term_start, teaching week list and weekday rather than stated directly; values near 7 and 28 create boundary cases.

factors.name: alt_room_fit
factors.description: Best match among listed free rooms for the displaced booking, judged by capacity against headcount and required features.

factors.name: alternatives_missing
factors.description: Alternatives section is null because the free-room search was not run, so no fitting room can be shown.

factors.name: headcount_ratio
factors.description: Displaced booking's expected headcount divided by the best alternative room's capacity; just above 1.0 is a near-miss boundary.

factors.name: required_feature
factors.description: Facility the displaced booking requires, to be checked against each alternative's feature list.

factors.name: owning_departments
factors.description: Whether the two bookings belong to the same department, different departments, or one is an external hire; drives how many parties must act.

factors.name: prior_clash_count
factors.description: Number of earlier clash reports on the same room and slot in history; a decoy that looks alarming but does not change the decisions.

sections.name: clash_report
sections.description: Report id, detection date, term_start, room code flagged and slot flagged by the scan.

sections.name: booking_a
sections.description: First booking: module code, department, weekday, start and end times, weeks list, headcount, required features, status.

sections.name: booking_b
sections.description: Second booking with the same fields plus approved_at and approver, which may be null.

sections.name: room
sections.description: Room record: canonical code, aliases list, capacity, feature list, building.

sections.name: alternatives
sections.description: List of free rooms for the slot with code, capacity, features and weeks free; null if search not run.

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of prior events on this room and slot: clash reports, change requests with state and dates.

F405.rendering_notes: overlap_type is shown only through booking_a and booking_b weekday, start/end times (HH:MM) and weeks lists (integers); week_pattern_disjoint gives non-intersecting week lists, adjacent_no_overlap gives one ending exactly when the other starts. room_code_alias puts an alias from room.aliases in booking_b.room; wrong_room_variant puts a near-identical code not in aliases. booking_b_status appears as booking_b.status; approval_out_of_order sets approved_at after the first occurrence date or approver null. pending_change_request adds a history entry type change_request, state open, target slot or room differing. days_to_first_occurrence must be computed from clash_report.detected_on, term_start, the earliest shared week and weekday; never state it. alt_room_fit and headcount_ratio show via alternatives capacities, feature lists and weeks_free versus the clashing weeks; alternatives_missing sets the section to null. required_feature appears in the displaced booking's required_features list. owning_departments appears via booking department fields or an external_hire flag. prior_clash_count adds past clash_report entries in history as decoys. Booking priority flags and the scan's flagged slot are decoys; the scan flags pairs even when weeks do not intersect. No field may state genuineness, fit, resolution, urgency or parties needed; no free-text fields.

F406.role: Duty front-of-house safety officer at a multi-gallery museum, reviewing each gallery session's capacity log the morning after
F406.setting: Every timed gallery session produces a capacity log combining door-counter intervals, ticket scans, a steward's manual tally, any approved capacity variations, counter maintenance records and short staff notes. The officer checks one log at a time. For each log they confirm whether any uplift genuinely applied, judge whether apparent overages are counting faults, rate how far and how long occupancy ran above the limit in force, and decide what happens to the log next.

variation_applies.instructions: The approved capacity variation applies to this session and gallery.

fault_explains_overage.instructions: The counter overage is explained by a documented counting fault.

criteria.true: Fault ticket covers this gate and date before session.
criteria.false: No ticket, wrong gate or date, or informal note only.

next_step.instructions: What should be done with this capacity log now?

criteria.file_as_complete: Log reconciles and needs no follow-up; file it as is.
criteria.request_counter_data: Ask the site team for the missing interval counter export.
criteria.amend_and_file: Correct a minor cross-section discrepancy, annotate it, then file.
criteria.restrict_admissions: Set a reduced admission cap for the gallery's next session.
criteria.escalate_safety_lead: Refer to the venue safety lead for formal overcapacity review.

peak_excess.instructions: By how much did reconciled peak occupancy exceed the limit in force?
criteria: Peak at or below 90% of limit
Peak above 90% and up to 100% of limit
Peak above limit by no more than 10%
Peak above limit by more than 10%

intervals_over.instructions: For how many 15-minute intervals was occupancy above the limit?
criteria: None: no interval above the limit in force
Single: exactly one interval above the limit
Few: two or three intervals above the limit
Several: four to eight intervals above the limit
Extended: more than eight intervals above the limit

factors.name: true_peak_ratio
factors.description: Reconciled peak occupancy as a fraction of the limit in force (certified limit, or the uplifted limit when a valid variation applies).

factors.name: intervals_over_limit
factors.description: Number of 15-minute intervals in which reconciled occupancy exceeded the limit in force; forced to 0 when true_peak_ratio is at or below 1.0.

factors.name: section_mismatch
factors.description: Which cross-section discrepancy, if any, is planted in the log.

factors.name: variation_present
factors.description: Whether a capacity variation (temporary uplift for an event or extra stewarding) is attached to the log.

factors.name: variation_scope
factors.description: Whether the attached variation actually covers this session: matching gallery and date, wrong gallery, expired or future date, or pending approval.

factors.name: counter_fault_logged
factors.description: Whether any maintenance record about door-counter accuracy exists near the session.

factors.name: fault_ticket_scope
factors.description: How well the fault record matches: same gate and date, a different gate, raised after the session, or only an informal staff remark.

factors.name: interval_export_missing
factors.description: Whether the per-interval counter export is absent, so only a session summary total is present.

factors.name: egress_check
factors.description: State of the steward's egress-route check for the session.

factors.name: prior_overages_30d
factors.description: Count of earlier logged overages for the same gallery in the past 30 days.

factors.name: staff_note_tone
factors.description: Tone of the free-text steward note, independent of the actual data: reassuring without support, factual, alarmed without support, or absent.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether the reconciled peak sits within 2% of a peak_excess threshold, or the counter and tally disagree across a level boundary.

sections.name: session
sections.description: Session id, gallery_code, session_date, open and close times, certified_limit from fire certificate.

sections.name: counts
sections.description: Interval list of door-counter occupancy, ticket_scans total, steward manual_tally_peak, summary_peak.

sections.name: variations
sections.description: Attached capacity variations: ref, gallery_code, valid_from, valid_to, uplift_to, status; may be empty list.

sections.name: equipment
sections.description: Counter gate ids, last_calibrated date, maintenance tickets with gate, raised_at, summary.

sections.name: staff_log
sections.description: Stewards on duty, egress_check state and time, one or two short free-text notes.

sections.name: history
sections.description: overages_30d count and dates of last logged overages for this gallery.

F406.rendering_notes: true_peak_ratio and intervals_over_limit appear only as counts.intervals[] entries (start, in, out, occupancy) against session.certified_limit or a variation's uplift_to; never write a ratio, an over_limit flag or an overage duration. section_mismatch is planted silently: ticket_scans differing from the counter-implied entries by under 5% (minor) or over 15% (major); manual_tally_peak differing from the interval peak; a variation or ticket gallery_code differing by one character from session.gallery_code; a variation valid window ending the day before session_date. variation_present adds an entry to variations; variation_scope sets its gallery_code, dates or status ('pending') so the reader must check that it applies, and otherwise the variations list is empty. counter_fault_logged adds a ticket in equipment.maintenance; fault_ticket_scope sets the gate id, a raised_at after session close, or replaces the ticket with a staff note such as 'counter at east door seemed jumpy'. interval_export_missing replaces counts.intervals with null and leaves only summary_peak. egress_check appears as staff_log.egress_check with values done, partial (with routes_checked 2 of 3) or null. prior_overages_30d appears in history.overages_30d with matching dates. staff_note_tone controls the wording of staff_log.notes; reassuring or alarmed notes are decoys and must not match the data unless the tone is factual. boundary_case nudges the interval peak to within 2% of 90%, 100% or 110% of the limit, or puts tally and counter on opposite sides of a threshold. No field may state a disposition, a severity, whether a variation applies or whether a fault explains the counts.

F407.role: Highways defect triage officer at a district council, reviewing one pothole report at a time
F407.setting: A council highways team receives pothole reports from the public, councillors, its own inspectors and utility contractors. For each report the triage officer checks the logged location against the asset register, any site inspection, past works at the same spot, planned schemes and temporary measures, and any works order already raised. The officer then decides whether the defect meets intervention criteria, whether it is a failed earlier repair, what to do with the report now, and how quickly policy requires a response.

meets_threshold.instructions: Inspected defect depth meets the intervention depth for this road.

criteria.true: Recorded inspection depth at or above the listed threshold
criteria.false: Depth below threshold, or no valid inspection measurement

repeat_failure.instructions: This defect is a recurrence of an earlier completed repair here.

criteria.true: Completed prior repair confirmed within ten metres of defect
criteria.false: No prior repair matched, or match only approximate

next_step.instructions: What should the triage officer do with this report now?

criteria.close_no_action: Close the report: below criteria, duplicate, or already repaired.
criteria.request_inspection: Obtain a valid site measurement before deciding on any repair.
criteria.order_repair: Raise or confirm a works order, timed around planned schemes.
criteria.escalate_engineer: Refer to a highways engineer for claims, injury or recurring failure.

staff_effort.instructions: How much staff time would fully resolving this record require?
criteria: Under one hour of staff time needed
One to eight hours of staff time
One to five working days of staff time
More than five working days of staff time

response_timescale.instructions: Within what timescale does policy require the defect to be addressed?
criteria: No repair required under current intervention policy
Routine repair within 28 days of inspection
Priority repair within five working days
Make safe within 24 hours of report

factors.name: road_category
factors.description: Hierarchy class of the road from the asset register; sets the intervention depth and the response bands

factors.name: depth_vs_threshold
factors.description: How the inspected depth compares with the category intervention depth, including values within 2 mm of the boundary

factors.name: inspection_state
factors.description: Whether a valid site inspection exists: done after the report, only scheduled, never done, or dated before the report was received, so it measured an earlier condition

factors.name: prior_repair_match
factors.description: Past completed repair near the defect: none, the same spot within guarantee, the same spot after guarantee expired, or nearby with only an approximate location

factors.name: temporary_make_safe
factors.description: A temporary fill or barrier is already in place and in date; it lowers urgency without removing the need for a permanent repair

factors.name: planned_scheme_soon
factors.description: Resurfacing or patching that covers the defect location is programmed to start within 28 days

factors.name: duplicate_count
factors.description: Number of other open reports logged against the same location; alarming on its face but often just duplicates

factors.name: reporter_source
factors.description: Origin of the report; own-inspector reports carry measurements, public reports often lack them

factors.name: injury_or_claim
factors.description: An injury, vehicle damage or a compensation claim is linked to the location

factors.name: order_status
factors.description: State of any existing works order: none, raised, partially complete, or completed but awaiting sign-off

factors.name: defect_width_mm
factors.description: Surface width of the defect; a decoy that looks alarming but does not drive policy thresholds

factors.name: photo_attached
factors.description: Whether the report carries a photo reference; absent photos weaken public-only reports

sections.name: report
sections.description: Report id, received timestamp, source channel, photo reference, linked duplicate ids, claim flag

sections.name: location
sections.description: USRN, road category, intervention_depth_mm from the asset register, grid reference, speed limit

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Inspector id, inspected_at date, depth_mm, width_mm, position offset; null when no inspection exists

sections.name: works_history
sections.description: List of past completed jobs at the street: job id, completed date, offset, guarantee_end

sections.name: programme
sections.description: Planned schemes with start dates and extents, plus temporary measures with installed and expiry dates

sections.name: current_order
sections.description: Existing works order id, raised date, status, completed_items and total_items; null if none

F407.rendering_notes: road_category appears as location.road_class, and the threshold as location.intervention_depth_mm; the record never says whether the threshold is met, so the reader must compare it with inspection.depth_mm. depth_vs_threshold sets inspection.depth_mm relative to that threshold, with boundary cases differing by 0 to 2 mm. inspection_state: completed_valid gives a full inspection object dated after report.received_at; scheduled gives inspection with depth_mm null and a future inspected_at labelled scheduled_for; not_done gives inspection: null; dated_before_report gives a full object whose inspected_at precedes received_at. prior_repair_match puts a works_history entry whose offset_m is within 10 m (same spot) or given only as a street-level null offset (nearby_unconfirmed), and guarantee_end falls after or before the report date. temporary_make_safe adds a programme.temp_measures entry covering the offset with an expiry date in the future (or omits it); planned_scheme_soon adds a programme.schemes entry whose extent covers the offset and whose start date falls within 28 days, while decoy schemes on other extents or starting later appear in both cases. duplicate_count is the length of report.linked_reports, which is a decoy for urgency. reporter_source is report.channel; own_inspector reports usually come with inspection filled. injury_or_claim is report.claim_ref (string id or null). order_status fills current_order with status and completed_items/total_items (partial when completed_items < total_items), and there is no priority field. defect_width_mm is inspection.width_mm and is a decoy. photo_attached is report.photo_ref or null. No field ever states urgency, priority, repeat-failure status, recommended action or whether criteria are met; all must be inferred by comparing fields across sections.

F408.role: Waste services case officer at a district council, reviewing each resident report of a missed bin collection
F408.setting: A district council's waste team receives online and phone reports that a household bin was not emptied. For each report the case officer compares the resident's report with the property record, the round schedule, the crew's round log and in-cab telematics, and the address's case history. The officer then decides whether the miss is genuine, whether a return visit is due and how soon, and whether the case needs a supervisor.

crew_missed.instructions: Round records show the crew missed a correctly presented bin.

criteria.true: Crew passed or skipped without a supported exception
criteria.false: Supported exception, disruption, catch-up, or no evidence of miss

report_matches.instructions: Reported stream and date match the property's scheduled collection.

criteria.true: Stream, week and day agree with schedule
criteria.false: Wrong stream, off-week, or reported before round finished

next_step.instructions: What should the case officer do with this report now?

criteria.close_no_action: Not a valid miss or already emptied; close the case.
criteria.request_evidence: Ask resident or crew for one specific missing item first.
criteria.return_conditional: Book a return once the resident fixes presentation or contamination.
criteria.schedule_return: Book an unconditional return visit for the missed bin.
criteria.escalate_supervisor: Refer to round supervisor for policy breach or repeated failure.

return_urgency.instructions: How soon must a return collection reach this property?
criteria: None: bin already emptied or report not upheld
Next round: waste waits for next scheduled collection day
Standard: return visit within two working days
Same day: return visit before end of today

repeat_failures.instructions: How many upheld misses does this address have in twelve weeks?
criteria: No upheld misses in the prior twelve weeks
Exactly one upheld miss in prior twelve weeks
Exactly two upheld misses in prior twelve weeks
Three or more upheld misses in twelve weeks

factors.name: stream_mismatch
factors.description: Whether the reported bin stream or date disagrees with the schedule: none, alternate-week confusion, a stream not due that week, or a claimed date one day off but within the reporting window

factors.name: report_timing
factors.description: When the report was logged relative to the round: after the round was marked complete, before the round finished, or after the 48-hour reporting window closed

factors.name: crew_exception
factors.description: Exception code the crew logged against this address's stop

factors.name: exception_supported
factors.description: Whether the crew exception is backed by a timestamped photo reference and a GPS stop at the address; when false, the code stands alone

factors.name: telematics_pass
factors.description: What in-cab telematics show at the address: a stop, a pass without stopping, no GPS data, or the street not visited

factors.name: round_disruption
factors.description: A declared disruption on the round with a catch-up date: none, vehicle breakdown, road closure or weather suspension

factors.name: already_collected
factors.description: Whether a sweep or catch-up vehicle has since emptied the bin, per a later round-log entry

factors.name: photo_attached
factors.description: Whether the resident attached a photo of the presented bin; its absence matters when a crew exception is unsupported

factors.name: address_id_mismatch
factors.description: Disagreement between report and property identifiers: none, flat number giving a different UPRN, or a postcode typo with the same UPRN

factors.name: prior_upheld_misses
factors.description: Upheld misses for this UPRN within the twelve weeks before the report

factors.name: history_decoys
factors.description: History entries that must not be counted: older than twelve weeks, rejected, pending, or logged against a neighbouring UPRN

factors.name: assisted_miss_breach
factors.description: Property is on the assisted collection register, where crews must fetch the bin themselves, yet the crew logged not_presented or passed without stopping

sections.name: report
sections.description: Resident's report: id, UPRN, address, postcode, logged time, stream, claimed date, photo flag

sections.name: property
sections.description: Property record: UPRN, flat number, postcode, assisted collection flag and date, bins held

sections.name: schedule
sections.description: Round schedule: round id, collection day, week pattern, streams due, scheduled date

sections.name: round_log
sections.description: Crew log: round status and completion time, disruption, catch-up date, stops with GPS, exception code, photo ref, sweep collection time

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of earlier cases: case id, UPRN, date logged, stream, outcome

F408.rendering_notes: stream_mismatch: compare report.stream_reported and report.claimed_date with schedule.streams_due and schedule.scheduled_date (week_pattern A/B drives alternate-week confusion). Never write a match flag. report_timing: compare report.logged_at with round_log.round_completed_at and with schedule.scheduled_date plus 48 hours. crew_exception: round_log.stops[] entry for the report's UPRN, field exception_code (null when none). exception_supported: the same stop has photo_ref non-null and gps_stop true; when false, photo_ref is null and gps_stop false or null. telematics_pass: stop gps_stop true/false, gps_stop null for no data, or no stop entry for the UPRN at all when the street was not visited. round_disruption: round_log.disruption_code plus catch_up_date (null when none). A disruption is a decoy if catch_up_date has already passed without a sweep entry. already_collected: round_log.sweep_collected_at is a timestamp later than logged_at; otherwise null. photo_attached: report.photo_attached boolean. address_id_mismatch: report.flat_no versus property.flat_no and report.uprn versus property.uprn, or report.postcode differing by one character from property.postcode. prior_upheld_misses: history[] entries for the same UPRN, outcome 'upheld', logged_on within 84 days before report.logged_at. history_decoys: add entries with outcome 'rejected' or 'pending', entries dated more than 84 days earlier, or entries for a neighbouring UPRN. Pending entries make the repeat count contestable. assisted_miss_breach: property.assisted_collection true with assisted_since date, and the stop for this UPRN shows exception_code 'not_presented' or gps_stop false. As a decoy, assisted_collection is also true on some records where the stop was normal. When assisted_miss_breach is present, return_urgency is Same day regardless of other fields. No record carries fields such as upheld, urgency, priority, fault or recommended_action. No free-text fields: all values are codes, numbers, booleans, ISO dates or null.

F409.role: Residents' parking permit officer at a district council parking services team, reviewing one permit application at a time
F409.setting: A council parking services back office processes residents' parking permit applications for controlled zones. Each application record combines what the applicant submitted, the residence evidence they uploaded, the vehicle registration lookup, the permit being requested and the account's permit and penalty history. The officer decides whether the applicant lives in the zone, what to do with the application, which issue drives the outcome, how strong any sign of permit misuse is, and how many required documents are still outstanding.

residency_shown.instructions: Applicant is shown to reside at the address within the zone.

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this permit application at this stage?

criteria.approve: All eligibility checks met; issue the full annual permit.
criteria.approve_temporary: Residency proven, one non-residency document outstanding; issue time-limited permit.
criteria.hold: Residency or keeper proof missing or conflicting; issue nothing yet.
criteria.refuse: Fails a stated eligibility rule; reject with written reasons.

main_issue.instructions: Which single issue most determines this application's outcome?

criteria.no_issue: No check fails; outcome follows standard eligibility rules.
criteria.vehicle_keeper: Registered keeper or plate differs from applicant or request.
criteria.residence_proof: Address evidence absent, stale, mismatched or dated out of order.
criteria.household_cap: Address already holds the zone's maximum permit allowance.
criteria.misuse_record: Account history shows cloned, altered or sold permits.

misuse_strength.instructions: How strong is the evidence of permit misuse on this account?
criteria: Clear: no unmitigated misuse indicator anywhere in record
Low: exactly one unmitigated misuse indicator present
Elevated: two or more unmitigated misuse indicators present
Confirmed: prior permit recorded as cloned, altered or sold

document_gaps.instructions: How many required documents are missing or unverified?
criteria: All required documents received and verified
One required document missing or unverified
Two required documents missing or unverified
Three or more required documents missing or unverified

factors.name: application_type
factors.description: Kind of application, which changes which documents are required (new needs residence and keeper proof; renewal needs only current proof if unchanged; change of vehicle needs keeper proof; change of address needs residence proof).

factors.name: address_match_level
factors.description: How the address on the residence evidence compares with the address on the application and the zone gazetteer entry.

factors.name: proof_age_days
factors.description: Age in days of the residence document at submission; the scheme accepts documents up to 90 days old. Values near 85 to 95 create boundary cases.

factors.name: docs_missing
factors.description: Number of required documents (residence proof, V5C or keeper letter, ID) not uploaded or uploaded but not yet verified.

factors.name: keeper_mismatch
factors.description: How the vehicle registration lookup compares with the applicant and the plate typed on the request.

factors.name: keeper_letter_on_file
factors.description: A lease agreement or employer company-car letter naming the applicant as main user is on file, which mitigates a different registered keeper.

factors.name: household_permits_held
factors.description: Number of live residents' permits already held at the same address; the zone cap is 2 per household.

factors.name: cap_exception_approved
factors.description: An approved exception (carer for a blue badge holder, or medical exception) is recorded, allowing a permit beyond the household cap.

factors.name: zone_pcn_count
factors.description: Penalty charge notices in the zone against the vehicle or account in the last 12 months; three or more uncancelled counts as a misuse indicator.

factors.name: pcns_cancelled
factors.description: Most of the zone PCNs were cancelled on appeal (signage fault or suspension error), which mitigates a high PCN count.

factors.name: date_order_anomaly
factors.description: Tenancy or council tax start date falls after the application submission date, or the residence document is dated after the request date, showing an out-of-order sequence.

factors.name: message_claim
factors.description: What the applicant's free-text message claims relative to the structured records: nothing relevant, a consistent explanation of a mismatch, or a claim the records contradict.

factors.name: prior_permit_cloned
factors.description: Aggravating fact: account history records a previous permit for this address or vehicle seized as cloned, altered or sold within the last 24 months. When true, misuse_strength is Confirmed and refusal follows.

sections.name: applicant
sections.description: Applicant identity, application date, application type and a free-text message.

sections.name: residence_evidence
sections.description: List of uploaded documents with type, issue date, address line, verification state, plus an evidence note.

sections.name: vehicle
sections.description: Registration lookup result: plate, registered keeper name, keeper address, supporting letters.

sections.name: request
sections.description: Permit requested: zone code, address, plate entered, duration, fee band.

sections.name: account_history
sections.description: Live household permits, past permits with status, zone PCNs, exceptions and an officer note.

F409.rendering_notes: applicant: {applicant_id, full_name, submitted_on (ISO), app_type (application_type), message (free text)}. message renders message_claim: nothing_relevant gives an unrelated sentence (e.g. asking about visitor vouchers); consistent_explanation explains a mismatch the records support (e.g. 'Car is a company lease, letter attached' when keeper_letter_on_file is true); contradicting_claim asserts something the records refute (e.g. 'I have lived here since 2019' when tenancy_start is last month). residence_evidence: docs list of {doc_type (council_tax_bill, tenancy_agreement, utility_bill, id_card), issued_on, address_line, verified (true/false/null)}, plus tenancy_start or ct_liability_from date and note (one sentence from the scanning team). address_match_level shows only by comparing docs[].address_line with request.address: format_only differs in punctuation or 'Flat 3' vs '3/'; different_flat changes the flat number; different_street changes the street. proof_age_days shows only as the gap between docs[].issued_on and applicant.submitted_on; never print the age. docs_missing shows as required documents absent from the list or present with verified null/false; the set of required documents depends on app_type, and a residence document older than 90 days counts as unverified. date_order_anomaly shows as tenancy_start/ct_liability_from or issued_on later than submitted_on. vehicle: {plate, keeper_name, keeper_postcode, supporting_letters: [] or [{type: lease_agreement|employer_letter, names_applicant: true}]}; keeper_mismatch shows by comparing vehicle.plate with request.plate_entered (plate_typo is one transposed or wrong character) and keeper_name with applicant.full_name; keeper_letter_on_file renders as a supporting_letters entry. request: {zone_code, address, plate_entered, duration_months, fee_band}; fee_band and emission-based pricing are decoys. account_history: live_permits list at address (count = household_permits_held; cap of 2 shown in zone_rules.max_per_household), past_permits [{permit_no, status: expired|surrendered|seized, seize_reason or null}] where prior_permit_cloned renders as status seized with seize_reason such as 'cloned copy found on different vehicle'; decoy surrendered permits appear on clean records. pcns list [{issued_on, contravention_code, status: paid|cancelled|open}] of length zone_pcn_count; pcns_cancelled sets most to cancelled with a reason. exceptions list (cap_exception_approved renders as an approved carer or medical exception with approved_on date) or empty. officer_note: short free-text, often a decoy (e.g. 'called applicant re payment, no answer'). Misuse indicators for misuse_strength: different_keeper without a supporting letter; three or more uncancelled zone PCNs; different_street address; date_order_anomaly; contradicting_claim. Mitigated indicators do not count. Main issue precedence when several apply: misuse_record, household_cap (only if cap reached and no exception), residence_proof, vehicle_keeper. Residency is shown only when a verified residence document dated within 90 days matches the address (exact or format_only) with no date-order anomaly. Contested cases arise when proof age sits at 88 to 92 days, when the address differs only by flat number with a consistent explanation, or when household permits equal the cap on a renewal. Never include fields such as eligible, risk, misuse_level, recommended_action or missing_count; verified flags per document are allowed because a real system shows them.

F410.role: Council market licensing officer reviewing street trader licence renewal applications
F410.setting: A district council's markets team processes renewals of annual street market trader licences. Each record pulls together the renewal application, the current licence and pitch allocation, compliance documents, the trader's fee account and twelve months of trading history. The officer reviews one renewal at a time and decides how to dispose of it, what inspection it needs, whether insurance is properly evidenced and how many cross-section discrepancies remain unresolved.

pli_term_covered.instructions: Public liability cover is evidenced for the whole renewed licence term.

criteria.true: Cover at the required sum spans the full term
criteria.false: Gap, indemnity shortfall, or renewal only assumed

renewal_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this renewal application now?

criteria.grant: Renew as applied; nothing unresolved across any section
criteria.grant_conditional: Renew with conditions; only minor or mitigated issues remain
criteria.defer: Hold until one outstanding document or confirmation arrives
criteria.refuse: Decline; unmitigated lapse or two or more serious breaches

inspection_level.instructions: What pre-renewal pitch inspection does this record warrant?

criteria.none_needed: Pitch and stock unchanged, hygiene evidence current where required
criteria.desk_check: Only documents to verify; any changes already formally approved
criteria.scheduled_visit: Unapproved pitch or stock change, no food safety gap
criteria.urgent_visit: Food sold without valid registration or open upheld safety complaint

reversal_time.instructions: How long would it take to fully undo this outcome?
criteria: Could be fully undone within one day
Needs one to seven days to undo
Needs eight days to three months to undo
Cannot be undone within three months

discrepancy_count.instructions: How many unresolved cross-section discrepancies does this renewal carry?
criteria: No unresolved discrepancies between any sections
Exactly one unresolved discrepancy found
Two or three unresolved discrepancies found
Four or more unresolved discrepancies found

factors.name: pli_cover_gap
factors.description: How the public liability policy dates and indemnity compare with the renewed term and the required sum

factors.name: broker_confirmation_held
factors.description: A broker renewal confirmation with a new end date covering the term is on file; mitigates a date gap but not an indemnity shortfall

factors.name: commodity_change
factors.description: How the commodities on the application differ from those on the current licence

factors.name: food_registration_state
factors.description: State of food business registration and hygiene rating where food is or will be sold

factors.name: stall_size_delta_m
factors.description: Difference in metres between requested stall width and allocated pitch width; council tolerance is 0.25 m

factors.name: variation_approved
factors.description: An approved variation on the current licence covers the size or commodity change

factors.name: fee_arrears_gbp
factors.description: Pitch fees due minus payments in the ledger; never shown as a single arrears figure

factors.name: payment_plan_active
factors.description: An agreed instalment plan with no missed instalments covers the arrears

factors.name: attendance_ratio
factors.description: Markets attended divided by markets allocated over 12 months; licence condition sets a minimum percentage

factors.name: absences_notified
factors.description: Missed markets were notified in advance with accepted reasons such as illness or weather cancellation

factors.name: complaint_profile
factors.description: Mix of complaints in the last 12 months by upheld status, category and whether still open

factors.name: holder_ref_mismatch
factors.description: How the holder reference and name on the application compare with the current licence

factors.name: docs_outstanding
factors.description: Number of required documents listed as pending on the application

sections.name: application
sections.description: Renewal request: refs, term dates, requested pitch size, commodities, pending documents

sections.name: licence_current
sections.description: Existing licence: holder, expiry, allocated pitch, commodities, conditions, approved variations

sections.name: compliance_docs
sections.description: Insurance policy, required indemnity, broker confirmation, food registration and hygiene rating

sections.name: account
sections.description: Fees due per period, payment ledger entries and any instalment plan

sections.name: history
sections.description: Twelve months of allocations, attendance, absence notices, complaints and enforcement

F410.rendering_notes: application: {app_ref, licence_no, holder_ref, holder_name, submitted, term_start, term_end, pitch_req:{market, width_m, depth_m}, commodities:[...], docs_pending:[...]} where docs_pending length = docs_outstanding. licence_current: {licence_no, holder_ref, holder_name, expires, pitch:{market, pitch_no, width_m, depth_m}, commodities:[...], conditions:{min_attendance_pct, max_width_m}, variations:[{type, detail, approved, approved_on}]}. compliance_docs: {pli:{insurer_ref, start, end, indemnity_gbp}, pli_required_gbp, broker_conf:{received, new_end} or null, food_reg:{registered, fhrs_rating, inspected_on} or null}. account: {fees_due:[{period, amount_gbp}], ledger:[{date, amount_gbp, method}], payment_plan:{active, instalments_left, missed} or null}. history: {allocated_12m, attended_12m, absence_notices:[{date, reason, accepted}], complaints:[{date, category, upheld, status}], enforcement_notices}. pli_cover_gap shows only through pli.end versus application.term_end and indemnity_gbp versus pli_required_gbp; broker_conf with new_end on or after term_end appears in about half of gap cases. commodity_change appears as differing lists; synonym_only uses wording like 'coffee' against 'hot drinks' and is a decoy, not a discrepancy. stall_size_delta_m is pitch_req.width_m minus pitch.width_m; values near 0.25 sit on the tolerance boundary. variation_approved appears as a matching entry in variations; non-matching or unapproved variations are decoys. Arrears are derived by summing fees_due minus ledger; the plan mitigates arrears only if active with missed = 0. attendance_ratio is attended_12m / allocated_12m against min_attendance_pct; accepted absence notices offset shortfall. holder_ref_mismatch: transcription_error swaps two digits but name matches; different_holder changes both. Decoys: insurer_ref changing between years, pitch_no differing on a different market day, not-upheld complaints, food_reg present for non-food stalls, ledger refunds. A discrepancy counts as unresolved unless a field elsewhere explains it (approved variation, broker confirmation, active plan, accepted absences). Inspection options apply by highest matching condition. No record contains a risk, decision, status-of-renewal, arrears total or discrepancy count field; all answers must be inferred.

F411.role: Vehicle licensing compliance officer at a district council taxi and private hire licensing unit, reviewing one vehicle's renewal inspection file at a time
F411.setting: Each record is the inspection file for a licensed taxi or private hire vehicle seeking plate renewal. It holds the licence details, the vehicle's identity and odometer, the inspection carried out at an approved testing station, the defects found and their rectification, the required supporting documents, and a short history of earlier inspections. The officer decides whether the renewal proceeds, what the inspection outcome was, how complete the paperwork is, how much safety exposure remains, and whether the odometer reading can be trusted.

odometer_consistent.instructions: The current odometer reading is consistent with the vehicle's recorded history.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this licence renewal application now?

criteria.renew: Grant as is; vehicle and paperwork fully meet standards.
criteria.request_evidence: One specific missing document or valid retest needed first.
criteria.conditional_renewal: Renew with dated condition to clear minor outstanding defects.
criteria.refuse_renewal: Major defect or several documents outstanding; odometer history sound.
criteria.refer_committee: Unexplained odometer drop present; licensing committee must decide.

inspection_outcome.instructions: Which category best describes the worst defect found at inspection?

criteria.clean_pass: No defects or advisories of any kind recorded at inspection.
criteria.advisory_only: Only advisory notes recorded; no item reached fail severity.
criteria.minor_fail: Worst failing item graded minor; nothing major or dangerous.
criteria.major_fail: At least one item graded major or dangerous at inspection.

document_gaps.instructions: How many required documents are missing or expired at review date?
criteria: Complete: no required document missing or expired
Single gap: exactly one document missing or expired
Two gaps: exactly two documents missing or expired
Multiple gaps: three or more missing or expired

outstanding_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst defect still outstanding today?
criteria: No defect outstanding; all rectified and validly retested
Worst outstanding item is an advisory only
Worst outstanding is minor, still within its deadline
Worst outstanding is minor, past its rectification deadline
At least one major or dangerous defect outstanding

factors.name: worst_defect_found
factors.description: Highest severity grade among items recorded at the inspection, before any rectification.

factors.name: rectification_state
factors.description: State of repair for failing items: not started, repaired but not retested, retest passed, or retest failed.

factors.name: deadline_passed
factors.description: Whether the review date is after the rectification deadline set for outstanding minor defects.

factors.name: documents_missing_count
factors.description: Number of required documents (insurance, MOT-equivalent certificate, V5-style registration, meter calibration, wheelchair equipment certificate where applicable) absent or past expiry.

factors.name: cover_note_mitigation
factors.description: An expired insurance or certificate entry carries a valid interim cover note or renewal receipt, so it counts as in date.
