factors.name: expiry_on_boundary
factors.description: One document's expiry date falls exactly on the review date, leaving in-date status arguable.

factors.name: odometer_drop
factors.description: Whether the current reading is below the highest earlier reading, and by how much: none, small (under 100 km, plausible keying slip) or large.

factors.name: cluster_replacement_documented
factors.description: A dated instrument cluster replacement with old and new readings is logged in history, explaining a drop.

factors.name: brake_test_missing
factors.description: The brake efficiency result in the inspection section is null, so the inspection is incomplete.

factors.name: retest_before_repair
factors.description: Recorded retest date precedes the logged repair date, so the retest cannot validate the repair.

factors.name: prior_failures_12m
factors.description: Count of failed inspections in the preceding twelve months; context and decoy only.

factors.name: vehicle_age_years
factors.description: Age of the vehicle from first registration; within policy limits, used as a decoy.

sections.name: licence
sections.description: Plate number, licence type (hackney or private hire), current expiry date and review date.

sections.name: vehicle
sections.description: Registration, make, model, first registration date, seats, current odometer_km.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Station id, inspection date, overall result code, brake_efficiency_pct, emissions and lighting checks.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of items with code, grade, rectify_by date, repaired_on, retest_on and retest_result.

sections.name: documents
sections.description: List of required documents with type, reference, expires_on, cover_note_ref and cover_until.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Earlier inspections with date, result and odometer_km, plus logged component replacements.

F411.rendering_notes: worst_defect_found appears only as grade values (advisory, minor, major, dangerous) on items in defects; an empty list means none. inspection.result_code is a terse station code (P, PA, F) that never distinguishes minor from major and is not the answer. rectification_state shows through repaired_on and retest_on/retest_result on failing items: both null = not started; repaired_on set and retest_on null = awaiting retest; retest_result 'pass' or 'fail'. retest_before_repair renders retest_on earlier than repaired_on with retest_result 'pass'; treat that item as unretested. deadline_passed is shown only by comparing defects.rectify_by with licence.review_date. documents_missing_count renders as required types absent from the list or expires_on before review_date; cover_note_mitigation adds cover_note_ref and cover_until after review_date to an expired entry, which then counts as in date. expiry_on_boundary sets expires_on equal to review_date with no cover note. odometer_drop compares vehicle.odometer_km with the highest history odometer_km; cluster_replacement_documented adds a history.replacements entry of type instrument_cluster dated between the readings with old_km and new_km that account for the drop; a drop without it makes the odometer claim false, and a small drop leaves it contested. brake_test_missing sets inspection.brake_efficiency_pct to null, which calls for request_evidence unless a major defect already justifies refusal. Precedence for next_step: unexplained odometer drop goes to refer_committee; else outstanding major/dangerous defect or two or more document gaps to refuse_renewal; else one document gap, null brake test or awaiting/invalid retest to request_evidence; else minor defects within deadline to conditional_renewal; else renew. prior_failures_12m (history results) and vehicle_age_years (first registration date) are decoys that never decide any answer alone. No field states a decision, risk level, completeness count or odometer verdict.

F412.role: Food safety follow-up officer in a district council environmental health team
F412.setting: After a food hygiene inspection finds contraventions, the operator is given deadlines to put them right. A follow-up officer reviews each case file one at a time. The file holds the premises details, the original inspection's contravention list, the revisit findings, correspondence with the operator (extension requests, replies and submitted evidence) and the compliance history including complaints and samples. The officer decides whether the case can close, what happens next, how overdue and how serious the remaining failings are, and which hazard area the worst open item falls in.

all_remedied.instructions: Every contravention from the inspection is verified as remedied at revisit.

criteria.true: Each listed item confirmed remedied by observation or verified evidence
criteria.false: Any item open, unchecked, unverified or contradicted elsewhere

next_step.instructions: What should happen with this follow-up case now?

criteria.close_case: No further action; case closed with compliance confirmed.
criteria.request_evidence: Ask operator for one specific missing proof before deciding.
criteria.issue_notice: Serve improvement notice with fixed deadlines for open items.
criteria.refer_lead: Pass to lead officer for prohibition or prosecution review.

worst_hazard.instructions: Which hazard area does the most serious open item concern?

criteria.no_open_item: Every contravention closed; nothing remains open to classify.
criteria.records_only: Worst open item is paperwork: HACCP, training or logs.
criteria.premises_fabric: Worst open item is structure, equipment or cleaning standard.
criteria.food_handling: Worst open item is temperature, cross-contamination or pest control.

overdue_extent.instructions: How far past due is the most overdue open item?
criteria: No open item is past its due date
Most overdue open item is 1 to 14 days late
Most overdue open item is 15 to 42 days late
Most overdue open item is over 42 days late

residual_risk.instructions: How serious is the public health risk still remaining?
criteria: Negligible: no open items of any kind remain
Low: only records or premises fabric items remain open
Elevated: one temperature, contamination or pest item, no adverse sample
Serious: 2+ such items, or one with adverse sample

factors.name: contravention_count
factors.description: Number of contraventions listed in the original inspection.

factors.name: resolution_share
factors.description: Proportion of listed items actually remedied by the revisit, before evidence is considered.

factors.name: worst_open_area
factors.description: Hazard area of the most serious item still open after revisit and evidence.

factors.name: food_handling_open_count
factors.description: Number of open temperature, contamination or pest items (0 when worst_open_area is not food_handling).

factors.name: cross_section_mismatch
factors.description: Unannounced disagreement between sections about an item's identity, date or status.

factors.name: days_past_original_due
factors.description: Revisit date minus original due date of the most overdue open item; negative means not yet due.

factors.name: extension_agreed
factors.description: Written extension agreed for the most overdue open item, moving its effective due date later.

factors.name: benign_explanation
factors.description: Documented innocent cause for an alarming finding, e.g. engineer job sheet for chiller fault or pest contractor visit already booked.

factors.name: operator_evidence
factors.description: State of evidence the operator sent for items not seen remedied at revisit.

factors.name: adverse_sample
factors.description: Latest food or swab sample since inspection returned unsatisfactory.

factors.name: complaint_since_inspection
factors.description: Public complaint received since inspection and how it relates to open items.

factors.name: prior_enforcement_count
factors.description: Formal notices or warnings served on the premises in the past five years.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Values placed on scale edges: exactly 14 or 42 days late, extension agreed only verbally, or item marked partly remedied.

factors.name: reassuring_note_decoy
factors.description: Free text asserting full compliance or good progress regardless of the actual item statuses.

sections.name: premises
sections.description: Premises reference, trading name, business type, risk band and food business operator name.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Inspection date, officer initials and list of contraventions with ref, area code, requirement text and due_date.

sections.name: revisit
sections.description: Revisit date, per-item findings (ref, status, observed) and a one-sentence officer_note.

sections.name: correspondence
sections.description: Extension requests with agreed flag and new date, operator_reply text and evidence items with verified flag.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior hygiene ratings, enforcement actions, complaints with one-line summary, and sample results since inspection.

F412.rendering_notes: inspection.contraventions has contravention_count entries, each with ref (e.g. C3), area code (REC, FAB, CLN, TMP, XCN, PST) and due_date. Map REC to records, FAB/CLN to premises fabric, TMP/XCN/PST to food handling; the worst open area must be inferred from codes, never stated. revisit.items[] status values: remedied, part_remedied, not_remedied, not_checked; resolution_share and worst_open_area drive which items are not remedied, with food_handling_open_count fixing how many TMP/XCN/PST items stay open. An item not seen at revisit counts as remedied only if correspondence.evidence lists it with verified true; operator_evidence sets this (submitted_unverified gives verified false or null; submitted_partial covers only some open refs). days_past_original_due appears only as inspection due_date versus revisit.date; when extension_agreed is true, correspondence.extensions holds the ref with agreed true and a later new_due_date, so overdue must be measured against it; when false the request may still appear with agreed false or null as a decoy. cross_section_mismatch: trivial_format uses e.g. 'c3' vs 'C3' or date written differently but same day; ref_mismatch has revisit or evidence citing a ref absent from inspection; date_conflict gives evidence dated after revisit or extension date before original due; reply_contradicts_revisit has operator_reply claiming an item fixed that revisit marks not_remedied. benign_explanation appears as an evidence item or history entry (engineer job sheet, pest contractor booking) that explains but does not remedy the finding. adverse_sample appears in history.samples with result 'unsatisfactory' and a ref link; complaint_since_inspection appears in history.complaints with a one-line summary and outcome field. prior_enforcement_count is the length of history.enforcement. boundary_case sets overdue days to exactly 14 or 42, extensions noted as 'agreed by phone' with agreed null, or part_remedied statuses. reassuring_note_decoy puts phrases like 'all works completed' or 'good progress noted' in officer_note or operator_reply irrespective of item statuses. Free-text fields are officer_note, operator_reply and complaint summary only. No field may state overall compliance, risk level, overdue band, recommended action or case outcome; unknown values are null.

F413.role: Technical compliance reviewer at a commercial pest control contractor, checking each completed technician visit log before it is filed and released to the client
F413.setting: A regional pest control contractor services food production units, warehouses, care homes and offices under contract. Technicians submit a structured visit log from a handheld device after each routine or call-out visit. The log covers treatments applied, bait and monitoring station checks, and van stock drawn and returned. A reviewer in the technical office reads one log at a time. The reviewer compares it with the site's contract profile and the previous visit, decides whether it can be filed, and judges how serious any breach is.

usage_reconciled.instructions: Product quantities applied agree with van stock withdrawals for this visit.

criteria.true: Every applied product matches its net stock withdrawal.
criteria.false: At least one product quantity disagrees or is unlogged.

activity_increased.instructions: Rodent activity has increased since the previous logged visit.

next_step.instructions: What should the reviewer do with this visit log now?

criteria.sign_off: Log complete and compliant; file and release without further action.
criteria.request_records: One missing sheet, quantity or date must be supplied first.
criteria.book_revisit: Arrange corrective revisit or retreatment, with conditions stated to technician.
criteria.escalate: Refer to technical manager for breach handling or client notification.

breach_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst breach of terms in this log?
criteria: Clear: no record gap, all treatments within limits
Paperwork: record gap only, all treatments within limits
Treatment: a dose, label or licence limit exceeded
Prohibited: site-banned product or zone used in treatment

parties_needed.instructions: How many separate people or teams must act to resolve this?
criteria: One person can resolve it alone
Two people or teams must act
Three or four people or teams must act
Five or more people or teams must act

factors.name: stock_mismatch
factors.description: Size of disagreement between quantity applied in treatments and net quantity withdrawn in van_stock for one product

factors.name: stock_return_logged
factors.description: Whether van_stock carries a return entry that offsets an apparent surplus withdrawal, which can explain an otherwise alarming gap

factors.name: station_count_gap
factors.description: Number of stations on the site register that do not appear as checked in the monitoring section

factors.name: monitoring_sheet_missing
factors.description: Monitoring section is null although the visit type requires station checks

factors.name: date_sequence
factors.description: Ordering of visit start, visit end, client sign-off and follow-up booking dates

factors.name: activity_trend
factors.description: Count of stations showing rodent activity now compared with the previous visit's count

factors.name: previous_visit_available
factors.description: Whether the previous visit's activity count is present in follow_up history; if absent, an increase cannot be supported

factors.name: dose_overage_pct
factors.description: Percentage by which applied quantity per treated area exceeds the label maximum; zero for most records, small values sit on the boundary

factors.name: licence_valid_on_visit
factors.description: Whether the technician's certification expiry date falls on or after the visit date

factors.name: restricted_product_used
factors.description: Aggravating fact: a toxic rodenticide or banned product is applied in a zone where the site profile prohibits it

factors.name: corrective_status
factors.description: State of corrective actions raised on this visit

factors.name: site_risk_tier
factors.description: Contract risk tier of the premises, which affects how far a borderline breach should be escalated

sections.name: site_profile
sections.description: Site ID, risk tier, registered station list, zones with permitted and banned products

sections.name: visit
sections.description: Visit ID, type, technician ID, licence expiry, start and end timestamps, client sign-off date

sections.name: treatments
sections.description: List of applications: product code, active ingredient, zone, area_m2, qty_applied with unit, label_max_per_m2

sections.name: monitoring
sections.description: List of station checks: station ID, zone, activity boolean, bait_taken_pct, condition; may be null

sections.name: van_stock
sections.description: Product movements for the visit: withdrawals and returns with product code, qty, unit, batch

sections.name: follow_up
sections.description: Previous visit ID and its active-station count, corrective actions with status and booked dates

F413.rendering_notes: stock_mismatch shows only as treatments.qty_applied set against van_stock withdrawals minus returns for the same product_code. Trivial gaps are usually unit artefacts, such as 0.5 kg withdrawn against 480 g applied. applied_qty_null renders qty_applied as null. stock_return_logged adds a van_stock entry with movement 'return' that can close an apparent surplus. station_count_gap leaves station IDs from site_profile.stations missing from monitoring, and the check list is shuffled so the gap is not obvious. monitoring_sheet_missing sets monitoring to null for visit.type 'routine'. date_sequence is visible only by comparing visit.start, visit.end, visit.client_signoff and follow_up booked dates. activity_trend is the count of monitoring entries with activity true against follow_up.prev_active_stations. If previous_visit_available is false, prev_active_stations is null or the previous visit is absent. dose_overage_pct appears only as qty_applied divided by area_m2 against label_max_per_m2, sometimes in mixed units. licence_valid_on_visit compares visit.tech_licence_expiry with visit.start. restricted_product_used puts a treatment in a zone whose site_profile entry has toxic_bait_permitted false or lists the product under banned_products. When it is present, breach_severity is always Prohibited and next_step is escalate. corrective_status appears in follow_up.actions statuses and dates. site_risk_tier is site_profile.tier. Decoys include batch numbers, weather, visit duration, bait_taken_pct on inactive stations, and non-toxic monitoring blocks in banned zones, which are permitted. Never include fields that state compliance, breach level, trend, reconciliation result or recommended action.

F414.role: Play-area safety officer in a local authority parks department, reviewing one submitted equipment inspection return at a time before it is accepted onto the asset file
F414.setting: Contracted and in-house inspectors submit structured inspection returns for individual pieces of fixed playground equipment. Each return combines the asset register entry, the measurements and findings from the visit, linked repair work orders, site conditions and recent inspection history. The officer checks the return against the register and the maintenance log, judges how serious the worst hazard is and how far remedial work has progressed, and decides whether the asset can stay in use, needs restriction or closure, or must wait for a missing confirmation.

prior_defects_cleared.instructions: Every defect raised at the previous inspection is now closed out.

surfacing_adequate.instructions: Measured surfacing depth meets the requirement for the measured fall height.

criteria.true: Recorded depth at or above requirement for measured height
criteria.false: Depth below requirement, unmeasured, or rated for lower height

asset_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this asset following this inspection?

criteria.sign_off: No open hazards; asset accepted for continued public use.
criteria.sign_off_actions: Use continues; non-urgent repairs scheduled with due dates.
criteria.hold: Decision deferred until one missing measurement or record confirmed.
criteria.restrict_use: Hazardous component isolated; rest of asset stays open.
criteria.close_asset: Whole asset taken out of use until repaired.

remedial_progress.instructions: What share of the raised remedial work orders is closed?
criteria: No raised work orders closed yet
Some closed, but fewer than half
Half or more closed, at least one open
All raised work orders closed, or none raised

hazard_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst confirmed hazard on this asset?
criteria: Negligible: only cosmetic wear or no defects recorded
Low: defect logged with no injury mechanism identified
Moderate: defect could cause minor injury such as cuts
High: defect could cause fracture or other serious injury
Critical: life-threatening hazard such as head or neck entrapment

factors.name: equipment_type
factors.description: Kind of fixed play equipment inspected; changes which measurements and defect codes are relevant (chain wear for swings, run-out for slides, bearing play for roundabouts).

factors.name: register_mismatch
factors.description: Disagreement between the asset register and the inspection: none; trivial (asset_id formatting or install date off by days); moderate (surfacing type in register differs from type recorded on site); large (register critical fall height differs from measured fall height by more than 0.5 m).

factors.name: surfacing_depth_margin_mm
factors.description: Measured minimum surfacing depth minus the depth required for the measured fall height and the recorded surfacing type; values near zero sit on the boundary.

factors.name: worst_defect_class
factors.description: Injury mechanism of the worst non-entrapment defect logged, expressed through the defect code and component recorded in findings.

factors.name: head_neck_entrapment_fail
factors.description: Decisive aggravating fact: the entrapment probe test is recorded as failed for the head and neck probe at one or more openings. When true the worst hazard is Critical regardless of any other field.

factors.name: prior_defects_open
factors.description: Number of defects listed in the previous inspection whose linked work orders are still open, missing, or closed against a different component_id.

factors.name: work_orders_closed_fraction
factors.description: Proportion of work orders raised for this asset since the previous inspection that carry status closed with a closed_date on or before the inspection date.

factors.name: temporary_measure_in_place
factors.description: Mitigation: maintenance shows a temporary measure isolating the defective component (seat removed, barrier fitted, platform boarded) dated before or on the inspection.

factors.name: approved_variance
factors.description: Mitigation: register holds a current variance reference approving a known deviation (e.g. reduced run-out or alternative surfacing) for this asset.

factors.name: followup_check_passed
factors.description: Mitigation: a later operational check in history, dated after the inspection, records the flagged component as passed.

factors.name: missing_measurement
factors.description: One required measurement for this equipment type is null (surfacing depth, fall height or chain wear), leaving one confirmation outstanding.

factors.name: inspector_grade
factors.description: Grade of the inspection carried out; a routine visual check carries less weight for structural findings than an annual main inspection.

factors.name: usage_level
factors.description: Recorded footfall band for the site; context and partial decoy, raises attention but never changes severity on its own.

factors.name: incident_reports_90d
factors.description: Count of public injury or damage reports for the asset in the last 90 days; an alarming signal that may or may not relate to the logged defects.

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Register entry: asset_id, site_id, equip_type, install_date, std_ref, crit_fall_height_m, surf_type, variance_ref.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Visit details: insp_date, insp_grade, inspector_id, measured fall_height_m, surf_type_found, surf_depth_mm, chain_wear_pct, probe_results list, findings list of defect codes.

sections.name: maintenance
sections.description: List of work orders: wo_id, asset_id, component_id, defect_ref, raised_date, status, closed_date, temp_measure.

sections.name: site
sections.description: Site conditions: usage_level, closure_status, incident_reports_90d, last_vandalism_date.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior inspections and follow-up checks: date, grade, defect_refs raised, component results.

F414.rendering_notes: register_mismatch appears only by comparing asset fields with inspection fields (asset_id string vs work-order asset_id, surf_type vs surf_type_found, crit_fall_height_m vs fall_height_m); never flagged. surfacing_depth_margin_mm is never given; the reader compares inspection.surf_depth_mm with the requirement implied by fall_height_m and surf_type_found, using a requirement table embedded as inspection.surf_req_table (list of height band, type, min_depth_mm). worst_defect_class shows as findings items with defect_code, component_id and injury_mech (cosmetic, none, minor, serious); head_neck_entrapment_fail shows as a probe_results item {probe:'head_neck', opening_id, result:'fail'}; decoy probe items for finger or torso probes may fail without implying Critical. prior_defects_open is derived by matching history[-1].defect_refs against maintenance defect_ref and status; decoys include orders closed with a closed_date after insp_date or against a different component_id. work_orders_closed_fraction is computed from maintenance status and dates; zero raised orders renders an empty list. temporary_measure_in_place renders as maintenance.temp_measure with a type and date; approved_variance as a non-null asset.variance_ref with expiry date (expired references act as decoys); followup_check_passed as a history entry dated after insp_date with result pass for the flagged component. missing_measurement renders the relevant field as null. inspector_grade appears in inspection.insp_grade; usage_level and incident_reports_90d in site. Mitigation and alarming signals are sampled independently so each alarm appears with and without mitigation. No field states severity, disposition, compliance or completion; there is no risk rating, pass/fail summary or recommended action field, and no free-text notes.

F415.role: Contract monitoring officer for a borough council's public conveniences service, reviewing one contractor shift cleaning log at a time for a single toilet block
F415.setting: A cleaning contractor submits a digital log for every shift at each council-owned public toilet block. The log covers scheduled cleaning slots, the visits actually recorded, any hygiene faults reported during the shift and their remedy, and a supervisor sign-off. The officer checks each submitted log against the schedule and the contract standard. The officer decides whether a clean was genuinely missed, whether the sign-off is valid and what to do with the log. The officer also rates how long users were exposed to an unremedied fault. Closures, approved exemptions and operative notes often explain apparent gaps, so the officer must weigh them against the alarming signals.

missed_clean.instructions: At least one scheduled clean was genuinely missed without valid exemption.

criteria.true: A slot lacks a completed visit and no covering closure.
criteria.false: All slots completed, or gaps covered by approved closure.

sign_off_valid.instructions: The supervisor sign-off is valid for this shift log.

criteria.true: Authorised supervisor signed after the final recorded visit.
criteria.false: Missing, unauthorised signer, or signed before final visit.

next_step.instructions: What should the officer do with this shift log?

criteria.accept: Log meets contract standard with no follow-up needed.
criteria.accept_noted: Minor recording lapse noted against contractor, no service failure.
criteria.hold: One unconfirmed item must be evidenced before deciding.
criteria.default_notice: Confirmed service failure triggers a contractual default notice.

staff_effort.instructions: How much staff time would fully resolving this record require?
criteria: Under one hour of staff time needed
One to eight hours of staff time
One to five working days of staff time
More than five working days of staff time

fault_exposure.instructions: How long was an unremedied hygiene fault open to users?
criteria: No fault open while block was public
Open-to-public fault remedied within 60 minutes
Open-to-public fault remedied after 60 to 240 minutes
Open over 240 minutes or never remedied

factors.name: scheduled_slots
factors.description: Number of cleaning slots scheduled for the shift; sets how many visits the log should contain.

factors.name: missed_slots
factors.description: Number of scheduled slots with no completed visit recorded (visit absent from list or status not_recorded).

factors.name: closure_covers_gap
factors.description: Whether an approved closure or exemption window in site.closures overlaps the missed slot(s); only meaningful when missed_slots > 0, otherwise renders as an unrelated closure or none.

factors.name: closure_approved
factors.description: Whether any closure entry carries an approver; an unapproved closure does not excuse a gap.

factors.name: sign_off_state
factors.description: State of the supervisor sign-off: valid, missing (section null), signed by an operative not on the supervisor list, or timestamped before the last visit.

factors.name: fault_type
factors.description: Hygiene fault reported during the shift, if any.

factors.name: fault_open_minutes
factors.description: Minutes between fault reported_at and remedied_at; values above 400 render as remedied_at null. Clusters near the 60 and 240 anchors.

factors.name: block_closed_during_fault
factors.description: Whether a closure window covers some or all of the fault-open period, reducing time the fault was open to the public.

factors.name: checklist_completion
factors.description: Completeness of per-visit task checklists: all ticked, some tasks unticked on at least one visit, or checklist null on at least one visit.

factors.name: photo_evidence
factors.description: Whether completed visits carry a photo reference; missing photos are a recording lapse, not proof of a missed clean.

factors.name: timestamp_out_of_order
factors.description: Whether a visit is logged before shift start or out of sequence with its neighbours, casting doubt on that visit.

factors.name: note_content
factors.description: What the free-text notes convey: routine, an alarming but benign remark, an explanation of a gap that is not backed by a closure entry, or a remark contradicting the structured log.

factors.name: prior_defaults_90d
factors.description: Count of default notices at this site in the last 90 days; context only and a decoy for this log's decisions.

sections.name: site
sections.description: Block identity, opening hours and a closures list with window, reason and approver.

sections.name: shift
sections.description: Shift date, start and end times, contractor crew and scheduled slot times.

sections.name: visits
sections.description: List of recorded visits with slot, timestamps, status, checklist, photo reference and op_note.

sections.name: faults
sections.description: List of hygiene faults with type, reported_at, remedied_at, source and remedy_note.

sections.name: sign_off
sections.description: Supervisor signer id, signer role, signed_at and a short comment; null if absent.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior 90-day counts for this site: defaults, complaints, audits passed.

F415.rendering_notes: scheduled_slots renders as shift.sched_slots (list of HH:MM times). missed_slots renders as slots in shift.sched_slots with no matching visits entry, or a visits entry with status 'not_recorded'; vary the two forms. closure_covers_gap renders as a site.closures entry whose from/to window spans the missed slot time; when false, closures is empty or holds a window elsewhere in the day. closure_approved renders as closures[].approved_by being an officer id or null. sign_off_state: valid gives a signer_role 'supervisor' and signed_at after the last visit's end time; missing makes sign_off null; unauthorised_signer gives signer_role 'operative'; signed_before_last_visit gives signed_at earlier than the final visits[].end. fault_type none gives an empty faults list. fault_open_minutes renders only as reported_at and remedied_at timestamps (remedied_at null if over 400); the reader must compute the duration. block_closed_during_fault renders as a closures window overlapping the fault interval; exposure counts only time the block was open. Its window may also be the one that covers a missed slot. checklist_completion renders in visits[].checklist as a map of task:boolean, with some false, or as null. photo_evidence renders as visits[].photo_ref string or null. timestamp_out_of_order renders as a visit start earlier than shift.start or earlier than the previous visit. note_content renders in visits[].op_note, faults[].remedy_note and sign_off.comment. Examples include 'strong smell, traced to sewer works on road outside' (alarming_benign) and 'block shut 11:00-12:00 for police incident', with no closures entry (explains_gap_unbacked). Another is 'pan cleared 10:40' while remedied_at is null or later (contradicts_log). Decoys are history.prior_defaults_90d, history.complaints_90d, site.footfall_band and faults[].source ('public_app' vs 'staff'), none of which decide this log's answers. Records must never contain fields such as missed, exposure_minutes, valid_sign_off, outcome or recommended_action. All durations and gaps must be inferred by comparing timestamps across sections. Use ISO 8601 date-times, numbers as numbers and null for unknown values.

F416.role: Area lifeguard supervisor reviewing each station's daily shift log before it is filed
F416.setting: A coastal council lifeguard service runs patrolled beaches from towers along a stretch of coast. Each tower submits one structured shift log per day covering roster, hourly sea conditions and flags, incidents, rescue equipment status and handover totals. The area supervisor reviews each log on its own and decides whether rescues had proper guard cover, whether the figures reconcile, how serious the day's worst casualty outcome was, how long essential kit was out of service, and what to do with the log now.

two_guard_cover.instructions: Every logged water rescue had at least two qualified guards present.

criteria.true: Each rescue lists two in-date qualified responders.
criteria.false: Some rescue had fewer than two qualified responders.

totals_reconcile.instructions: Handover totals agree with the itemised incidents and equipment entries.

criteria.true: Rescue, first-aid and kit-defect totals match itemised entries.
criteria.false: At least one total differs from itemised entries.

next_step.instructions: What should the area supervisor do with this shift log now?

criteria.accept_log: Log consistent and complete; file without further action.
criteria.request_item: One specific supporting record missing; request it before filing.
criteria.amend_and_file: Only minor clerical discrepancy; supervisor corrects entry and files.
criteria.corrective_order: Operational lapse found; order station fix before next shift.
criteria.escalate_review: Serious outcome or uncovered rescue; refer to area safety manager.

outcome_severity.instructions: How serious was the worst casualty outcome recorded this shift?
criteria: None: no casualty, or on-site first aid only
Referred: casualty directed to own doctor or clinic
Conveyed: ambulance called and casualty taken to hospital
Critical: CPR, AED shock or fatality recorded

kit_outage.instructions: How long was essential rescue kit out of service without substitute?
criteria: No essential kit out of service unsubstituted
Unsubstituted outage totalling under 60 minutes
Unsubstituted outage totalling 60 to 180 minutes
Unsubstituted outage totalling over 180 minutes

factors.name: rescue_count
factors.description: Number of water rescues itemised in the incidents list; zero makes two_guard_cover vacuously true and lowers attention.

factors.name: rescue_cover_shortfall
factors.description: Whether one rescue lacked a second qualified guard: none, only one responder listed, a responder whose qualification had lapsed, or a responder not rostered on at that time.

factors.name: mutual_aid_logged
factors.description: A guard from a neighbouring tower, with in-date qualification, appears among the rescue responders, restoring two-guard presence when the shortfall is single_guard or off_roster.

factors.name: totals_mismatch
factors.description: Discrepancy between handover totals and itemised entries: none, rescue count off by one, first-aid count off by one, a defect counted but not listed in equipment, an incident dated to another day, or several at once.

factors.name: worst_outcome
factors.description: Most serious casualty disposition among incidents, shown through outcome codes, ambulance references and AED usage fields.

factors.name: kit_gap_band
factors.description: Total time an essential item (AED, oxygen, rescue board, tube) was logged out of service; end_time_null leaves the return time unknown.

factors.name: kit_substitute_logged
factors.description: A spare unit identifier is recorded against the outage for its whole duration, so the gap does not count as unsubstituted.

factors.name: missing_record
factors.description: One supporting reference absent: AED daily check sheet, ambulance job reference for a conveyed casualty, or qualification record for a listed responder.

factors.name: flag_lag
factors.description: At least one hourly reading shows rip_risk high while the flag field still shows red_yellow rather than red.

factors.name: zone_relocated
factors.description: The same reading has bathing_zone_moved true, meaning flags were shifted away from the rip, which mitigates the flag lag.

factors.name: signoff_present
factors.description: Senior guard sign-off identifier and time present in the shift section; absence pushes towards request or amend.

factors.name: boundary_placement
factors.description: Places a value on a scale or claim boundary: outage of exactly 60 or 180 minutes from rounded times, or a responder qualification expiring on the shift date.

factors.name: decoy_load
factors.description: Amount of alarming but irrelevant detail: very high beach-user estimate, strong offshore wind, cold water, many advisory contacts.

sections.name: shift
sections.description: Station id, tower code, shift date, start and end times, sign-off guard id and time.

sections.name: roster
sections.description: List of guards with id, role, on and off times, qualification expiry date, home station.

sections.name: conditions
sections.description: Hourly readings: time, wave_m, wind_kt, wind_dir, water_c, rip_risk, flag, bathing_zone_moved.

sections.name: incidents
sections.description: List of incidents: id, date, time, type, responder ids, outcome code, aed_used, ambulance_ref, referral_ref.

sections.name: equipment
sections.description: Essential kit items: item, unit id, last_check date, out_from, out_to, substitute_unit_id.

sections.name: handover
sections.description: Totals: rescues, first_aid, kit_defects, advisories, beach_users_est, check_sheet_ref.

F416.rendering_notes: rescue_count sets the number of incidents with type water_rescue. rescue_cover_shortfall is shown only indirectly: single_guard gives one responder id; responder_qual_expired gives a responder whose roster qual_expiry precedes the shift date; responder_off_roster gives a responder whose roster on/off times exclude the incident time. mutual_aid_logged adds a responder whose roster home_station differs from shift.station_id with in-date qualification; it does not fix an expired qualification. two_guard_cover is true only if every rescue has two responders who are rostered at that time with qual_expiry on or after the shift date; with boundary_placement, expiry equals shift date, leaving it contested. totals_mismatch is never announced: handover.rescues or first_aid differs by one from the itemised count, handover.kit_defects exceeds equipment entries with out_from set, or an incident date differs from shift.date; totals_reconcile is true only when none apply. worst_outcome appears via outcome codes (released, gp_advised, conveyed, cpr_commenced, deceased), aed_used and ambulance_ref; a conveyed casualty with ambulance_ref null corresponds to missing_record ambulance_ref, but outcome code still decides severity. kit_gap_band is computed from out_from and out_to; end_time_null sets out_to null, making kit_outage contested between adjacent levels; kit_substitute_logged fills substitute_unit_id, and a fully substituted outage scores the lowest level. missing_record nulls handover.check_sheet_ref, ambulance_ref or a roster qual_expiry. flag_lag shows rip_risk high with flag red_yellow in a reading; zone_relocated sets bathing_zone_moved true in that same reading. Next step: escalate_review when outcome is critical, or a rescue lacked two qualified guards and outcome is conveyed or worse; corrective_order for an unmitigated cover shortfall, an unmitigated flag lag, or unsubstituted outage of 60 minutes or more; request_item when only a missing_record is present (or sign-off missing); amend_and_file when only a trivial totals mismatch or date misentry exists; accept_log otherwise. Decoys: beach_users_est, wind_kt, water_c, advisories and wave_m are alarming-looking but decide nothing alone. No field ever states compliance, severity, risk or a recommended action; no free-text notes are included.

F417.role: Mooring allocations officer at a municipal harbour, reviewing each berth allocation request before the vessel arrives
F417.setting: A mid-sized commercial and leisure harbour assigns visiting and seasonal vessels to pontoon and quay berths. Each allocation record joins the vessel's declared and surveyed particulars, the assigned berth's limits, the booked stay, supporting documents, the berthing account and the vessel's prior visits. The officer checks one record at a time, reconciles the sections and decides whether the allocation can stand.

length_fits.instructions: Vessel's surveyed length fits within the assigned berth limit.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this mooring allocation now?

criteria.confirm_allocation: Record is complete and consistent; allocation stands as booked.
criteria.request_document: One specific missing document or figure must arrive before deciding.
criteria.allocate_with_conditions: Allocate now with stated conditions such as reduced stay or tide limits.
criteria.refer_harbourmaster: Problem exceeds officer authority; harbour master must decide on it.

primary_issue.instructions: Which single issue most affects this allocation?

criteria.no_issue: Sections agree and nothing required is missing or overdue.
criteria.dimension_mismatch: Vessel length or draught disagrees with berth limits or survey.
criteria.document_gap: Insurance, certificate or inspection is missing, null or expired.
criteria.account_arrears: Unpaid berthing dues or deposit outstanding without approved plan.
criteria.date_conflict: Stay dates overlap another booking or appear out of order.

ukc_band.instructions: How much under-keel clearance remains at lowest charted tide?
criteria: Grounding: draught equals or exceeds low-water berth depth
Tight: clearance under half a metre at low water
Adequate: clearance half a metre to under one metre
Ample: clearance of one metre or more

unresolved_count.instructions: How many unresolved cross-section discrepancies does this record contain?
criteria: No unresolved discrepancies across any section
Exactly one unresolved discrepancy between sections
Two unresolved discrepancies between sections
Three or more unresolved discrepancies between sections

factors.name: loa_mismatch_pct
factors.description: Percentage by which declared length overall differs from the surveyed length; zero in many records, small in some, large in a few

factors.name: berth_length_fit
factors.description: How surveyed length compares with the berth's maximum length, including the published fender allowance

factors.name: ukc_margin_m
factors.description: Berth depth at lowest charted tide minus the vessel's draught, in metres; negative means grounding

factors.name: draught_source
factors.description: Where the draught figure comes from: survey certificate, owner declaration only, or not recorded

factors.name: insurance_status
factors.description: Third-party insurance state relative to the booked stay

factors.name: inspection_state
factors.description: Safety inspection status and its date relative to arrival

factors.name: arrears_amount
factors.description: Outstanding berthing dues on the account in pounds

factors.name: payment_plan_approved
factors.description: An approved instalment plan covers any outstanding dues

factors.name: dimension_waiver
factors.description: A harbour master waiver permits the vessel on this berth despite a length or depth shortfall

factors.name: date_overlap
factors.description: Overlap between this stay and the next booking on the same berth

factors.name: trusted_regular
factors.description: Long-standing berth holder with several clean prior visits

factors.name: prior_incidents
factors.description: Count of recorded berthing incidents on previous visits

factors.name: boundary_placement
factors.description: Key values are set exactly on a threshold, such as clearance of 0.5 m or length equal to limit

sections.name: vessel
sections.description: Vessel identifier, type, declared loa_m, beam_m and draught_m, plus draught_src

sections.name: berth
sections.description: Assigned berth id, max_loa_m, fender_allow_m, depth_lat_m and any waiver reference

sections.name: booking
sections.description: Arrival and departure dates, nights booked and next booking on the berth

sections.name: documents
sections.description: Survey certificate with surveyed loa and draught, insurance expiry and inspection date

sections.name: account
sections.description: Dues outstanding, deposit paid flag, payment plan id and credit balance

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of prior visits with dates, berth ids and incident counts

F417.rendering_notes: loa_mismatch_pct shows only as vessel.loa_m against documents.survey.loa_m; berth_length_fit is derived by comparing documents.survey.loa_m with berth.max_loa_m plus berth.fender_allow_m. ukc_margin_m is never shown; the reader subtracts the effective draught (survey draught if present, else vessel.draught_m) from berth.depth_lat_m. draught_source appears as vessel.draught_src and documents.survey.draught_m being a number or null. insurance_status shows as documents.insurance_expiry (ISO date, null, or section key absent) compared with booking.departure. inspection_state shows as documents.inspection_date null, a future date flagged by documents.inspection_booked true, or a date after booking.departure. arrears_amount is account.dues_outstanding_gbp; payment_plan_approved appears as account.plan_id non-null with account.plan_status 'approved'. dimension_waiver appears as berth.waiver_ref non-null with berth.waiver_expiry covering the stay. date_overlap is computed from booking.departure against booking.next_on_berth.arrival. trusted_regular and prior_incidents appear only through the history list length, dates and per-visit incident counts. Decoys: account.credit_balance_gbp, vessel.beam_m (beam never limits these berths), vessel.home_port, history entries on other berths, and a survey date that is old but still in validity. No field states fit, clearance band, issue type, discrepancy count or recommended action; there is no status, risk or priority field.

F418.role: Area station staffing auditor, who reviews each completed platform staffing log against rosters, sign-on records and approved dispensations
F418.setting: A regional rail operator's station staffing assurance desk. After every shift, the duty manager submits a platform staffing log for each staffed platform. The auditor checks it one at a time. The log must show who was on the platform, when they signed on and off, whether they held in-date competence (dispatch, platform safety), any gaps below the platform's minimum staffing level, how gaps were covered, and whether an approved single-staffing or reduced-staffing dispensation applied. The auditor decides whether the log can be accepted, needs records chased, needs correcting with a team briefing, or must go to the route operations manager.

headcount_verified.instructions: Every person logged on platform has a matching valid sign-on.

criteria.true: Each logged person has matching sign-on and in-date competence.
criteria.false: Any logged person lacks sign-on, or competence is lapsed or absent.

next_step.instructions: What should the reviewer do with this staffing log now?

criteria.accept_log: Log reconciles and exposure is nil or covered by dispensation.
criteria.request_records: A named sign-on sheet or dispensation reference is missing.
criteria.correct_and_brief: Amend log entries and brief the team on a found shortfall.
criteria.escalate_ops: Refer to route operations manager for safety-critical breach or repeats.

coverage_outcome.instructions: How was the platform's minimum staffing covered during service hours?

criteria.fully_rostered: All minimum posts filled by rostered staff throughout service.
criteria.cover_arranged: Every gap filled by redeployed or relief staff, none left open.
criteria.partial_cover: Some gap minutes filled, but an open period remained.
criteria.uncovered: Gap left wholly unfilled from its start to its end.

reversal_time.instructions: How long would it take to fully undo this outcome?
criteria: Could be fully undone within one day
Needs one to seven days to undo
Needs eight days to three months to undo
Cannot be undone within three months

exposure_severity.instructions: How serious was the worst staffing exposure during passenger service?
criteria: No period below minimum during passenger service
Below minimum, but within a valid approved dispensation
Below minimum without valid dispensation, no safety duty missed
Safety-critical duty performed without certified staff present

factors.name: roster_attendance_mismatch
factors.description: Size and location of disagreement between rostered posts and attendance sign-on records: none; trivial (sign-on a few minutes off); minor (staff id swapped for an undocumented substitute); major (rostered person has no sign-on at all, or sign-off precedes logged end of duty by 30+ minutes)

factors.name: shortfall_minutes
factors.description: Total minutes the platform was below its minimum staffing level, derived only from gap events and sign-on/off times, never stated as a total

factors.name: shortfall_timing
factors.description: When the shortfall fell relative to the platform's passenger service window in the shift section

factors.name: dispensation_present
factors.description: Whether the controls section carries an approved reduced-staffing dispensation reference; the main mitigating signal

factors.name: dispensation_fit
factors.description: How well a present dispensation actually matches the gap: covers the whole gap; expired part-way through the gap; issued for a different platform number; or covers the time but its approver field is blank

factors.name: cover_arrangement
factors.description: How gap periods were filled: no cover recorded, full cover by redeployed or relief staff, or cover that starts late or ends early, leaving open minutes

factors.name: unqualified_dispatch
factors.description: Aggravating fact: at least one train was dispatched from a staff-dispatch platform during a gap by a person whose dispatch competence is absent or expired on the shift date, visible only by matching dispatch event times to attendance competence records

factors.name: competence_lapse
factors.description: Whether a logged person's platform safety competence expiry date in attendance falls before the shift date, separate from dispatch competence

factors.name: benign_closure
factors.description: Whether a planned possession or platform closure in controls overlaps the gap, so no trains called during part or all of it

factors.name: note_consistency
factors.description: Whether the duty manager's free-text remarks agree with listed events: consistent; contradicts (names a cover person absent from attendance, or claims no gaps when events show one); vague (mentions 'short-handed' with no times)

factors.name: missing_section
factors.description: Whether a needed part of the record is absent or null: none missing, attendance list null, or controls section referenced in remarks but null

factors.name: prior_shortfalls_30d
factors.description: Count of earlier logged shortfalls at this platform in the last 30 days; three or more supports escalation when a current unapproved shortfall exists, otherwise a decoy

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether a key time sits exactly on a boundary, such as a gap ending at the minute service starts or a dispensation valid_to equal to the gap end, leaving judges split

sections.name: shift
sections.description: Station code, platform number, shift date, shift start and end, passenger service window, min_staff, dispatch_mode

sections.name: roster
sections.description: List of planned posts: post, staff_id, role, planned_start, planned_end

sections.name: attendance
sections.description: List of sign-on records: staff_id, sign_on, sign_off, safety_comp_exp, dispatch_comp_exp; may be null

sections.name: events
sections.description: List of timed entries: type (gap_start, gap_end, cover_start, cover_end, dispatch, redeploy), time, staff_id, platform

sections.name: controls
sections.description: Dispensation and possession details: disp_ref, disp_platform, valid_from, valid_to, approved_by, possession_from, possession_to, prior_shortfalls_30d

sections.name: remarks
sections.description: One to three short free-text lines from the duty manager about the shift

F418.rendering_notes: roster_attendance_mismatch appears as differences between roster and attendance: shifted sign_on times, a different staff_id with no redeploy event, or a missing attendance row. shortfall_minutes and shortfall_timing are never given as totals; derive them from gap_start/gap_end and cover events against shift.service_from/service_to. dispensation_present controls whether controls.disp_ref is filled or null. dispensation_fit shows as valid_to before gap_end, disp_platform differing from shift.platform, or approved_by null. cover_arrangement appears as cover_start/cover_end events that span the gap fully, partly or not at all. unqualified_dispatch is visible only when a dispatch event time falls inside a gap and that staff_id's dispatch_comp_exp is null or before shift.date, while shift.dispatch_mode is 'staff'. competence_lapse shows as safety_comp_exp earlier than shift.date. benign_closure fills possession_from/to overlapping the gap. note_consistency is in remarks lines, for example naming a relief person absent from attendance, or saying 'all covered' against an open gap. missing_section sets attendance or controls to null, often while remarks refer to it. prior_shortfalls_30d sits in controls as a plain integer. Decoys: expiry dates falling within days after the shift date, which are still valid; gaps entirely outside the service window; a high prior_shortfalls count on a clean shift; remarks expressing worry with no matching event; overtime flags on roster rows. No field may state severity, breach status, coverage outcome, verification result or recommended action. Totals, flags such as 'breach' and computed gap durations must never appear.

F419.role: Aerodrome pavement friction analyst reviewing each continuous friction measuring equipment survey before it is accepted
F419.setting: A regional airport's airside engineering office keeps one record per runway friction survey. Each record holds survey metadata and the threshold levels in force, the measuring device's calibration and settings, the measured runs split into runway thirds and 100 m segments, surface texture readings, maintenance history and the sign-off state. The analyst reviews one record at a time. For each, they decide whether a genuine deficit is shown, what happens next, the main driver of any deficit, how severe the worst reading is and how complete the required evidence is.

genuine_deficit.instructions: The record shows a genuine friction deficit below the maintenance planning level.

next_step.instructions: What should happen next with this friction test record?

criteria.file_routine: Valid test, every value at or above maintenance planning level.
criteria.hold_retest: Validity in doubt from calibration, conditions or gaps; no minimum breach.
criteria.monitor_closely: Valid deficit below planning level, removal works already scheduled.
criteria.schedule_works: Valid deficit below planning level, no corrective works scheduled.
criteria.restrict_ops: Any third or segment below minimum; NOTAM and restriction needed.

deficit_driver.instructions: What is the main driver of any friction deficit recorded?

criteria.none_found: No third or segment falls below maintenance planning level.
criteria.rubber_deposits: Deficit concentrated in touchdown zones, texture adequate, removal overdue.
criteria.surface_texture: Deficit spread along runway alongside low measured macrotexture depth.
criteria.test_artefact: Deficit coincides with off-standard test settings or higher cross-check.

friction_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst friction reading against the thresholds?
criteria: Clear: all thirds and segments at or above design level
Watch: lowest value between maintenance planning and design levels
Planning: lowest value below maintenance planning, above minimum level
Critical: any third or 100 m segment below minimum

evidence_completeness.instructions: How complete is the required evidence in this test record?
criteria: Four or more required elements missing, null or misdated
Three required elements missing, null or misdated
Two required elements missing, null or misdated
One required element missing, null or misdated
All required elements present and dated before sign-off

factors.name: min_third_band
factors.description: Band of the lowest runway-third average friction, relative to the design objective, maintenance planning and minimum levels stated in the record

factors.name: near_boundary
factors.description: Lowest third average sits within 0.01 of the threshold that separates its band from the neighbouring band

factors.name: localised_segment_below_min
factors.description: Aggravating fact: at least one 100 m segment average falls below the minimum friction level, even when every third average is higher

factors.name: deficit_location
factors.description: Where along the runway the lowest readings cluster

factors.name: days_since_rubber_removal
factors.description: Days between the last completed rubber removal and the survey date

factors.name: removal_scheduled
factors.description: An open rubber removal or resurfacing works order starts within 14 days of the survey

factors.name: calibration_status
factors.description: State of the device calibration relative to the survey date

factors.name: missing_elements_count
factors.description: Number of further required elements left null or absent: tyre pressure, water depth, reverse-direction run, weather block, sign-off

factors.name: test_condition_anomaly
factors.description: Off-standard test condition that could depress readings

factors.name: macrotexture_band
factors.description: Mean texture depth on the weakest third relative to the record's texture threshold

factors.name: cross_check_result
factors.description: Outcome of a second-device check run within 48 hours of the survey

factors.name: prior_survey_trend
factors.description: Pattern of the previous two surveys' lowest third values

sections.name: test_meta
sections.description: Runway designator, survey date and time, test speed, threshold levels in force, weather block

sections.name: device
sections.description: Device type and serial, calibration certificate date and expiry, tyre pressure, self-wetting water depth

sections.name: runs
sections.description: List of runs by direction, each with three third averages and 100 m segment averages

sections.name: surface
sections.description: Mean texture depth per third, texture threshold, contaminant observed at test

sections.name: maintenance
sections.description: Last rubber removal date, open works orders with start dates, prior surveys and cross-check runs

sections.name: review
sections.description: Analyst assignment, sign-off timestamp and sign-off role, null when not yet signed

F419.rendering_notes: test_meta.thresholds carries design, maint_planning and minimum values for the stated speed, for example 0.72/0.52/0.42 at 65 km/h. A decoy set for 95 km/h is shown but does not apply when test_speed_kmh is 65. min_third_band is rendered only through runs[].thirds numeric averages; the analyst compares the lowest third average across both directions with the thresholds. near_boundary places that lowest value within 0.01 of a threshold. localised_segment_below_min appears as one value in runs[].segments_100m below thresholds.minimum, while the thirds average stays higher because the neighbouring segments are good. deficit_location shapes which thirds and segments are low: the touchdown thirds for each direction, all thirds, or the middle third. days_since_rubber_removal is derived from maintenance.last_rubber_removal against test_meta.survey_date. removal_scheduled appears as a maintenance.works_orders entry with type rubber_removal and start_date within 14 days. Decoys: a closed past works order and a works order for an unrelated taxiway. calibration_status: valid means device.cal_expiry is after the survey date; expired means cal_expiry is before it; post_dated means cal_cert_date is after the survey date; missing means the calibration fields are null. missing_elements_count nulls device.tyre_pressure_kpa, device.water_depth_mm, test_meta.weather, review.signed_at, or removes the reverse-direction run. Each missing or null element and any non-valid calibration counts towards evidence_completeness. test_condition_anomaly: tyre_pressure_off shows a pressure outside the spec range given in device.tyre_spec_kpa; natural_rain shows test_meta.weather.precip_mm above 0 with surface.contaminant wet; speed_off shows runs[].mean_speed_kmh more than 5 km/h from test_speed_kmh. macrotexture_band appears as surface.mtd_mm per third against surface.mtd_threshold_mm. cross_check_result appears as maintenance.cross_checks with device serial, date and third averages, or as an empty list. prior_survey_trend appears as maintenance.prior_surveys with dates and lowest_third values, or as an empty list. Further decoys: wind speed, air temperature, runway length, run count, a high-reading third, device serial. No field states a band, severity, validity, cause, recommended action or completeness score. No boolean flags such as below_minimum or valid_test. No free-text fields.

F420.role: Load control officer at an air freight hub, reviewing each completed ULD pallet build record before it is released to the ramp for loading
F420.setting: A cargo terminal builds airline pallets (ULDs) from many air waybills. Each build produces a record that combines the planned build, the manifested pieces, the measured result at the build station, the dangerous goods notification, any approvals, and a log of checks. The load control officer reviews one pallet record at a time and decides whether the pieces reconcile, what to do with the pallet, which discrepancy class matters most, how far the weighed gross departs from plan, and how much physical rework is needed.

pieces_reconciled.instructions: Every manifested piece is accounted for on this pallet build.

criteria.true: Counts match, or shortfall covered by part-shipment record
criteria.false: Unexplained shortfall, extra piece, or count not recorded

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this pallet before departure?

criteria.release: Pallet goes to the ramp as built and documented
criteria.release_conditional: Released once a single ramp-side securing fix is confirmed
criteria.hold: Kept at build area awaiting one outstanding confirmation or document
criteria.rebuild: Returned to build team to remove, add or reposition pieces

worst_discrepancy.instructions: What is the most serious unresolved discrepancy class on this record?

criteria.none: No unresolved disagreement between any sections of the record
criteria.paperwork_only: Only identifiers or document fields disagree; physical build within limits
criteria.physical_build: Weight, height, piece count or securing outside limits, no DG issue
criteria.dangerous_goods: Dangerous goods segregation or NOTOC disagreement remains unresolved

weight_deviation.instructions: How far does measured gross weight depart from planned gross?
criteria: Measured gross within 1% of planned gross
Measured gross differs from plan by over 1% to 3%
Measured gross differs from plan by over 3% to 5%
Measured gross differs from plan by over 5%

rework_extent.instructions: How much physical rework does this build need before release?
criteria: None: build stands as recorded, no physical change
Minor: one securing fix only, strap or net
Partial: some pieces removed, added or repositioned
Full: pallet broken down and built again

factors.name: weight_deviation_pct
factors.description: Signed percentage by which the scale gross differs from planned gross (sum of manifest line weights plus ULD tare); values cluster near the 1%, 3% and 5% boundaries in some records

factors.name: piece_count_gap
factors.description: Net difference between manifested pieces and pieces counted on the build for one or more AWB lines; 0 means all counted, positive means short, negative means extra

factors.name: part_shipment_on_file
factors.description: Whether an approved part-shipment entry exists that exactly covers a piece shortfall on the affected AWB; sampled independently so shortfalls appear with and without it

factors.name: height_vs_contour
factors.description: How the measured maximum height compares with the contour limit for the assigned position

factors.name: contour_waiver
factors.description: Whether an approved contour waiver for this ULD and position raises the allowed height; sampled near even so over-height appears with and without mitigation

factors.name: dg_state
factors.description: Dangerous goods content and segregation between classes on the same pallet

factors.name: notoc_match
factors.description: Whether the NOTOC lines agree with DG pieces in the manifest (UN number, class, piece count)

factors.name: securing_state
factors.description: State of straps and net on the measured build compared with the requirement for the ULD type

factors.name: scale_cal_overdue
factors.description: Whether the build scale's calibration due date is earlier than the build timestamp, making the weighed gross unconfirmed

factors.name: reweigh_logged
factors.description: Whether an independent reweigh on a calibrated scale is logged after the build; mitigates an overdue scale or a borderline deviation

factors.name: doc_field_mismatch
factors.description: A document-only disagreement between sections that does not affect the physical build

factors.name: minutes_to_cutoff
factors.description: Minutes between record review time and the flight's ULD acceptance cut-off; decoy that creates apparent urgency but does not change any answer

factors.name: prior_rebuilds
factors.description: Number of earlier rebuilds of this ULD for the same flight in the checks log; decoy history count that does not by itself change answers

sections.name: plan_header
sections.description: ULD id and serial, type, flight, date, deck position, contour code, contour_max_cm, tare_kg, planned_gross_kg, straps_required, cutoff_utc

sections.name: manifest_lines
sections.description: List of AWB lines with awb, dest, pcs, weight_kg, dims_cm, shc codes, un_no and dg_class or null

sections.name: build_measured
sections.description: Build station result: built_utc, scale_id, scale_gross_kg, max_height_cm, pcs_counted by AWB, straps_fitted, net_fitted (boolean or null), uld_serial_scanned

sections.name: dg_notoc
sections.description: NOTOC lines with awb, un_no, dg_class, pcs, position; null when no DG declared

sections.name: approvals
sections.description: Lists of part_shipments (awb, pcs_this_flight) and contour_waivers (uld, position, max_cm), possibly empty

sections.name: checks_log
sections.description: Scale calibration due date, reweigh entries with scale and kg, earlier rebuild entries with timestamps

F420.rendering_notes: No free-text fields; all values are codes, numbers, ISO timestamps, booleans or null. weight_deviation_pct: plan_header.planned_gross_kg equals tare_kg plus the sum of manifest_lines weight_kg; build_measured.scale_gross_kg differs by the sampled percentage. The officer must compute the percentage; no field shows it. If reweigh_logged, checks_log.reweigh holds a calibrated-scale reading which supersedes the build scale for the weight score. piece_count_gap: build_measured.pcs_counted lists counts per AWB; one or more lines differ from manifest pcs. Place the shortfall on varied lines, sometimes split across two. If part_shipment_on_file and the gap is a shortfall, approvals.part_shipments shows pcs_this_flight equal to the counted figure for that AWB. Occasionally pcs_counted for one AWB is null, which makes pieces_reconciled false. height_vs_contour: compare build_measured.max_height_cm with plan_header.contour_max_cm; a contour_waiver entry for the same ULD and position replaces the limit, but only if its uld and position match the header. In some records the waiver names a different position as a decoy. dg_state: shown via manifest shc and dg_class pairs on the same ULD; segregation conflicts arise from incompatible class pairs. notoc_match: dg_notoc lines omit an AWB or show different pcs. When there is no DG, dg_notoc is null. securing_state: straps_fitted compared with straps_required; net_fitted is null for net_not_logged. scale_cal_overdue: checks_log.scale_cal_due is earlier than build_measured.built_utc. doc_field_mismatch: an AWB in dg_notoc or part_shipments has transposed digits, a manifest dest differs from the flight destination, or uld_serial_scanned differs from the header serial. minutes_to_cutoff and prior_rebuilds are decoys and change no answer. Answer logic: worst_discrepancy takes the most serious unresolved class in the order dangerous_goods > physical_build > paperwork_only > none. Physical_build covers weight deviation over 3%, unwaived over-height, an unexplained piece gap, or any securing shortfall. rework_extent is None when nothing physical is needed. It is Minor for one_strap_short or net_not_logged, Partial for unwaived over-height up to 5cm, extra pieces, or weight deviation over 3% to 5%, and Full for over-height over 5cm, two or more straps short with other issues, a DG segregation conflict, or deviation over 5%. Disposition is rebuild when rework is Partial or Full. Otherwise it is hold when one confirmation is outstanding: overdue scale without reweigh, a NOTOC mismatch, a document field mismatch, or net not logged. Otherwise it is release_conditional when rework is Minor, and release otherwise. Contested records arise when a deviation sits within 0.2 points of a threshold, height is exactly at the limit, or a waiver's max_cm equals the measured height. Never include fields such as status, risk, ok, approved_for_release or discrepancy flags that state an answer.

F421.role: Depot damage assessor at a regional parcel sorting depot, reviewing one damaged-item record at a time
F421.setting: When a parcel is found damaged at or after intake, depot staff open a damage record. It combines manifest data, scan history, an inspection report, the sender's declared value or claim, and short free-text notes. The assessor works out whether the depot is liable, whether the record is complete enough to act on and how much of the item's value is lost. They then decide what happens to the record next.

depot_fault.instructions: Damage occurred while the parcel was in this depot's custody.

criteria.true: Damage first recorded after a clean inbound scan here.
criteria.false: Damage predates intake, or timing cannot be established.

contents_match.instructions: Damaged item described in the report matches the manifest's declared contents.

next_step.instructions: What should the assessor do with this damage record now?

criteria.close_no_action: Record complete and no claim or onward action is required
criteria.request_evidence: Obtain one named missing item, such as photos, before deciding
criteria.approve_repack: Accept depot liability now; repack, forward or write off item
criteria.escalate_supervisor: Refer to claims supervisor for value, tampering or liability dispute

loss_share.instructions: What share of the declared value is lost to damage?
criteria: Negligible: estimated loss under 5% of declared value
Partial: estimated loss from 5% to under 50%
Major: estimated loss from 50% to under 100%
Total: item written off, loss equals full declared value

parties_needed.instructions: How many separate people or teams must act to resolve this?
criteria: One person can resolve it alone
Two people or teams must act
Three or four people or teams must act
Five or more people or teams must act

factors.name: damage_timing
factors.description: When the damage actually arose relative to depot intake: already present on arrival, caused during depot handling, or genuinely unclear from the scans

factors.name: manifest_mismatch
factors.description: Where the inspection report disagrees with the manifest: none, a trivial unit or format difference, a quantity difference, a different item description, or a large weight gap

factors.name: inspection_state
factors.description: Completeness of the damage inspection: complete, photos not attached, inspection still pending, or damage_report section null

factors.name: loss_pct
factors.description: True estimated loss as a percentage of declared value; values cluster near the 5% and 50% boundaries in some records

factors.name: declared_value
factors.description: Sender's declared value in GBP; high values push towards supervisor referral

factors.name: scan_order_anomaly
factors.description: Damage was logged with a timestamp earlier than the depot inbound scan, or an outbound scan precedes inspection

factors.name: tamper_signs
factors.description: Evidence of resealing, cut tape or missing contents suggesting interference rather than accidental damage

factors.name: sender_packaging_poor
factors.description: Mitigating factor: the sender's packaging was inadequate for the contents, which weakens depot liability even when damage arose in the depot

factors.name: prior_damage_scans
factors.description: Number of earlier scan events at upstream hubs carrying a damage or exception code

factors.name: fragile_misrouted
factors.description: The manifest carries a fragile service flag, but the handling events show the parcel went through the standard conveyor rather than manual handling

factors.name: note_slant
factors.description: Tone of the free-text notes, which may be neutral, may blame the sender or carrier, or may assert depot fault without evidence; this is a decoy

factors.name: claim_amount_gap
factors.description: Ratio of the sender's claimed amount to the depot's own repair or replacement estimate; above 1 means an overclaim

sections.name: parcel
sections.description: Manifest data: parcel_id, service, fragile flag, declared contents, quantity, weight_kg, declared_value_gbp

sections.name: handling_events
sections.description: Ordered list of scan events with ts, site, event code and exception code

sections.name: damage_report
sections.description: Inspection record: inspected_ts, inspector, observed_item, qty_found, weight_kg, condition, photos list, repair_est_gbp; may be null

sections.name: claim
sections.description: Sender claim: claim_id, claimed_gbp, item_desc, packaging_desc, submitted date; may be null

sections.name: notes
sections.description: One to three short free-text lines from depot staff or the sender

F421.rendering_notes: damage_timing shows only indirectly, through handling_events: an exception code (e.g. DMG, CRUSH) at an upstream hub or on the inbound scan means before_intake; clean inbound followed by a damage code at a depot sort event means in_depot; unclear means the first damage code coincides with the inbound scan, or the events are sparse. prior_damage_scans adds that many upstream exception codes; some are decoy codes such as ADDR or WET-label that are not damage. manifest_mismatch is shown by comparing parcel.declared contents, quantity and weight_kg against damage_report.observed_item, qty_found and weight_kg: trivial_unit uses g against kg or a synonym, quantity uses an off-by-one or more, item_description names a different product, and weight_large differs by over 20%. Mismatches are never flagged. inspection_state works as follows: photos_missing gives an empty photos list; inspection_pending sets inspected_ts and repair_est_gbp to null; report_null sets damage_report to null. loss_pct is rendered as damage_report.repair_est_gbp relative to parcel.declared_value_gbp, or as condition 'written_off'; the assessor must compute the share. claim.claimed_gbp equals repair_est_gbp multiplied by claim_amount_gap, so an inflated claim is a decoy for the loss scale. scan_order_anomaly sets damage_report.inspected_ts or a damage event before the inbound scan ts. tamper_signs appears in damage_report.condition text (e.g. 'tape cut and resealed') or as qty_found below the manifest quantity with an intact box. sender_packaging_poor appears in claim.packaging_desc or in a note (e.g. 'single-wall box, no void fill'). fragile_misrouted pairs parcel.fragile=true with a CONV-STD event in handling_events. note_slant drives the notes text; notes that admit or deny fault are never decisive on their own. No field states liability, fault, a loss band, a next action or a severity; the record contains only raw manifest, scan, inspection and claim data.

F422.role: GDP Responsible Person reviewing customer returns held in the warehouse quarantine cage
F422.setting: A licensed pharmaceutical wholesale warehouse receives returned stock from pharmacies and hospitals. Each return is booked into a locked quarantine location and must be dispositioned before its hold limit. The Responsible Person opens one return record at a time. They compare the customer's claim, the original dispatch, the physical inspection, unique-identifier scans, temperature evidence and the customer's storage compliance, then decide what happens to the stock.

storage_maintained.instructions: Stock stayed within labelled storage conditions while away from the warehouse.

batch_traceable.instructions: Every counted pack belongs to a batch originally dispatched to this customer.

criteria.true: Each counted batch appears on the linked dispatch.
criteria.false: A counted batch is missing from dispatch, or no dispatch is linked.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this quarantined return now?

criteria.release_stock: All packs pass every check; return them to saleable stock.
criteria.request_evidence: One named document is missing; obtain it before deciding.
criteria.partial_release: Release sound packs; send failed or short-dated packs for destruction.
criteria.reject_destroy: No pack is resaleable; book the whole return for destruction.
criteria.escalate_qp: Unexplained authenticity or traceability failure; refer to the Qualified Person.
