resaleable_share.instructions: What share of counted packs is fit for saleable stock?
criteria: No counted pack is fit for resale
Fewer than half of counted packs fit
Half or more, but not all, fit
Every counted pack fit for resale

disposition_urgency.instructions: How soon must this return be dispositioned before its hold limit?
criteria: Routine: more than 20 days remain before hold limit
Planned: 10 to 20 days remain before limit
Prompt: 4 to 9 days remain before limit
Urgent: 0 to 3 days remain before limit
Overdue: effective hold limit already passed

factors.name: storage_class
factors.description: Labelled storage requirement of the product: ambient up to 25°C, or refrigerated 2–8°C. This sets which temperature evidence is needed.

factors.name: logger_coverage
factors.description: Whether the temperature logger window spans the period from customer delivery to warehouse receipt, leaves a gap at either end, or is absent.

factors.name: excursion_minutes
factors.description: Cumulative minutes the logged readings sat outside the labelled range. Values below 30 are rendered as 0.

factors.name: stability_allowance_on_file
factors.description: Mitigation: a manufacturer stability statement is on file that tolerates excursions up to a stated duration and temperature.

factors.name: batch_reconciliation
factors.description: How counted batch and expiry compare with the original dispatch lines: exact; same batch with expiry in a different format; one line with a batch never dispatched to this customer; or no dispatch reference found.

factors.name: count_discrepancy_packs
factors.description: Difference between packs claimed on the customer return note and packs physically counted, spread across one or more lines.

factors.name: damaged_pack_fraction
factors.description: Share of counted packs with broken anti-tamper seals, crushed cartons or pharmacy labels attached.

factors.name: uid_alert
factors.description: Alarming signal: at least one pack's unique identifier scan returns a decommissioned or unknown status at verification.

factors.name: uid_alert_explained
factors.description: Mitigation for a scan alert: the decommission event was made at this customer's own site within 10 days, so the pack is eligible for reactivation.

factors.name: days_out_of_control
factors.description: Days between delivery to the customer and receipt back at the warehouse, compared against the policy maximum for saleable returns.

factors.name: customer_audit_current
factors.description: Mitigation: the customer site holds an in-date storage audit and a signed storage declaration covering this return.

factors.name: quarantine_days_remaining
factors.description: Days from review date to the original hold limit (received date plus hold limit days). Negative means the limit has passed.

factors.name: hold_extension_approved
factors.description: Mitigation: an approved hold extension moves the effective limit to a later date.

factors.name: shelf_life_months_remaining
factors.description: Months from review date to the counted pack expiry, compared with the minimum remaining shelf life required for saleable stock.

sections.name: return_header
sections.description: Return id, customer site, delivered_at, received_at, review_date, reason code, and claimed lines with qty_claimed.

sections.name: dispatch_ref
sections.description: Original dispatch number and date, with lines of gtin, batch, expiry and qty_dispatched; null if unlinked.

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Counted lines with gtin, batch, expiry, qty_counted, packs_damaged and seals_intact, plus a list of uid_scans with status and event details.

sections.name: temperature
sections.description: Storage class, labelled range, logger id, logger_start and logger_end, min_c, max_c, minutes_out_of_range, and a stability_ref (null if none).

sections.name: customer_compliance
sections.description: Last storage audit date, audit_valid_until, and whether a storage declaration was received for this return.

sections.name: quarantine_control
sections.description: Location, hold_limit_days, extension object, max_days_out_of_control and min_shelf_life_months policy values.

F422.rendering_notes: storage_class appears in temperature.storage_class and temperature.labelled_range. logger_coverage is never stated; the reader must compare logger_start and logger_end with return_header.delivered_at and received_at. A gap shows as a start after delivery or an end before receipt; absent means logger_id, logger_start and logger_end are null. excursion_minutes appears as temperature.minutes_out_of_range, alongside min_c and max_c that sit outside or inside the labelled range consistently. stability_allowance_on_file appears as temperature.stability_ref, an object with max_hours and max_c, or null. batch_reconciliation is shown only by comparing inspection line batch and expiry with dispatch_ref lines. expiry_format_only renders as the same batch with expiry written as month-year on one side and a full date on the other. no_dispatch_link renders dispatch_ref as null. count_discrepancy_packs is split across lines as differences between return_header claimed qty_claimed and inspection qty_counted. damaged_pack_fraction is rendered as per-line packs_damaged and seals_intact counts. uid_alert appears as one or more inspection.uid_scans entries with status 'decommissioned' or 'unknown'. uid_alert_explained adds decommission_site matching the customer site id and a decommission_at within 10 days of review_date; otherwise the site is different or null. days_out_of_control must be computed from delivered_at and received_at against quarantine_control.max_days_out_of_control. customer_audit_current appears as audit_valid_until on or after review_date plus declaration_received true. quarantine_days_remaining is computed from received_at plus hold_limit_days against review_date. hold_extension_approved appears as extension {approved: true, new_limit_date}, which replaces the original limit; otherwise approved is false and new_limit_date is null. shelf_life_months_remaining is computed from counted expiry against review_date and min_shelf_life_months. Decoys: return_reason_code (for example ORDER_ERROR, OVERSTOCK, DAMAGED_IN_TRANSIT) does not decide anything, and a damage reason code may come with intact packs. quarantine_location codes, logger battery level, and an extra matching dispatch line for a product not returned are also decoys. Mismatches are never flagged. No field may state resaleability, urgency, disposition, risk or a pass/fail verdict.

F423.role: Press-check approver (pressroom quality lead) at a commercial sheet-fed litho plant
F423.setting: Each record is one press-check event for a single job on a single press: the approver compares the OK sheet's colour and register readings with the job spec and the signed proof, checks the run log for sheets already printed, and decides whether the run may continue.

colour_in_tolerance.instructions: Every measured patch on the OK sheet is within the applicable tolerance.

criteria.true: All patches read at or under the applicable delta E limit
criteria.false: A patch exceeds the limit, or patch readings are missing

run_before_signoff.instructions: Production sheets were logged before the OK sheet was signed.

criteria.true: Production sheets precede signature, or run without any signature
criteria.false: No production sheets logged ahead of a signature

next_step.instructions: What should the press-check approver do with this record now?

criteria.release_run: Check passes and is signed; press continues the run unchanged.
criteria.hold_for_signoff: Press waits until the missing signed OK sheet is received.
criteria.adjust_and_recheck: Correct colour or register on press, re-pull and remeasure sheet.
criteria.escalate_manager: Refer to production manager to decide reprint or customer contact.

staff_effort.instructions: How much staff time would fully resolving this record require?
criteria: Under one hour of staff time needed
One to eight hours of staff time
One to five working days of staff time
More than five working days of staff time

scrap_exposure.instructions: How many production sheets are at risk of being scrapped?
criteria: No suspect production sheets printed yet
Suspect sheets within the job's overs allowance
Suspect sheets exceed overs, below 10% of run
Suspect sheets at or above 10% of run

factors.name: colour_deviation
factors.description: How far the worst OK-sheet patch sits from the spec delta E limit: none over, marginal (within 0.2 of the limit either side), one patch over, several patches over.

factors.name: concession_on_file
factors.description: Customer has signed a concession raising the allowed delta E for the job; when present the concession limit replaces the spec limit.

factors.name: readings_completeness
factors.description: Whether the colour readings section is complete, has some patch values null, or is null altogether.

factors.name: signoff_state
factors.description: Customer OK-sheet signature status: signed before production, not signed, or signed with a timestamp later than the first production sheet.

factors.name: sheets_before_check
factors.description: Production sheets counted in the run log ahead of the OK sheet or its signature.

factors.name: wrong_stock_loaded
factors.description: Stock code loaded on press differs from the job's specified stock and production sheets were printed on it, at least 10% of run quantity.

factors.name: overs_allowance_pct
factors.description: Percentage of run quantity the job allows as overs and spoilage; sets the boundary between the second and third scrap levels.

factors.name: register_offset_mm
factors.description: Worst measured misregister between colour units on the OK sheet, against a 0.15 mm spec.

factors.name: offset_in_trim_only
factors.description: The worst misregister reading comes from a target in the trim area outside the finished image, so it does not affect saleable product.

factors.name: spectro_calibration_age_days
factors.description: Days since the spectrophotometer used for readings was last calibrated; over 90 days makes marginal readings arguable.

factors.name: customer_tier
factors.description: Account tier of the customer; a decoy that does not change any answer.

factors.name: prior_stoppages
factors.description: Count of earlier press stoppages on this job in the run log; a decoy unless tied to a reading.

sections.name: job
sections.description: Job id, product type, stock_spec code, run_qty, overs_pct, due_date, customer_tier, spec_max_de.

sections.name: proof_signoff
sections.description: Contract proof id and date, ok_sheet_no, signed_at, customer_present flag, concession object or null.

sections.name: colour_readings
sections.description: Instrument id, calibrated_on date, list of patches with ink, target_lab and measured delta_e.

sections.name: registration
sections.description: List of register targets with unit pair, offset_mm and in_image boolean.

sections.name: run_log
sections.description: Press id, stock_loaded code, first_production_at, sheets_production, sheets_makeready, stoppages list.

F423.rendering_notes: colour_deviation appears only as colour_readings.patches[].delta_e numbers compared with job.spec_max_de, or with proof_signoff.concession.accepted_max_de when concession_on_file is true (otherwise concession is null). The same over-limit patch values occur with and without a concession about equally. readings_completeness: some patch delta_e values null, or colour_readings itself null; missing readings make colour_in_tolerance false and point next_step to adjust_and_recheck (re-pull and measure). signoff_state: proof_signoff.signed_at null when unsigned; when signed_after_production, signed_at is later than run_log.first_production_at. sheets_before_check is visible only as run_log.sheets_production with first_production_at timestamps relative to signed_at. wrong_stock_loaded shows only as run_log.stock_loaded differing from job.stock_spec, with sheets_production at least 10% of run_qty; this alone sets scrap_exposure to its top level and next_step to escalate_manager. Suspect sheets are production sheets printed while a spec failure held: wrong stock, colour over the applicable limit, or in-image misregister over 0.15 mm; compare their count with job.overs_pct times run_qty. register_offset_mm sits in registration.targets[].offset_mm; offset_in_trim_only sets in_image false on the worst target, so a large offset there is harmless. calibrated_on older than 90 days before the check date makes marginal readings contestable. Decoys: customer_tier, customer_present, prior_stoppages, sheets_makeready (make-ready waste is not production) and due_date. next_step ordering: release_run when readings pass and signature precedes production; hold_for_signoff when readings and register pass but signature is missing; adjust_and_recheck when colour, in-image register or readings fail but no wrong stock and suspect sheets are within overs; escalate_manager for wrong stock or suspect sheets beyond overs. No field states pass/fail, severity, tolerance verdict or recommended action; there are no free-text fields.

F424.role: Cellar quality technologist who signs off each fermented batch before it is released to packaging
F424.setting: A regional craft brewery's QA desk. Each record is one batch's fermentation log exported from the brewhouse system. It covers the batch header, daily gravity and temperature readings, cellar events with short operator notes, lab QC results, and the packaging release request. The technologist reviews one batch at a time and decides whether fermentation is genuinely finished, whether contamination is supported, what happens to the batch next, how serious its worst deviation is, and how many record discrepancies must be fixed before sign-off.

terminal_gravity.instructions: Fermentation reached terminal gravity within the recipe's target band.

criteria.true: Two consecutive stable readings inside target FG band
criteria.false: Gravity still moving, outside band, or stability unconfirmed

contamination_supported.instructions: The log's evidence supports microbial contamination of this batch.

criteria.true: Positive plate or corroborated off-flavour, not explained away
criteria.false: No positive result, or signal explained or unconfirmed

batch_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this batch next?

criteria.release: All results in and within spec; package as requested.
criteria.release_conditional: Results complete; minor fix or record correction required at packaging.
criteria.hold_retest: A pending or borderline result needs one confirming retest.
criteria.rework: Correctable defect; extend conditioning, re-pitch or blend before release.
criteria.dump: Uncorrectable defect or hard-limit breach; batch must be discarded.

deviation_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst unexplained deviation in this batch log?
criteria: Nil: no unexplained out-of-spec reading or lab result
Minor: worst unexplained deviation within 10% beyond limit
Major: worst unexplained deviation more than 10% beyond limit
Critical: hard limit breached or irreversible step logged

record_discrepancies.instructions: How many cross-section discrepancies must be corrected before sign-off?
criteria: No discrepancies between corresponding values across sections
Exactly one discrepancy between corresponding values
Two or three discrepancies between corresponding values
Four or more discrepancies between corresponding values

factors.name: gravity_status
factors.description: True state of attenuation at the end of the readings: stable inside the target FG band, stuck high, still dropping, or over-attenuated below the band.

factors.name: final_reading_gap
factors.description: Only one reading exists at the apparent terminal gravity, so stability across two readings cannot be confirmed.

factors.name: temp_excursion
factors.description: Largest fermentation temperature excursion above the strain's working range: none, brief and small (under 2°C for under 12 h), or sustained and large.

factors.name: excursion_mitigated
factors.description: An excursion is explained by an approved free-rise diacetyl rest or a probe fault confirmed by a second probe. Applies only when an excursion exists.

factors.name: micro_signal
factors.description: Strongest contamination signal in the log: none, a sensory note only (e.g. sour, phenolic), a presumptive plate growth, or a confirmed plate count above spec.

factors.name: micro_mitigated
factors.description: The micro signal is undercut by a later negative retest, a lab note attributing growth to plating error, or a sensory note from an untrained taster contradicted by the panel.

factors.name: diacetyl_mgl
factors.description: Measured diacetyl in mg/L against a spec limit of 0.10. Values cluster near the limit so some batches sit on the boundary.

factors.name: discrepancy_count
factors.description: Number of seeded material mismatches between corresponding fields in different sections: vessel ID, yeast strain or generation, volume, brew date vs first reading, target OG vs first gravity, batch ID in lab vs header.

factors.name: decoy_mismatch
factors.description: Presence of a trivial apparent mismatch that is not a real discrepancy: a rounding difference (≤0.001 SG, ≤0.5 hl) or a unit-converted value (°P vs SG) that agrees once converted.

factors.name: lab_result_pending
factors.description: One required lab result (ABV, diacetyl, or micro plate) is null with status pending at the time of review.

factors.name: hard_limit_breach
factors.description: Decisive aggravating fact: fermentation peaked above the strain's stated maximum tolerance (autolysis risk), the batch was blended into another tank before QA sign-off, or ABV exceeds the labelled duty band by more than 0.5% abv.

factors.name: release_pressure
factors.description: Urgency expressed in the release request note (none, routine, rush for an event or contract). Decoy only; it never changes the correct answers.

factors.name: operator_note_tone
factors.description: Tone of free-text operator notes, independent of the data: neutral, alarmed about something the data shows is fine, or reassuring about something the data shows is a problem.

sections.name: batch
sections.description: Header: batch_id, recipe, style, brew_date, vessel_id, volume_hl, yeast_strain, yeast_gen, og_target, fg_target_min, fg_target_max, strain_max_temp_c.

sections.name: readings
sections.description: List of dated readings: ts, gravity_sg or gravity_plato, temp_c, ph, probe_id.

sections.name: events
sections.description: List of cellar events (pitch, dry_hop, temp_change, transfer, blend, retest_request) with ts, vessel_id, actor and a one-sentence note.

sections.name: lab
sections.description: QC results: batch_ref, abv_pct, abv_label_band, diacetyl_mgl, micro_plate {result, cfu_ml, plated_on}, retest list, lab_note.

sections.name: release_request
sections.description: Packaging request: requested_date, format, volume_hl, vessel_id, requested_by, note.

F424.rendering_notes: gravity_status shows only through the readings list: the last two to four gravity values compared with batch.fg_target_min/max (some in °Plato, needing conversion). final_reading_gap leaves a single reading at the terminal value, with the prior reading still falling. temp_excursion appears as readings temp_c values above batch.strain_max_temp_c minus a margin. excursion_mitigated adds a temp_change event noting an approved free-rise, or a second probe_id reading normal at the same ts with a note flagging the first probe. micro_signal appears as an events note (sensory), lab.micro_plate.result 'presumptive' or a cfu_ml count. micro_mitigated adds a negative entry in lab.retest or a lab_note citing plating error or a panel contradiction. diacetyl_mgl sits in lab.diacetyl_mgl, often 0.09 to 0.11. discrepancy_count is realised as mismatches spread across varied pairs: batch.vessel_id vs a transfer event or release_request.vessel_id, batch.volume_hl vs release_request.volume_hl (beyond 0.5 hl), yeast_strain or yeast_gen vs the pitch event note, brew_date vs first reading ts, og_target vs first gravity (beyond 0.003 SG), lab.batch_ref vs batch_id. decoy_mismatch inserts rounding or unit-converted values that agree and must not be counted. lab_result_pending sets one lab value to null with a pending flag. hard_limit_breach appears as a reading above strain_max_temp_c, a blend or transfer event into another vessel dated before any QA sign-off, or lab.abv_pct exceeding abv_label_band by more than 0.5. When present, deviation_severity is Critical and the disposition is dump. release_pressure appears only in release_request.note. operator_note_tone shapes events notes and may contradict the data. No field may state an answer: no status, risk, complete, contaminated, severity or discrepancy-count fields. Free text is limited to events notes, lab_note and release_request.note, each one sentence.

F425.role: Grading floor quality controller at an egg packing station
F425.setting: A quality controller reviews one graded batch record at a time after it comes off the grader. Each record covers one consignment of eggs from a single flock: what the farm declared at intake, what the grader counted by size and outgrade bin, the equipment and store checks around the run, the flock's health status, and what was packed and stamped. The controller decides whether the counts hold together, what to do with the batch, what most explains any anomaly, how long the eggs waited before packing, and how heavy the outgrade loss was.

counts_reconcile.instructions: Intake, grader and packing egg counts agree within half a percent.

batch_disposition.instructions: What should happen to this graded batch now?

criteria.release_class_a: Checks complete, counts reconcile, packed within ten days of lay.
criteria.hold_pending: One check result or count confirmation still outstanding before release.
criteria.downgrade_class_b: Fails Class A timing or quality but fit for processing.
criteria.reject_withdraw: Positive swab or untraceable stamp code; keep out of food chain.

anomaly_cause.instructions: Which single cause best explains this batch's main anomaly?

criteria.no_anomaly: Counts agree and outgrades sit within normal station range.
criteria.count_error: Egg counts disagree between sections with no quality explanation.
criteria.equipment_fault: Overdue calibration without a passing recheck drives defect readings.
criteria.shell_quality: Ageing flock or shell defects account for raised outgrades.
criteria.storage_temperature: Unexplained sustained store temperature excursion accounts for dirty outgrades.

lay_to_pack.instructions: How many days passed between the oldest lay date and packing?
criteria: Prompt: packed within 3 days of oldest lay
Standard: packed 4 to 7 days after lay
Late: packed 8 to 10 days after lay
Overdue: packed more than 10 days after lay

outgrade_share.instructions: What share of eggs fed to the grader went to outgrades?
criteria: Fewer than 2% of graded eggs outgraded
From 2% to under 5% outgraded
From 5% to under 10% outgraded
10% or more of graded eggs outgraded

factors.name: count_gap_size
factors.description: Size of the largest disagreement between corresponding egg counts in different sections: none, trivial (under 0.5%), moderate (0.5% to 3%), or large (over 3%).

factors.name: count_gap_location
factors.description: Where the count disagreement sits: declared intake versus grader eggs_in, size and outgrade bins versus eggs_in, or packed units versus grader class_a_total.

factors.name: stamp_code_mismatch
factors.description: Producer code stamped at packing differs from the consignment producer code, usually by the method digit or one farm character.

factors.name: lay_to_pack_days
factors.description: Days between the oldest lay date in the consignment and the pack date; values of 3, 7, 10 and 11 sit on level boundaries.

factors.name: mixed_lay_dates
factors.description: Consignment lists two lay dates; the older one governs timing but the newer one is listed first.

factors.name: missing_check
factors.description: Which required check is absent or unfinished: none, candling sample null, salmonella swab result pending, scale check missing, or candling sample logged after run end.

factors.name: swab_positive
factors.description: Most recent flock salmonella swab returned positive; only possible when the swab is not pending.

factors.name: outgrade_rate_pct
factors.description: Sum of outgrade bins as a percentage of grader eggs_in; values near 2, 5 and 10 sit on level boundaries.

factors.name: dominant_defect
factors.description: Outgrade bin holding the largest share of rejected eggs.

factors.name: calibration_overdue
factors.description: Crack detector last calibration date is older than its stated interval at run start.

factors.name: calibration_mitigated
factors.description: A manual candling recheck during the run found a crack rate matching the detector within one percentage point.

factors.name: temp_excursion
factors.description: Egg store temperature above limit before grading: none, brief (under 30 minutes) or sustained (30 minutes or more).

factors.name: temp_mitigated
factors.description: A defrost cycle or door-open event is logged overlapping the excursion window, offering a benign explanation.

factors.name: flock_age_weeks
factors.description: Age of the laying flock; flocks over 65 weeks plausibly explain raised cracks without any equipment fault.

sections.name: consignment
sections.description: Intake details: farm_ref, flock_id, producer_code, method, lay_dates list, received_at, declared_eggs, trays.

sections.name: grading_run
sections.description: Grader output: grader_id, run_start, run_end, eggs_in, by_size counts, outgrades bins, class_a_total.

sections.name: checks
sections.description: Crack detector calibration, candling sample, scale check and egg store temperature log.

sections.name: flock
sections.description: Flock health: age_weeks, salmonella_vaccinated, last_swab with date and result, swab_pending.

sections.name: packing
sections.description: Pack output: pack_date, packs list of size and count, stamp_code, best_before, label_class.

F425.rendering_notes: count_gap_size and count_gap_location show only as differing numbers: consignment.declared_eggs against grading_run.eggs_in; the sum of grading_run.by_size (S, M, L, XL) plus grading_run.outgrades against eggs_in; or the sum of packing.packs (pack_size times count) against grading_run.class_a_total. Never add a variance field. consignment.trays is a decoy: trays times 30 rarely equals declared_eggs exactly and should not be treated as authoritative. stamp_code_mismatch appears as packing.stamp_code differing from consignment.producer_code (for example 1UK-4F17 against 2UK-4F17); consignment.method is a decoy that may or may not match. lay_to_pack_days is computed from the oldest entry in consignment.lay_dates and packing.pack_date; when mixed_lay_dates is true the newer date is listed first. packing.best_before is a decoy usually 28 days from the newest lay date. missing_check renders as checks.candling_sample null, flock.swab_pending true with last_swab.result null, checks.scale_check null, or checks.candling_sample.sampled_at later than grading_run.run_end. swab_positive renders as flock.last_swab.result 'positive'; flock.salmonella_vaccinated is a decoy that is usually true either way. outgrade_rate_pct and dominant_defect render only as counts in grading_run.outgrades (cracks, dirties, blood_spots, leakers, misshapen); misshapen stays small and is a decoy. calibration_overdue shows as checks.crack_detector.last_calibrated plus interval_days against run_start; calibration_mitigated adds checks.crack_detector.manual_recheck with n and cracks_found. temp_excursion shows as checks.store_temp.minutes_above_limit and max_c; temp_mitigated shows as checks.store_temp.defrost_logged true or a door_open_at time inside the window. flock_age_weeks appears only in flock.age_weeks. No field may state a disposition, cause, pass or fail, risk level, outgrade percentage or days-to-pack; packing.label_class always shows the intended class A, not the decision. No free-text fields.

F426.role: Packhouse spray-record checker reviewing grower orchard spray records before accepting each fruit lot
F426.setting: A fruit packhouse receives harvested lots from contracted orchards. Before a lot is packed, a checker opens the grower's spray application record for the block the lot came from. The checker compares applications against product label references, sprayer calibration and harvest dates, then decides whether the lot can proceed.

phi_cleared.instructions: Every product's withholding period elapsed before the first pick date.

criteria.true: All applications cleared their withholding period before picking.
criteria.false: An interval had not elapsed, or cannot be confirmed.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this spray record and lot now?

criteria.release_lot: Accept the record; lot proceeds to packing with no action.
criteria.request_evidence: Ask the grower for one named missing document before deciding.
criteria.hold_and_test: Hold the lot now and order residue sampling before release.
criteria.escalate: Refer to technical manager for rejection or regulator notification.

finding_class.instructions: What is the most serious class of finding here?

criteria.no_finding: All sections agree; no discrepancy of any kind found.
criteria.clerical_only: Only identifier, unit or code mismatches; doses and timing compliant.
criteria.label_deviation: Rate, application count or crop outside authorisation; intervals respected.
criteria.interval_breach: Picking began before at least one product's withholding period ended.

reversal_time.instructions: How long would it take to fully undo this outcome?
criteria: Could be fully undone within one day
Needs one to seven days to undo
Needs eight days to three months to undo
Cannot be undone within three months

rate_overrun.instructions: How far does the highest computed rate exceed its maximum?
criteria: Every product at or below its authorised maximum
Highest product over maximum by up to 10%
Highest product over maximum by above 10% to 25%
Highest product over maximum by more than 25%

factors.name: phi_status
factors.description: Gap between each application date and harvest.first_pick_date relative to product_ref.phi_days for the worst product.

factors.name: rate_overrun_band
factors.description: Highest ratio of qty_applied divided by area_treated_ha against max_rate_per_ha, after unit conversion.

factors.name: partial_block_spray
factors.description: Applications list area_treated_ha smaller than block.planted_area_ha; legitimate spot spraying that changes the computed rate if the wrong area is used.

factors.name: clerical_mismatch
factors.description: A minor disagreement between sections that does not affect dose or timing.

factors.name: minor_use_auth
factors.description: A minor-use authorisation reference exists in product_ref covering the block crop or a higher maximum rate, mitigating off-label or overrun signals.

factors.name: residue_test_clear
factors.description: Harvest residue test was sampled after picking and returned below limits, mitigating interval or rate concerns.

factors.name: calibration_state
factors.description: Sprayer calibration validity on the application dates, with nozzle output deviation as a partial mitigator.

factors.name: missing_item
factors.description: One piece of evidence absent that a decision may need.

factors.name: season_count_excess
factors.description: A product is applied more times this season than product_ref.max_apps_per_season allows.

factors.name: off_label_crop
factors.description: A product's approved_crops list does not include the block crop.

factors.name: num_applications
factors.description: Number of application entries in the season record.

factors.name: high_wind_decoy
factors.description: An application logs wind speed near or above the usual drift threshold, with sprayer_type sometimes a recycling tunnel sprayer that makes it harmless.

sections.name: block
sections.description: Block identity: block_id, grower_id, crop, variety, planted_area_ha, lot_id reference.

sections.name: applications
sections.description: List of spray events: app_id, date, product_code, qty_applied, qty_unit, area_treated_ha, water_l_ha, sprayer_id, operator_cert_no, wind_kmh.

sections.name: product_ref
sections.description: Label reference per product: product_code, active, max_rate_per_ha, rate_unit, phi_days, max_apps_per_season, approved_crops, minor_use_auth_ref.

sections.name: equipment
sections.description: Sprayer details: sprayer_id, sprayer_type, last_calibration, calibration_valid_to, nozzle_dev_pct.

sections.name: harvest
sections.description: Lot details: lot_id, block_id, first_pick_date, bins, residue_test with sampled, result_date, below_limit.

F426.rendering_notes: phi_status shows only through applications[].date, harvest.first_pick_date and product_ref[].phi_days; boundary_day puts the gap exactly at phi_days so inclusive versus exclusive counting is debatable; app_date_missing sets one date to null. rate_overrun_band is never stated: the reader must compute qty_applied / area_treated_ha, converting mL to L or g to kg where qty_unit differs from rate_unit, and compare with max_rate_per_ha (or the higher authorised rate when minor_use_auth_ref is non-null). partial_block_spray makes area_treated_ha below planted_area_ha; dividing by planted area understates the rate, which is a decoy. clerical_mismatch appears as unit_ml_vs_l (qty_unit inconsistent with magnitude), product_code_typo (e.g. 'CPX-210' vs 'CPX210'), sprayer_id_format between applications and equipment, or harvest.block_id differing from block.block_id by one character. minor_use_auth sets product_ref[].minor_use_auth_ref to a reference string, otherwise null. residue_test_clear sets harvest.residue_test.sampled true and below_limit true; residue_result_pending sets sampled true with below_limit and result_date null. calibration_state shows via equipment.calibration_valid_to versus application dates and nozzle_dev_pct (under 5 low, over 10 high); missing removes the dates. equipment_section_missing sets equipment to null; product_ref_entry_missing omits one used product; operator_cert_null nulls operator_cert_no on one entry. season_count_excess requires counting applications per product_code. off_label_crop omits block.crop from approved_crops. high_wind_decoy sets wind_kmh 18 to 25 with sprayer_type 'tunnel_recycling' about half the time. No field ever states compliance, overrun percentage, interval status, a finding category or a recommended action; there are no free-text fields.

F427.role: Monitoring data reviewer for a regional upland peatland restoration programme, checking each submitted field visit record
F427.setting: Field surveyors visit rewetted blanket bog sites to read dipwells, inspect peat dams, photograph fixed points and score vegetation quadrats. Each visit record arrives as a small JSON object. The reviewer reads one record at a time and decides several things. Did any water table drop come from failing dams? What should happen to the record next? Where does the water table sit against the site's target band? How bad is the worst dam defect? How complete is the required evidence?

dam_caused_drop.instructions: Recorded water table drop stems from dam defects, not dry weather.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this visit record now?

criteria.accept_record: Record complete, no defect needing action; file as routine.
criteria.request_data: A required element is missing; ask surveyor for it first.
criteria.recheck_next_visit: Minor issue only; add a targeted check to next routine visit.
criteria.schedule_repair: Dam defect needs works; raise repair order with contractor now.
criteria.escalate_lead: Dam failed or failure repeats; refer to programme lead.

hydro_state.instructions: Where does the mean water table sit against the target band?

criteria.well_below: Mean depth more than 15 cm below target band floor.
criteria.below_band: Mean depth up to 15 cm below target band floor.
criteria.within_band: Mean depth inside the site's target water table band.
criteria.above_band: Mean level above the band top, surface ponding likely.

dam_severity.instructions: How severe is the worst dam defect recorded this visit?
criteria: Intact: every inspected dam holding water, no defect logged
Seepage: water passing around dam, pool level maintained
Partial breach: overtopping or side-cut, pool below design level
Failed: dam breached, no water held behind it

evidence_completeness.instructions: How complete is the required monitoring evidence for this visit?
criteria: At most one of four required elements recorded
Two of four required elements recorded
Three of four required elements recorded
All four recorded, at least one only partly
All four required elements recorded in full

factors.name: dipwell_coverage
factors.description: Fraction of scheduled dipwells with a reading this visit; below 1.0 counts as partly recorded, below 0.25 as not recorded

factors.name: photos_status
factors.description: Whether fixed-point photographs were uploaded: full set, partial set or none (photos field null)

factors.name: quadrats_status
factors.description: Vegetation quadrat survey state: all quadrats scored, some scored, or section null because the survey was not done

factors.name: dam_inspection_logged
factors.description: Whether the dam inspection list is present; when false the structures.inspections list is null and dam severity cannot be confirmed

factors.name: worst_dam_defect
factors.description: True condition of the worst inspected dam, shown only through per-dam pool_level_cm compared with design_pool_cm and a defect code

factors.name: water_table_offset_cm
factors.description: Mean dipwell depth relative to the target band from site_targets; negative is below the band floor, positive is above the band top, and values near -15 or 0 are boundary cases

factors.name: rainfall_pct_normal
factors.description: 30-day rainfall as percentage of the long-term normal; low values offer a benign weather explanation for any water table drop

factors.name: control_dipwells_dropped
factors.description: Whether reference dipwells away from any dam also fell since the last visit, which points to weather rather than dam leakage

factors.name: repair_order_open
factors.description: An existing open works order already covers the defective dam, which mitigates the need to raise a new repair

factors.name: prior_failure_same_dam
factors.description: Count of earlier visits logging a breach at the same dam; two or more is a repeat failure

factors.name: date_sequence_fault
factors.description: The logger download timestamp or dam inspection date falls before visit_date, so those readings may belong to an earlier visit

factors.name: surveyor_grade
factors.description: Surveyor accreditation level; an accredited surveyor's remark that seepage is minor is more trusted than a trainee's

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Tone of the free-text surveyor note, which may overstate or play down the actual dam and water readings (decoy)

factors.name: grazing_signs
factors.description: Sheep or deer trampling and dung noted on the bog surface; irrelevant to hydrology and dam questions (decoy)

sections.name: visit
sections.description: Visit id, site_ref, visit_date, surveyor_id, surveyor_grade, weather_on_day.

sections.name: site_targets
sections.description: Target water table band (band_top_cm, band_floor_cm), dipwells_scheduled, dams_total, last_visit_date.

sections.name: hydrology
sections.description: List of dipwell readings, control dipwell readings with previous values, logger_download_at, rain_30d_pct_normal.

sections.name: structures
sections.description: Dam inspection list with pool levels, defect codes and remarks, plus open_work_orders list.

sections.name: vegetation
sections.description: Quadrat scores or null, photo set count, grazing_signs flag.

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Free-text surveyor_note and a prior_visits history list of dated dam breach entries.

F427.rendering_notes: There are four required elements: dipwell readings, fixed-point photos, vegetation quadrats and the dam inspection log. Dipwell readings come from dipwell_coverage: hydrology.dipwells lists only the read wells, and site_targets.dipwells_scheduled is the expected count, so the reviewer must compare the two. Under 25% read counts as not recorded; under 100% counts as partly recorded. Photos come from photos_status as vegetation.photos_uploaded against photos_expected, null when none. Quadrats come from quadrats_status: vegetation.quadrats is a list with some score fields null when partial, and the whole field is null when missing. When dam_inspection_logged is false, structures.inspections is null. worst_dam_defect appears per dam as pool_level_cm against design_pool_cm, a defect_code (OK, SEEP, OVTP, SIDE, BRCH) and a one-sentence remark; the severity is never stated as a label. water_table_offset_cm is never shown directly. Each dipwell shows depth_cm below the surface, which the reviewer must average and compare with band_top_cm and band_floor_cm; negative depths mean water above the surface. rainfall_pct_normal is hydrology.rain_30d_pct_normal. control_dipwells_dropped appears as hydrology.controls, each with depth_cm and prev_depth_cm. repair_order_open appears as an entry in structures.open_work_orders naming the dam_id with status 'raised' or 'contractor_booked'. prior_failure_same_dam appears as dated entries in notes.prior_visits. date_sequence_fault makes logger_download_at or an inspection's inspected_on earlier than visit.visit_date. note_tone shapes notes.surveyor_note, a sentence or two that can sound alarmed even when the dams are intact, or reassuring over a partial breach. Decoys are the surveyor note tone, grazing_signs, weather_on_day and photo counts; none of these bear on the hydrology or dam questions. Records must never contain fields such as severity, hydro_state, completeness, action_required or cause_of_drop. Answers must be inferred by comparing values across sections.

F428.role: Flood asset inspection reviewer at a regional river and coastal flood authority, checking each submitted gate inspection record before it is filed
F428.setting: Field inspectors submit one structured record per flood defence gate visit, covering mitre, vertical lift, flap, radial and stoplog gates. The reviewer reconciles the record against the asset register, defect list, works history and operating context. They then decide whether the latest closure test is valid, what to do next, which component class holds the worst open defect, how many cross-section discrepancies exist, and how severe the gate's flood risk is.

closure_test_valid.instructions: The latest logged closure test shows the gate sealing within limits.

criteria.true: Current test logged, within rated time and leakage limit
criteria.false: Test missing, failed, late, leaking or predates later repair

next_step.instructions: What should be done with this inspection record now?

criteria.sign_off: Record complete and acceptable; file without further action required.
criteria.request_retest: Ask for a post-repair closure test before deciding.
criteria.raise_repair: Issue a works order now, with interim operating restrictions.
criteria.escalate_engineer: Refer to the duty asset engineer for an urgent decision.

defect_class.instructions: Which component class holds the highest-graded open defect?

criteria.no_open_defect: No open defect above grade 1 is recorded.
criteria.seal: Highest-graded defect affects seals, sills or leakage paths.
criteria.drive_actuation: Highest-graded defect affects hinges, hoists, motors or locking gear.
criteria.structural: Highest-graded defect affects leaf, frame, anchorage or concrete.

section_discrepancies.instructions: How many values disagree between sections of the record?
criteria: Every cross-section value agrees with its counterpart
One value disagrees with its counterpart elsewhere
Two values disagree with their counterparts elsewhere
Three or more values disagree across sections

flood_risk.instructions: How severe is the flood risk from the gate's current condition?
criteria: Low: closes within rated time, no defect above grade 2
Moderate: closes within rated time, one grade 3 defect
High: closes late, or any grade 4 defect
Critical: cannot close, or outage exceeds permitted window

factors.name: gate_type
factors.description: Type of gate inspected; changes which components and units appear but not the decision logic

factors.name: closure_time_ratio
factors.description: Measured closure time in the inspection divided by rated closure time in the asset register

factors.name: max_defect_grade
factors.description: Highest grade (1 to 4) among open defects in the defect list

factors.name: dominant_defect_component
factors.description: Component class of the highest-graded open defect

factors.name: mismatch_count
factors.description: Number of genuine disagreements between corresponding values in different sections

factors.name: mismatch_location
factors.description: Where the first mismatch sits when mismatch_count is above zero

factors.name: test_status
factors.description: State of the latest closure test relative to repairs and limits

factors.name: repair_progress
factors.description: Status of work on the highest-graded defect

factors.name: mitigation_present
factors.description: Whether a mitigating arrangement accompanies the alarming signal

factors.name: mitigation_kind
factors.description: Form of mitigation when present

factors.name: days_to_forecast_peak
factors.description: Days from inspection date to the next forecast peak level reaching the gate sill

factors.name: borderline_case
factors.description: Key value placed on a threshold, e.g. closure ratio 0.98 to 1.02 or leakage at limit

factors.name: outage_beyond_permit
factors.description: Gate held out of service past its permit expiry while a flood alert is active

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Register data: asset_id, gate_type, rated_closure_s, seal_type, clear_width, consequence_class

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Visit details: insp_id, asset_id, insp_date, closure_test object with timings and leakage

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of open and closed defects with component, grade, measurements, first_seen

sections.name: maintenance
sections.description: Works orders with status, dates, retest reference, plus last_service date

sections.name: operations
sections.description: Outage state, permit, temporary barrier, flood alert flag and level forecast

F428.rendering_notes: asset: gate_type, rated_closure_s, seal_type (e.g. 'J_bulb', 'music_note'), clear_width with clear_width_unit, consequence_class (decoy: high class alone sets no level). inspection: asset_id (may differ from register by one character), insp_date, closure_test {performed bool, test_date, closure_s, leakage_l_min, leakage_limit_l_min, result 'pass'/'fail'/null}; closure_s = closure_time_ratio x rated_closure_s; not_performed gives performed false and null timings; failed shows result 'fail' or closure_s null with performed true; passed_predates_repair shows test_date earlier than the relevant work order's completed date. defects: list of {code, component, grade, length_mm or loss_pct, status 'open'/'closed', first_seen}; component values map to defect_class (seal/sill/leak path, hinge/hoist/motor/lock, leaf/frame/anchor/concrete); decoys include closed grade 4 defects and open grade 1 cosmetic paint defects. maintenance: work_orders list {wo_id, component, defect_code, grade_raised, status 'scheduled'/'in_progress'/'complete', raised, completed, retest_insp_id}; repair_progress drives status and whether retest_insp_id is null; old completed orders on other components are decoys; last_service is a decoy. operations: outage {status 'in_service'/'out_of_service', since, permit_ref, permit_expiry}, temp_barrier_deployed bool, flood_alert_active bool, forecast {peak_date, peak_level_mAOD, sill_level_mAOD}. Mismatches render as: different asset_id between asset and inspection; seal_type in register vs seal component in defects; width given in mm in one place and m elsewhere with inconsistent value; test before repair completion; work order grade_raised differing from defect grade; rated_closure_s quoted differently in work order. Rounding differences (e.g. 4.50 vs 4.5) are not mismatches. outage_beyond_permit renders as status out_of_service, permit_expiry earlier than insp_date and flood_alert_active true; it alone sets flood_risk to Critical and next_step to escalate_engineer. Mitigation renders as temp_barrier_deployed true, a valid permit_expiry after insp_date, a scheduled works order covering the worst defect, or a passing retest linked in maintenance; it may lower next_step (e.g. scheduled order lets a grade 3 seal defect be signed off) but never changes the observable flood_risk anchors. Ties in highest grade across components are deliberate contested cases. The record never contains fields like fit_for_service, risk_level, mismatch_flag or recommended_action; there are no free-text fields.

F429.role: Reservoir duty engineer reviewing gated spillway shift logs before sign-off
F429.setting: A water utility's reservoir operations team keeps one structured log per shift for each gated spillway. The duty engineer reviews each log alone and reconciles reservoir levels, gate movements, the discharge calculation, instrument readings and the notification trail. They decide whether the release stayed within licence, whether gate data agrees across sections, what happens to the log next, and which trigger tier the readings reached.

within_licence.instructions: The spillway release stayed within the licensed discharge limit throughout the shift.

criteria.true: Measured and calculated peak discharge both under limit.
criteria.false: A discharge figure exceeds the limit or is unavailable.

gates_reconciled.instructions: Gate openings in the operations list match those used in the discharge calculation.

next_step.instructions: What should the reviewer do with this shift log next?

criteria.accept_log: Sections reconcile and every required step is already recorded.
criteria.query_operator: Exactly one confirmation or minor data correction outstanding before closure.
criteria.hold_for_inspection: Post-operation inspection or an instrument field check remains outstanding.
criteria.escalate: Action trigger, licence breach or large data conflict needs senior engineer.

trigger_tier.instructions: Which highest trigger tier do this log's readings reach?
criteria: Normal: no reading at or above any alert trigger
Alert: highest reading between alert and action triggers
Action: at least one reading at or above action trigger
Critical: licensed ramp rate or discharge limit broken

parties_needed.instructions: How many separate people or teams must act to resolve this?
criteria: One person can resolve it alone
Two people or teams must act
Three or four people or teams must act
Five or more people or teams must act

factors.name: reservoir_tier
factors.description: Highest trigger band reached by the reservoir level or an unexplained piezometer reading during the shift

factors.name: near_boundary
factors.description: The peak level sits within 0.02 m of the next trigger threshold, so the tier can be read either way

factors.name: discharge_vs_licence
factors.description: Peak released discharge relative to the licensed maximum

factors.name: gate_position_mismatch
factors.description: Size of the disagreement between gate openings in gate_ops and those used in discharge.calc_inputs

factors.name: discharge_discrepancy_pct
factors.description: Percentage gap between the gauged downstream flow and the gate-rating calculated discharge

factors.name: datum_mismatch
factors.description: One reservoir level is recorded against gauge zero rather than the site datum, which offsets it by a fixed amount

factors.name: missing_section
factors.description: A required part of the log that is absent or null

factors.name: notice_after_release
factors.description: The downstream warning notification timestamp falls after the first gate opening, although it is required beforehand

factors.name: inspection_status
factors.description: State of the post-operation spillway chute and gate inspection

factors.name: piezometer_rise
factors.description: An embankment piezometer rises above its alert value during the release

factors.name: tailwater_explains_rise
factors.description: Mitigation: the recorded tailwater rise coincides with the piezometer increase and accounts for it

factors.name: ramp_limit_breached
factors.description: Aggravating: a gate opened faster than the licensed maximum ramp rate, so downstream flow rose beyond permitted speed

sections.name: log_header
sections.description: Dam and spillway identifiers, shift window, operator ID, log version and licence limits

sections.name: reservoir
sections.description: Timed level readings with datum, trigger thresholds and 24-hour rainfall

sections.name: gate_ops
sections.description: List of gate movements with gate ID, timestamp and opening before and after in metres

sections.name: discharge
sections.description: Calculation inputs per gate, calculated peak, gauged downstream peak and tailwater level

sections.name: instruments
sections.description: Piezometer and seepage weir readings with alert values and timestamps

sections.name: notifications
sections.description: Downstream warnings and internal call-outs with timestamps and acknowledgement flags

F429.rendering_notes: log_header holds licence_q_max_m3s and ramp_max_m_per_10min. reservoir_tier and near_boundary appear only through reservoir.readings[].level_m compared with reservoir.triggers.alert_m and action_m. When near_boundary is true, the peak sits within 0.02 m of a threshold. datum_mismatch makes one reading carry datum:'gauge_zero' while the others use 'site', with a fixed offset shown in reservoir.gauge_zero_offset_m. discharge_vs_licence is shown by discharge.calc_peak_m3s and gauged_peak_m3s against licence_q_max_m3s; near_limit puts one figure within 3% of the limit on either side. gate_position_mismatch compares gate_ops[].open_after_m with discharge.calc_inputs[].opening_m for the same gate_id: trivial is under 0.02 m, material is 0.05 to 0.2 m, large is over 0.2 m or a gate missing from one list. discharge_discrepancy_pct is the gap between calc_peak_m3s and gauged_peak_m3s. missing_section sets instruments to null, omits notifications entirely, or sets discharge.gauged_peak_m3s to null. notice_after_release is visible only by comparing notifications[type='downstream_warning'].sent_at with the earliest gate_ops timestamp. inspection_status appears as instruments.post_op_inspection: {status, completed_at}, with completed_at null unless the inspection is completed. piezometer_rise shows as a reading above its alert_kpa. tailwater_explains_rise shows as discharge.tailwater_m readings rising within 30 minutes of that reading. ramp_limit_breached is detectable only by computing the change in opening over time between consecutive gate_ops entries for one gate and comparing it with ramp_max_m_per_10min. Decoys: operator_id, log_version, rainfall_mm_24h, gate_ops entries with zero change, and seepage weir readings that are always within limits. No field states a tier, risk, breach, reconciliation result or recommended action; no free-text fields.

F430.role: Area asset condition engineer reviewing submitted substation inspection round reports
F430.setting: A regional distribution network operator's asset team receives one completed inspection round report per visit from field inspectors covering primary and secondary substations. Each report lists the site's asset register with operating limits, the round schedule, the readings taken (transformer oil temperature and level, SF6 gas pressure, battery float voltage, breaker operation counts), any defects the inspector logged with short notes, recent history (previous round readings, open work orders, permits to work, load events) and the network supply arrangement. The engineer reconciles these sections, judges how abnormal and how consequential the findings are, and decides what follow-up the report needs. No field states severity or disposition; these must be inferred.

defect_corroborated.instructions: The worst logged defect is corroborated by the recorded readings.

benign_explanation.instructions: The worst abnormal reading has a documented non-fault explanation.

criteria.true: Permit, known gauge fault or load event explains it.
criteria.false: No abnormal reading, or nothing documented accounts for it.

follow_up.instructions: What follow-up should this inspection round report receive next?

criteria.file_closed: Accept report as filed; no further action is required.
criteria.recheck_next_round: Accept, but flag one asset for targeted recheck next round.
criteria.hold_return: Return to inspector for one missing reading or photo first.
criteria.work_order: Raise planned maintenance work order within normal priority window.
criteria.urgent_attendance: Dispatch crew or arrange switching within twenty-four hours.

limit_deviation.instructions: How far does the worst reading stray beyond its limits?
criteria: All readings within their normal operating bands
Worst reading outside normal band, below alarm limit
Worst reading at or beyond alarm, below trip limit
Worst reading at or beyond its trip limit

supply_exposure.instructions: If the worst defective asset failed, how many customers lose supply?
criteria: None: no open defect, or in-service partner carries load
Few: fewer than 100 customers would lose supply
Some: 100 to 999 customers would lose supply
Many: 1,000 to 9,999 customers would lose supply
Widespread: 10,000 or more customers would lose supply

factors.name: worst_reading_band
factors.description: Band of the most abnormal reading relative to the register limits for that asset and parameter: within normal band, outside normal band only, at or beyond alarm, at or beyond trip.

factors.name: limit_unit_mismatch
factors.description: The worst reading is recorded in a different unit from the register limit (kPa vs bar, mV per cell vs V per string), so a raw comparison misleads until converted.

factors.name: benign_cause_present
factors.description: History contains a mitigating item that could explain an abnormal reading: active permit to work, gauge already logged as faulty, recorded load transfer or heatwave, or recent oil top-up.

factors.name: benign_cause_type
factors.description: Kind of mitigating item when present.

factors.name: benign_cause_covers
factors.description: Whether the mitigating item actually matches the abnormal asset and visit date; when false it names a different asset ID or its validity window ended before the round date, acting as a decoy.

factors.name: defect_claim
factors.description: Relationship between the inspector's worst logged defect and the readings: no defect logged, defect matches an abnormal reading, defect overstates a reading that is only mildly off, or defect has no supporting reading at all.

factors.name: trend_vs_last_round
factors.description: Direction of the worst parameter compared with the previous round's reading for the same asset.

factors.name: scheduled_assets_missed
factors.description: Number of assets in the round schedule with no reading entry from this visit.

factors.name: evidence_missing
factors.description: A defect references a photo or a confirming reading that is absent (photo_ref null, or the parameter named in the note was not recorded).

factors.name: redundancy_state
factors.description: State of the worst asset's redundant partner: in service, out of service on the outage plan, or no partner exists.

factors.name: customers_fed
factors.description: Customers supplied through the worst defective asset, from the register.

factors.name: trivial_discrepancies
factors.description: Count of harmless cross-section mismatches (asset ID suffix spelt differently, round date vs reading timestamp off by a day across midnight, inspector initials vs full name) that should not change any answer.

factors.name: near_boundary
factors.description: Worst reading sits within 2% of a band limit, or customers_fed sits within 5% of a supply_exposure threshold, leaving judges split.

sections.name: site
sections.description: Site ID, name, voltage, and asset register with units, normal band, alarm and trip limits, customers fed and partner ID.

sections.name: round
sections.description: Round ID, visit date, inspector, start and finish times, scheduled asset IDs, and a free-text inspector_note.

sections.name: readings
sections.description: List of readings: asset_id, param, value, unit, timestamp.

sections.name: defects
sections.description: List of logged defects: defect_id, asset_id, category, photo_ref, and a one-sentence free-text note.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Previous round readings, open work orders with short descriptions, permits to work with validity windows, and load events.

sections.name: network
sections.description: Outage plan entries, partner asset statuses and supply arrangement for the site.

F430.rendering_notes: worst_reading_band appears only as readings[].value against site.assets[] normal_band, alarm_limit and trip_limit; never print a band label. limit_unit_mismatch: readings[].unit differs from site.assets[].unit (e.g. 5.6 bar reading against a 520 kPa alarm), so the reviewer must convert. benign_cause_present/type: history.permits[] with a valid window, history.open_work_orders[].desc such as 'SF6 gauge on CB2 reading low, replacement ordered', history.load_events[] recording a transfer or high ambient temperature, or a top-up entry. benign_cause_covers=false: the item cites a neighbouring asset ID (T1 vs T2) or a permit window ending before round.date; it must look plausible. defect_claim: defects[].note wording vs readings (an 'oil weeping heavily' note with oil level in band = overstated; a note naming a parameter never recorded = unsupported); none_logged gives an empty defects list. trend_vs_last_round: compare readings with history.previous_round; no_previous gives history.previous_round null. scheduled_assets_missed: round.scheduled_assets contains IDs with no readings entry. evidence_missing: defects[].photo_ref null or a confirming parameter absent. redundancy_state: site.assets[].partner_id plus network.partner_status and network.outage_plan dates covering round.date; a partner listed in service in site but on outage in network is a deliberate cross-section conflict where network wins. customers_fed sits in site.assets[]; supply_exposure is zero when the partner is in service. trivial_discrepancies are scattered decoys (ID casing, midnight timestamps, initials) and must not drive answers. round.inspector_note may contain decoy reassurance ('all fine on site') or alarm ('smell of burning near panel') unsupported elsewhere. Rough answer logic: hold_return when evidence_missing or a scheduled asset missed and the outcome depends on it; recheck_next_round for outside_normal or covered alarm readings; work_order for uncovered alarm readings that are stable; urgent_attendance for trip, or uncovered alarm worsening with no in-service partner. Never include fields such as severity, priority, risk, recommended_action, explained or customers_at_risk.

F431.role: Metering validation analyst at a district heat network operator, checking each billing-period meter reading before it is released to customer billing
F431.setting: A residential and commercial heat network supplies dwellings and small premises through heat interface units, each with a heat meter. Every billing period, each meter produces one reading record. Some are remote reads, some are submitted by customers, some come from engineer visits, and some are system estimates. The analyst opens one record at a time. Each record holds the meter's identity and condition, the current reading, recent reading history, device diagnostics and site context. The analyst decides whether the reading is billable, whether any anomaly points to the meter itself, what to do next, and how far consumption has strayed from what was expected.

meter_fault.instructions: The consumption anomaly is attributable to a faulty or tampered meter.

criteria.true: Diagnostics, seal or delta-T evidence corroborate a device fault.
criteria.false: No corroborating fault evidence, or a benign explanation fits.

billable_actual.instructions: The period reading is a valid actual reading fit for billing.

criteria.true: Actual read, in sequence, with consumption explained or plausible.
criteria.false: Estimated, out of order, unevidenced or unexplained implausible consumption.

next_step.instructions: What should happen with this meter reading now?

criteria.accept_reading: Reading passes checks; release to billing without further work.
criteria.request_photo_read: Ask occupant or site for dated meter photograph before deciding.
criteria.bill_estimate: Replace unusable read with flagged estimate; correct at next actual.
criteria.escalate_engineer: Refer to metering lead for site visit or dispute handling.

staff_effort.instructions: How much staff time would fully resolving this record require?
criteria: Under one hour of staff time needed
One to eight hours of staff time
One to five working days of staff time
More than five working days of staff time

consumption_deviation.instructions: How far does period consumption deviate from expected baseline?
criteria: Deviation under 15% of weather-adjusted expected
Deviation 15% to under 40% from expected
Deviation 40% to under 100% from expected
Deviation of 100% or more from expected

factors.name: read_source
factors.description: How the current period reading was obtained. Remote and engineer reads are trusted. Customer reads need photographic evidence. System estimates are never actual reads.

factors.name: read_sequence_issue
factors.description: Ordering problem between the current read and history: read date earlier than the previous read, register value lower than the previous read, or duplicate timestamp.

factors.name: missing_section
factors.description: Which part of the record is absent or null. Diagnostics may be null, the previous-read entry may be missing so consumption cannot be computed, or the photo reference may be missing on a customer read.

factors.name: consumption_ratio
factors.description: Actual period consumption divided by the weather-adjusted expected consumption. It drives the deviation score and includes values sitting on the 15%, 40% and 100% boundaries.

factors.name: occupancy_change
factors.description: Site context shows a void period, a tenancy change or a new occupant within the period. This explains unusually low or high consumption.

factors.name: degree_day_ratio
factors.description: Heating degree days this period divided by the same period last year. A cold period mitigates high consumption and a mild one mitigates low consumption; the analyst must apply this when judging deviation.

factors.name: diagnostic_error_count
factors.description: Number of active device error codes, such as flow sensor fault, temperature probe open circuit or air in sensor. Two or more corroborate a fault; one alone does not settle it.

factors.name: meter_works_order
factors.description: An open or recently closed works order for meter exchange or recalibration falls within the period. This benignly explains a register reset or step change.

factors.name: consecutive_estimates
factors.description: Count of immediately preceding periods billed on estimates in the history list. Three or more makes another estimate unacceptable and pushes toward an actual read or escalation.

factors.name: delta_t_implausible
factors.description: Diagnostics show the return temperature at or above the flow temperature, or a near-zero delta-T while volume accumulates. This suggests swapped or failed temperature probes.

factors.name: seal_status
factors.description: Tamper seal state on the meter. It may be intact, broken with an engineer visit logged on the same date, broken with no matching visit, or not recorded.

factors.name: dispute_open
factors.description: The customer has an open billing or meter accuracy dispute recorded against this supply point. This requires escalation regardless of read quality.

sections.name: meter
sections.description: Meter identity and condition: serial, type, install date, last verification date, seal state and seal check date.

sections.name: period_read
sections.description: Current reading: read date, energy register kWh, volume register m3, read source code and photo reference.

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of previous period reads with date, register kWh, source code, and same-period consumption from last year.

sections.name: diagnostics
sections.description: Device telemetry: active error codes, mean flow and return temperatures, battery state and firmware; may be null.

sections.name: site_context
sections.description: Supply point context: occupancy status and change date, degree days now and last year, works orders, dispute flag.

F431.rendering_notes: read_source appears as period_read.src_code (AMR, CUS, ENG, EST). system_estimate also leaves period_read.photo_ref null, which is normal for that source. read_sequence_issue is never stated. It must be inferred by comparing period_read.read_date and reg_kwh with the latest history entry: an earlier date, a lower register, or the same timestamp. missing_section shows as diagnostics: null, a history list lacking the immediately preceding period, or period_read.photo_ref: null on a CUS read. consumption_ratio is rendered only indirectly. Period consumption is period_read.reg_kwh minus the last history reg_kwh. Expected consumption is history.same_period_ly_kwh scaled by site_context.hdd_current divided by site_context.hdd_prior_year. Raw numbers must be chosen so the computed ratio lands where the factor says, including exact boundary cases. occupancy_change appears as site_context.occupancy (occupied, void, changed) with tenancy_change_date inside the period. degree_day_ratio appears through the two hdd fields. diagnostic_error_count is the length of diagnostics.error_codes, using terse codes such as E_FLOW, E_TPROBE, E_AIR or E_COMMS. delta_t_implausible appears through diagnostics.flow_temp_c and return_temp_c values, never as a flag. meter_works_order appears as site_context.works_orders entries with type METER_EXCH or RECAL, plus open/closed status and date. consecutive_estimates is the count of trailing EST entries in history. seal_status appears as meter.seal_state (intact, broken, null) plus meter.seal_checked_date. A broken seal is matched or unmatched by an ENG history entry or works order on the same date. dispute_open appears as site_context.dispute_open boolean. Decoys: diagnostics.battery_pct low (irrelevant to read validity); a lone E_COMMS code (affects remote transmission only); firmware version; tariff_code; and meter.last_verified_date being old but still within its validity window. No field may state validity, anomaly, fault, deviation percentage, recommended action or risk. Numbers are numbers, dates are ISO, unknowns are null, and there are no free-text fields.

F432.role: Section lead keeper reviewing end-of-shift enclosure logs before they are filed
F432.setting: A mid-sized zoo's animal records system holds one structured log per enclosure per shift, built from keeper hand-held entries. The section lead opens each log the morning after and reconciles head counts, feeding, check rounds and close-of-shift security. They then decide whether to file it, chase a missing entry, act or refer it upward. Logs contain only coded and numeric fields, with no free-text notes.

count_reconciles.instructions: Closing animal count reconciles with opening count and logged movements.

criteria.true: Closing count equals opening plus logged ins minus outs
criteria.false: Counts differ with no matching movement entry

secure_at_close.instructions: Enclosure was confirmed secure at close with no open barrier fault.

criteria.true: Lock checks logged after last round; no unresolved fault
criteria.false: Lock check absent, early, or barrier fault still open

next_step.instructions: What should the section lead do with this log now?

criteria.sign_off: Log complete and consistent; file it with no follow-up.
criteria.request_entry: One named entry or section missing; ask the keeper first.
criteria.recheck_round: Schedule a targeted recheck next round; animals left as they are.
criteria.keeper_action: Send a keeper now to recount, secure or correct on site.
criteria.escalate: Refer to duty vet or curator for a decision beyond lead.

intake_shortfall.instructions: How large is the gap between diet sheet and logged intake?
criteria: None: logged intake at least 90% of diet sheet
Minor: logged intake between 60% and 89% of sheet
Marked: logged intake between 25% and 59% of sheet
Severe: logged intake below 25% of diet sheet

missed_rounds.instructions: How many scheduled check rounds have no logged entry?
criteria: Every scheduled round has a logged entry
Exactly one scheduled round has no entry
Two or three scheduled rounds have no entry
Four or more scheduled rounds lack entries

factors.name: count_discrepancy
factors.description: Relationship between shift.opening_count, shift.closing_count and movements list; a gap may be covered by a transfer entry or left unexplained

factors.name: barrier_fault
factors.description: State of any barrier or door fault ticket in close_check

factors.name: lock_check_timing
factors.description: Whether lock checks are logged and whether their timestamps fall after the last round and before shift end

factors.name: intake_ratio
factors.description: Offered weight minus leftover weight divided by diet sheet weight; values cluster near the 0.6 and 0.9 boundaries

factors.name: intake_mitigation
factors.description: Benign reason for low intake present: diet sheet flags fast day, pre-procedure fast, or scatter feed marked unweighable

factors.name: unrecorded_rounds
factors.description: Number of scheduled rounds in the rounds list with logged false or null entry time

factors.name: cctv_cover
factors.description: Gap rounds carry a cctv_reviewed flag with reviewer id, lowering concern without filling the entry

factors.name: temp_excursion
factors.description: Enclosure temperature readings in rounds compared with enclosure set range

factors.name: heater_maintenance_window
factors.description: Enclosure lists a scheduled maintenance window overlapping the out-of-range readings

factors.name: field_mismatch
factors.description: Minor or major cross-section inconsistency unrelated or related to answers: diet unit kg vs g, animal id in feeding absent from roster, diet sheet date after shift date

factors.name: behaviour_codes
factors.description: Count of concerning coded behaviour observations across rounds (LETH, LAME, STER, AGGR)

factors.name: vet_case_open
factors.description: An active vet case id already covers the flagged animal, lowering need to escalate

factors.name: missing_section
factors.description: One section absent or null, making a decision depend on a single missing item

factors.name: risk_category
factors.description: Dangerous-animal category of the species, affecting how far a security or count gap must be escalated

sections.name: enclosure
sections.description: Enclosure id, species code, risk_cat, roster of animal ids, temp_range_c, maint_window, active_vet_case

sections.name: shift
sections.description: Shift date, keeper_id, start and end times, opening_count, closing_count

sections.name: movements
sections.description: List of transfers in or out with animal_id, direction, time, destination enclosure

sections.name: feeding
sections.description: Diet sheet version date and items with sheet_g, offered_g, leftover_g, unit, fast_flag, scatter_flag

sections.name: rounds
sections.description: Scheduled check rounds with sched_time, logged, entry_time, temp_c, behaviour codes, cctv_reviewed, reviewer_id

sections.name: close_check
sections.description: Lock checks per door with time, barrier fault ticket id, ticket_state, retest_due

F432.rendering_notes: count_discrepancy appears only as numbers in shift.opening_count and shift.closing_count against movements entries; movement_logged_elsewhere puts the transfer in movements with a time inside the shift. barrier_fault shows in close_check.ticket_state (closed, repaired, open) with retest_due date; repaired_retest_pending is a deliberate boundary case for secure_at_close. lock_check_timing shows as per-door times compared with the last rounds.entry_time and shift.end; partial_doors_only omits one door listed in the enclosure. intake_ratio is never stated: it is derived from offered_g minus leftover_g against sheet_g. intake_mitigation sets fast_flag or scatter_flag on an item, or a pre-procedure fast in active_vet_case. unrecorded_rounds shows as logged false or entry_time null; cctv_cover adds cctv_reviewed true with reviewer_id on those rounds only. temp_excursion shows as temp_c values outside enclosure.temp_range_c; heater_maintenance_window overlaps their times. field_mismatch is a decoy or real inconsistency: unit_kg_vs_g records leftover in kg beside sheet in g, so the reader must convert. Behaviour concerns are coded only (LETH, LAME, STER, AGGR) and never explained. A missing_section is rendered as null or an absent key. No field may state a verdict, risk level, shortfall percentage, count of missed rounds, secure/insecure status or recommended action. Timestamps carry harmless minute-level offsets as decoys. No free-text fields at all.

F433.role: Veterinary panel reviewer at an endurance ride vet gate, checking each horse's completed inspection card before it may start the next loop
F433.setting: A one-day endurance ride run over several loops, with a vet gate after each loop. When a horse arrives at a gate, the crew has a fixed recovery window to bring its pulse down. The horse is then presented to a gate vet, who records pulse, a cardiac recovery index (CRI), metabolic signs, a gait grade from a trot-up and any tack injuries. The panel reviewer reads the combined record of timing, vet card, treatment log and notes, then decides whether the horse is fit to continue, what outcome code applies, how serious the welfare risk is and whether the record is complete. Ride rules are stated in the record: pulse limit, recovery window and hold length.

pulse_met.instructions: Horse met the pulse criterion within the permitted recovery window.

next_step.instructions: What should the panel do with this vet card now?

criteria.clear_to_continue: All parameters met and recorded; horse proceeds without further action.
criteria.request_recheck: One reading or trot-up missing; obtain it before deciding.
criteria.eliminate_ftq: Clear failure recorded; enter fail-to-qualify and stop the horse now.
