criteria.refer_president: Treatment, rule breach or dispute; pass to veterinary commission president.

outcome_code.instructions: Which outcome code best fits this inspection's findings?

criteria.pass: Pulse, gait, metabolic and tack checks all within limits.
criteria.ftq_other: Only a wound, tack injury or procedural breach fails.
criteria.ftq_gait: Gait irregular on trot-up while metabolic parameters remain acceptable.
criteria.ftq_metabolic: Pulse or metabolic parameter failed while gait remains regular.
criteria.ftq_combined: Both gait and at least one metabolic parameter failed.

welfare_risk.instructions: How serious is the welfare risk to this horse now?
criteria: Low: every recorded parameter within the gate limits.
Elevated: exactly one parameter outside limits, none severe.
High: two or more parameters outside gate limits.
Critical: pulse above 80 or horse on course uncleared.

record_completeness.instructions: How complete is this horse's inspection record?
criteria: Two or more required readings or signatures missing.
Exactly one required reading or signature missing.
All readings present, but one time out of sequence.
All readings present, signed, and times in sequence.

factors.name: pulse_status
factors.description: Where the presented pulse sits against the stated limit and window: well under, exactly at the limit, met only after the window closed, or not met at all.

factors.name: time_mismatch
factors.description: Difference between the arrival time in the gate section and the arrival time copied onto the vet card. When large, it changes whether the window was met.

factors.name: gait_grade
factors.description: Lameness grade recorded at the trot-up: regular, inconsistent grade 1, or irregular grade 2 or above.

factors.name: gait_mitigation
factors.description: A benign explanation for the gait observation, such as a second trot-up on firm ground graded regular, or a passport note of a long-standing conformational irregularity seen at earlier gates.

factors.name: metabolic_flags
factors.description: Number of metabolic parameters recorded outside normal limits: mucous membranes, capillary refill, gut sounds, skin tent.

factors.name: cri_rise
factors.description: Rise in bpm between the first CRI pulse and the second pulse taken after the trot-up. Above 4 is a concern.

factors.name: missing_items
factors.description: Count of required vet-card entries left null: a CRI reading, the gait grade, the vet signature or the presentation time.

factors.name: out_of_sequence
factors.description: A logged time that cannot be right, such as a re-inspection stamped before the first exam or a presentation stamped before arrival.

factors.name: tack_wound
factors.description: Tack or girth injury noted on the card: none, a minor rub with no broken skin, or an open wound.

factors.name: prior_gate_history
factors.description: Results from this horse's earlier gates today: all clean, one earlier recheck, or a borderline pulse at a previous gate.

factors.name: treatment_logged
factors.description: Treatment entry for this gate: none, treatment approved by the vet (for example cooling or oral electrolytes), or invasive treatment such as IV fluids, which bars continuation.

factors.name: departed_before_clearance
factors.description: Aggravating fact: the gate departure time falls before the vet signature time, or before a required re-inspection, so the horse went out on course uncleared.

factors.name: note_tone
factors.description: Free-text rider or crew note: none, a benign explanation that bears on the findings, or an alarming remark about something irrelevant (decoy).

sections.name: horse
sections.description: Horse id, name, passport number, age, and a list of earlier gate results today.

sections.name: gate
sections.description: Loop number, ride rules (pulse limit, recovery window, hold length), and arrival and departure times.

sections.name: vet_card
sections.description: Presentation time, pulse readings, CRI pair, metabolic parameters, trot-up gait grades, tack findings and vet signature time.

sections.name: treatment
sections.description: List of treatments given at this gate with time, type and approving vet; null if none.

sections.name: notes
sections.description: Short free-text rider note and a one-line vet remark.

F433.rendering_notes: Rule values sit in gate.rules: pulse_limit_bpm (usually 64), recovery_window_min (usually 20) and hold_min. pulse_status appears only as vet_card.pulse_bpm and vet_card.presented_at, which must be compared with gate.arrived_at plus the window. Nothing says whether the pulse was met. time_mismatch puts a separate vet_card.arrival_copied value that can differ from gate.arrived_at, and which one is used can flip the window result. gait_grade appears as vet_card.trot_ups, a list of objects with surface and grade. gait_mitigation adds a second trot-up graded regular, or a horse.passport_remark such as 'known left fore irregularity, regular at loops 1-2'. metabolic_flags sets values in vet_card.metabolic (mm: 'pink'/'pale'/'injected', crt_s, gut_sounds per quadrant, skin_tent_s), with no count given. cri_rise is shown as vet_card.cri: {first_bpm, second_bpm}. missing_items nulls fields such as cri.second_bpm, gait grade, vet_signed_at or presented_at. out_of_sequence produces an impossible timestamp ordering. tack_wound appears in vet_card.tack: {site, finding}. prior_gate_history fills horse.earlier_gates. treatment_logged fills treatment entries; invasive treatment is visible only as type 'iv_fluids', with no flag. departed_before_clearance shows only as gate.departed_at earlier than vet_card.vet_signed_at, or departed_at present while a recheck is pending. note_tone writes notes.rider_note, for example 'girth slipped on the climb, rub is old' or the decoy 'nearly lost a shoe on the road section' when the feet are fine. Other decoys: horse.age, gate.ambient_temp_c, and a vet_remark of 'busy gate, long queue'. Never include fields such as result, outcome, risk, fit_to_continue or complete; every answer must be inferred by comparison across sections.

F434.role: Course safety coordinator reviewing post-shift marshal point reports for a closed-road cycling race
F434.setting: After each stage of a multi-day closed-road road race, every marshal post files a structured shift report. The course safety coordinator checks each report against race control's own log, the sweep vehicle record and the medical handover list. For each report the coordinator decides whether the post was properly held, what kind of incident occurred, how serious the worst consequence was, and what follow-up the report needs before the next stage.

coverage_held.instructions: Marshals held the post continuously until the sweep vehicle passed.

criteria.true: Signed-in coverage spans first rider to sweep passage.
criteria.false: Coverage gap, early departure, or sweep time unverifiable.

next_step.instructions: What should the safety coordinator do with this report next?

criteria.file: Report matches control record and no safety items remain open.
criteria.query_marshal: Clerical mismatch only, correctable by the post marshal directly.
criteria.hold_confirm: One outcome awaits confirmation from medical or race control.
criteria.safety_review: Confirmed safety failure needing formal review by the safety panel.

incident_class.instructions: Which category describes the most serious incident at this post?

criteria.no_incident: Neither post log nor control record lists an incident here.
criteria.mechanical_only: Only punctures or mechanical stops recorded; no rider fell.
criteria.rider_fall: At least one rider fell; nothing entered the closed course.
criteria.course_intrusion: A vehicle, person or animal entered the closed course.

reversal_time.instructions: How long would it take to fully undo this outcome?
criteria: Could be fully undone within one day
Needs one to seven days to undo
Needs eight days to three months to undo
Cannot be undone within three months

consequence_severity.instructions: How serious is the worst confirmed safety consequence at this post?
criteria: No rider fell, was injured, or met traffic
Rider fell but continued without medic attendance
Medic attended or rider abandoned, no hospital transfer
Hospital transfer, or riders met reopened traffic

factors.name: reopen_before_sweep
factors.description: Race control reopened this road section to traffic before the sweep vehicle and last riders had passed the post; riders rode into live traffic. Decisive aggravating fact.

factors.name: incident_mix
factors.description: Most serious incident type that actually occurred at the post, after reconciling post log with control log.

factors.name: control_log_mismatch
factors.description: Kind of discrepancy between the post incident list and race control's log for this km range.

factors.name: intrusion_mitigated
factors.description: When an intrusion occurred, a moto marshal escort or a rider hold kept riders and intruder apart with no contact.

factors.name: worst_rider_outcome
factors.description: Worst outcome for any rider involved in an incident at this post.

factors.name: staffing_gap
factors.description: Pattern of marshal presence relative to first rider and sweep passage.

factors.name: relief_swap_logged
factors.description: A relief marshal signed in to cover an apparent staffing gap, which may close the gap.

factors.name: radio_check_failures
factors.description: Number of failed scheduled radio checks from the post; alarming but often covered by a successful backup phone contact.

factors.name: medic_arrival_minutes
factors.description: Minutes from medic call to medic arrival, when a medic was called.

factors.name: medical_handover_confirmed
factors.description: Race control's medical handover list carries a matching reference for the post's medical incident.

factors.name: sweep_record_missing
factors.description: The sweep vehicle passage record for this post is absent, so coverage to sweep cannot be verified.

factors.name: timestamp_boundary
factors.description: Marshal off-post time falls within one minute of the sweep passage time, leaving coverage on a boundary.

sections.name: event
sections.description: Stage identifiers, date, road closure window and rider start count.

sections.name: post
sections.description: Marshal post location, type, roster, sign-in and sign-off times, relief swaps.

sections.name: incidents
sections.description: Post-logged incident list with times, km, type, bibs, medic and rider status.

sections.name: comms
sections.description: Scheduled radio checks, backup phone contacts and escalations to race control.

sections.name: control_record
sections.description: Race control's incident log, medical handovers, abandonments and road reopening times.

sections.name: sweep
sections.description: Sweep vehicle passage time, last rider bib and post clearance time; may be null.

F434.rendering_notes: event: event_id, stage_no, date (ISO), closure_start, closure_end, riders_started. post: post_id, km_marker, post_type (junction, descent, roundabout, feed_zone), marshals_rostered, marshals_signed_in, on_post_from, off_post_at, relief list of {marshal_ref, signed_in, signed_out}. incidents: list of {inc_ref, time, km, type (mechanical, fall, vehicle_on_course, pedestrian_on_course, animal_on_course), bibs, medic_called, medic_cancelled, medic_arrival_min, rider_status (continued, abandoned, transferred), escort_present, riders_held}. comms: radio_checks list of {time, ok}, backup_phone list of {time, ok}, escalations list of {time, inc_ref, acknowledged}. control_record: incident_log list of {ctl_ref, time, km, type, bibs}, medical_handovers list of {ref, bib, km, destination}, abandonments list of bibs, road_reopened_at map of km range to ISO time. sweep: passed_at, last_rider_bib, post_cleared_at, or the whole section null. Factor mapping: reopen_before_sweep shows only as road_reopened_at for the range covering km_marker earlier than sweep.passed_at, with last_rider_bib passing after it; never as a flag. incident_mix is set by the reconciled union of post and control incidents near km_marker; control_log_mismatch renders as a 1 to 4 minute time offset (trivial), a swapped digit in a bib, a control incident absent from the post list, or a post incident absent from control. intrusion_mitigated renders as escort_present or riders_held true with no fall in the same minute. worst_rider_outcome renders via rider_status, medic_called/medic_cancelled, abandonments and medical_handovers destination (hospital name vs race_medical_tent). medical_handover_confirmed absent with a medic-attended incident supports hold. staffing_gap renders through on_post_from vs first rider time, gaps in signed_in counts, and off_post_at vs sweep.passed_at; relief_swap_logged adds a relief entry covering the gap, sometimes only partially. radio_check_failures appear as ok false entries, with backup_phone ok true about half the time. sweep_record_missing nulls the sweep section. timestamp_boundary sets off_post_at within 60 seconds of sweep.passed_at. Decoys: medical_handovers to hospital for bibs at other km markers; medic_called true later cancelled; vehicle entries for official race vehicles listed in control; small time offsets that match the same incident. No field may state coverage status, severity, category or recommended action; answers must be derived by comparing sections.

F435.role: Venue safety officer reviewing zone capacity check records
F435.setting: A large concert venue's event safety office. After doors open, every audience zone at each event produces one capacity check record. It holds the zone's licence terms and limits, ticketing figures, ingress counter readings, steward sign-ins and the exit route inspection log. The safety officer reviews one zone record at a time. They decide whether occupancy was verifiably over limit, what to do next, what drove any discrepancy, how short stewarding was, and how many exit routes went unconfirmed before doors.

verified_exceedance.instructions: A zone's verified occupancy exceeded its effective licensed limit during this event.

disposition.instructions: What should the safety officer do with this zone check?

criteria.sign_off: Counts, staffing and exits all reconcile; approve with no follow-up.
criteria.conditional_sign_off: Approve now; only minor gaps already being remedied are logged.
criteria.hold: Withhold approval until one missing confirmation or recount arrives.
criteria.restrict_entry: Event live with verified risk; pause admissions to the zone.
criteria.escalate: Event ended with verified breach; refer to licensing authority.

discrepancy_source.instructions: What is the main source of any over-limit discrepancy?

criteria.none: Verified counts and tickets issued stay within effective limit.
criteria.counter_fault: Only a device flagged faulty shows counts above the limit.
criteria.ticket_overissue: Tickets issued exceed even the limit ticketing itself used.
criteria.limit_mismatch: Ticketing applied a zone limit differing from the effective licence.

steward_shortfall.instructions: How far below the required steward count was signed-in deployment?
criteria: Met: signed-in stewards equal or exceed the required number
Slight: under 10% below the required number
Marked: 10% to under 25% below required
Severe: 25% or more below, or roster absent

unconfirmed_exits.instructions: How many exit routes lacked a clear check before doors?
criteria: Every exit route checked clear before doors opened
Exactly one exit route lacked a pre-doors clear check
Exactly two exit routes lacked a pre-doors clear check
Three or four exit routes lacked a clear check
Five or more routes, or no exit log

factors.name: zone_type
factors.description: Kind of audience zone. Changes typical limits, steward requirements and number of exit routes without changing the decision logic.

factors.name: event_phase
factors.description: Whether the check was filed while the event is still live or after it ended. Separates restrict_entry from escalate.

factors.name: occupancy_ratio
factors.description: True peak occupancy divided by the effective zone limit. Values near 1.0 sit on the boundary.

factors.name: counter_status
factors.description: State of the ingress counter device. calibration_due is a decoy, as the reading remains valid. fault_logged makes the raw reading unverified.

factors.name: counter_inflation
factors.description: Fractional over-read added to the raw counter peak, applied only when counter_status is fault_logged. It can push a within-limit zone apparently over.

factors.name: manual_recount_present
factors.description: Whether a timestamped manual clicker recount exists. It gives the true occupancy and can rescue a faulty counter reading.

factors.name: capacity_variation
factors.description: Temporary raised limit. Only approved_in_time changes the effective limit. approved_late has an approval date after doors_open. pending has no approval date.

factors.name: tickets_issued_ratio
factors.description: Tickets issued for the zone, including complimentary tickets, divided by the effective limit.

factors.name: limit_mismatch
factors.description: Ticketing configured the zone with a limit different from the effective licence limit, such as a stale base limit or an unapproved variation figure.

factors.name: steward_gap_pct
factors.description: Signed-in stewards below the required number, as a fraction of required. Negative values mean a surplus. Values cluster near the 10% and 25% anchors.

factors.name: relief_called
factors.description: Relief stewards have been called with an ETA. This mitigates disposition only; it never changes the signed-in count.

factors.name: roster_missing
factors.description: The stewarding section is null, so deployment cannot be shown.

factors.name: exits_unconfirmed
factors.description: Number of listed exit routes with no clear check timestamped before doors. Causes are a missing entry, a null checked_at, a check after doors_open, or an obstructed status with no clear recheck before doors.

factors.name: exit_log_missing
factors.description: The exit_checks section is null, so every route counts as unconfirmed.

sections.name: event
sections.description: event_id, zone_id, zone_type, doors_open and check_filed_at timestamps, phase.

sections.name: licence
sections.description: base_limit, variation object or null, stewards_required, exit_routes list of route ids.

sections.name: ticketing
sections.description: zone_limit_used, issued, comps_included, scanned_in.

sections.name: ingress
sections.description: device_id, device_status, raw_peak, peak_at, manual_recount object or null.

sections.name: stewarding
sections.description: rostered, signed_in, relief object or null; whole section may be null.

sections.name: exit_checks
sections.description: List of route checks with route_id, checked_at, status; may be null.

F435.rendering_notes: event: phase is live or post_event; doors_open and check_filed_at are ISO datetimes. licence: base_limit is an integer. variation is null for none; otherwise {ref, new_limit, status, approved_on}. approved_in_time has approved_on before doors_open. approved_late has approved_on after doors_open, often the same day, which is out-of-order evidence that the variation does not apply. pending has status "pending" and approved_on null. The effective limit is new_limit only for approved_in_time, otherwise base_limit; the reader must derive it. stewards_required is an integer; exit_routes lists 3 to 8 route ids. ticketing: zone_limit_used equals the effective limit unless limit_mismatch, in which case it shows base_limit or the late or pending new_limit. issued = round(tickets_issued_ratio x effective limit). comps_included is a decoy subset already inside issued. scanned_in is a decoy, slightly below issued because of no-shows and re-entries. Source rule: ticket_overissue applies when issued exceeds zone_limit_used. limit_mismatch applies when issued exceeds the effective limit but not zone_limit_used. counter_fault applies when only a fault_logged raw_peak exceeds the limit. ingress: raw_peak = true occupancy, times (1 + counter_inflation) when device_status is fault_logged. calibration_due is a decoy and still valid. manual_recount is {count, at} with count equal to true occupancy, or null. Verified occupancy is raw_peak when the device is ok or calibration_due. When the device is fault_logged, verified occupancy is the recount; with no recount it is unverified, so the exceedance claim is false and the record usually needs hold. stewarding: signed_in = round(stewards_required x (1 - steward_gap_pct)). rostered is a decoy and is always at least signed_in. relief is {called_at, eta_min} or null; it mitigates disposition only. The section is null when roster_missing. exit_checks: one entry per checked route. Unconfirmed routes show as an absent route_id, a null checked_at, a checked_at after doors_open, or status "obstructed" with no later "clear" entry before doors. Some unconfirmed routes have a decoy "clear" recheck after doors. The section is null when exit_log_missing. Contested cases: verified occupancy within 1% of the limit; recount disagreeing with an ok-status counter by a few people; steward gaps that round onto 10% or 25%; approved_on minutes after doors. No field may state the answers: never include breach, verified_occupancy, effective_limit, shortfall, unconfirmed_count, risk or recommendation fields. Every answer must be derived by comparing values across sections.

F436.role: Corrections editor on a regional daily newspaper's standards desk, reviewing one reader correction request at a time against the published article, the reporter's notes and the source documents
F436.setting: A corrections request queue. Each record bundles a published article's metadata and disputed passage, the reader's complaint, the desk's evidence check against reporter notes and source documents, the article's edit and correction history, and any draft correction already written. The editor decides whether a real error exists, what to do now, where the error came from, how far it spread and how serious it is.

error_confirmed.instructions: The published article contains a factual error confirmed by documentary evidence.

criteria.true: Source document contradicts what was published.
criteria.false: Matches source, unverified, or only a dispute of opinion.

next_step.instructions: What should the desk do with this request now?

criteria.no_action: Close request; published text stands or is already correctly amended.
criteria.request_evidence: Hold and ask for one named missing document first.
criteria.correct_now: Amend and publish correction once draft wording matches source.
criteria.escalate: Refer to standards editor or legal before any change.

error_origin.instructions: At which stage was the published inaccuracy first introduced?

criteria.no_inaccuracy: Published text matches the best available source record.
criteria.source_supplied: Outside source gave the wrong fact; reporter quoted it faithfully.
criteria.reporter_drafting: Reporter's filed copy differs from their own notes or documents.
criteria.editing_stage: Filed copy was correct; error added during subbing or headlining.

spread.instructions: How widely was the disputed version distributed before review?
criteria: Online only, live under 24 hours
Online only, live 24 hours or longer
Online plus exactly one of print or syndication
Online, print edition and syndication partners all carried it

harm_severity.instructions: How serious is the disputed error if left uncorrected?
criteria: Cosmetic: spelling, style or punctuation; no fact changed
Minor: wrong incidental fact, no named party affected
Material: wrong fact attributed to a named person or organisation
Grave: wrongly implies a named party committed wrongdoing

factors.name: error_status
factors.description: Whether the evidence actually shows an error: source contradicts published text, source agrees, evidence cannot yet settle it, or the complaint disputes interpretation rather than fact

factors.name: error_origin_stage
factors.description: Stage where the wrong fact first appears when comparing source document, reporter notes, filed copy and published text; none when no error

factors.name: discrepancy_field
factors.description: Which kind of value differs between sections: a figure, a personal or place name, a date, a job title or role, or headline wording

factors.name: discrepancy_size
factors.description: How large the mismatch is between published value and source value, from a one-letter slip to a wholly different fact

factors.name: claim_type
factors.description: Nature of the disputed passage: cosmetic, incidental fact, fact about a named party, or implication of wrongdoing by a named party

factors.name: hours_live
factors.description: Hours between first online publication and the review timestamp, derived from two dates rather than stated

factors.name: distribution_channels
factors.description: Channels beyond the website that carried the disputed version: none, print only, syndication only, or both

factors.name: mitigation_present
factors.description: A benign explanation that lowers concern: error already silently fixed before syndication pickup, source has since issued its own revised figure, or print edition went out before the error was introduced

factors.name: missing_evidence
factors.description: One key document is absent: reporter notes not attached, or complainant's cited source not supplied, leaving the comparison incomplete

factors.name: legal_signal
factors.description: Complainant or named party mentions solicitors or formal action; mitigated in about half of cases by a note that legal has already reviewed and cleared routine correction

factors.name: legal_cleared
factors.description: Given a legal signal, whether history shows legal already reviewed and cleared standard correction handling

factors.name: draft_fix_mismatch
factors.description: Draft correction exists but its stated value or name differs from the source document, so the fix is drafted but not yet usable

factors.name: prior_corrections
factors.description: Number of earlier corrections logged on the same article; a decoy that raises suspicion but does not decide any answer

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Record placed on a scale boundary: hours_live within an hour of 24, or a passage naming a party only indirectly, splitting judges

sections.name: article
sections.description: Published piece: slug, section, byline, first_published_at, channels list, disputed_passage text and headline

sections.name: complaint
sections.description: Reader request: received_at, complainant_type, claimed_correct_value, cited_source, one-sentence summary

sections.name: desk_check
sections.description: Evidence comparison: source_doc value, reporter_notes value, filed_copy value, attachments list, reporter_note free text

sections.name: history
sections.description: Edit log and prior corrections: list of timestamped edits, prior correction count, legal review entries

sections.name: draft_correction
sections.description: Proposed fix, possibly null: draft text, stated corrected value, drafted_by, drafted_at

F436.rendering_notes: error_status shows only by comparing article.disputed_passage with desk_check.source_doc (confirmed), agreement between them (matches_source), source_doc null or 'awaiting' (unverifiable_pending), or complaint.summary objecting to characterisation not a value (opinion_dispute). error_origin_stage is found by locating the first divergence along desk_check.source_doc -> reporter_notes -> filed_copy -> article.disputed_passage; editing_stage also shows as a history edit by a sub-editor after filing. discrepancy_field and discrepancy_size set which value differs and by how much (e.g. 1,240 vs 1,420; Smyth vs Smith; 14 March vs 4 March). claim_type is implicit in the disputed passage wording (typo, incidental count, attribution to a named councillor or firm, implied fraud or assault). hours_live is never stated: compute from article.first_published_at and the record's review_at in complaint or history. distribution_channels appear in article.channels list; mitigation can show history evidence that print went out before the erroneous edit, so print copy was not affected. mitigation_present appears as a history entry or reporter_note line (silent fix timestamp, source's own revised release). missing_evidence shows as an attachment listed but null, or cited_source with no matching document. legal_signal appears in complaint.summary; legal_cleared as a history legal review entry. draft_fix_mismatch shows as draft_correction.stated_value differing from source_doc. prior_corrections is a decoy count. Decoys: complainant_type 'subject_of_story' sounds alarming but does not decide anything; reporter_note may defend the copy confidently even when notes contradict it; a high prior_corrections count with no current error. Never include fields such as error_confirmed, severity, origin, spread level or recommended_action; the record must not state any answer.

F437.role: Quality assurance linguist at a translation agency, checking each completed job record before the deliverable is released to the client
F437.setting: A mid-sized translation agency routes every finished job through a QA linguist. The QA linguist opens one job record at a time and compares several things: the order, the source file, the delivered target file, the automated QA report, the bilingual review and the job's history. They then decide whether the deliverable can go out, what is wrong with it and what happens next. Mismatches between sections are never flagged by the system. The reviewer must find them by comparing values.

scope_matches.instructions: Delivered file covers the full ordered source scope and version.

criteria.true: Segment counts and source version agree with the order.
criteria.false: Segments missing, wrong version, or counts disagree materially.

reviewed_in_time.instructions: Independent review was completed and signed off before client delivery.

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this job record now?

criteria.release: Deliver now; counts, checks and sign-off all consistent.
criteria.hold_for_item: One named artefact missing; request it before deciding.
criteria.return_for_fix: Fixable errors found; translator corrects and resubmits before deadline.
criteria.escalate_am: Client terms breached or late; account manager must decide.

open_severity.instructions: What is the highest severity of errors still open?
criteria: None: no open errors in QA or review
Minor: open errors are all minor severity
Major: at least one major error, none critical
Critical: at least one critical error still open

parties_needed.instructions: How many separate people or teams must act to resolve this?
criteria: One person can resolve it alone
Two people or teams must act
Three or four people or teams must act
Five or more people or teams must act

factors.name: scope_mismatch
factors.description: How the delivered segments and word count relate to the ordered source scope and version.

factors.name: locale_mismatch
factors.description: Delivered target locale differs from the locale on the order, e.g. pt-BR delivered against a pt-PT order.

factors.name: glossary_version_state
factors.description: Termbase version used in the deliverable compared with the version required by the order.

factors.name: review_status
factors.description: State and timing of the independent bilingual review relative to delivery.

factors.name: open_error_profile
factors.description: Highest severity among errors still unresolved across the QA report and the review.

factors.name: auto_qa_present
factors.description: Whether the automated QA report was run and attached; if false the qa_report section is null.

factors.name: qa_false_positive_share
factors.description: Share of automated QA flags the translator marked as false positives, which inflates raw flag counts as a decoy.

factors.name: number_mismatch_count
factors.description: Numbers, dates or units in target segments that disagree with the source, found by comparing segment samples.

factors.name: deadline_slack_hours
factors.description: Hours between delivery (or now, if undelivered) and the client due time; negative means late.

factors.name: client_waiver
factors.description: Mitigation: the order terms record that the client accepted the older glossary, a locale variant or a revised due date.

factors.name: prior_revision_rounds
factors.description: Count of earlier rejections or revision rounds on this job or the same client project.

factors.name: dtp_step_pending
factors.description: A required desktop publishing or layout step is listed in the workflow but has no completion date.

sections.name: job
sections.description: Order data: job_id, client_ref, lang_pair, target_locale, ordered_words, source_version, glossary_version, due_at, terms flags, workflow steps.

sections.name: source
sections.description: Source file facts: file_id, version, segment_count, word_count, repetitions and fuzzy breakdown.

sections.name: deliverable
sections.description: Target file facts: file_id, built_from_version, target_locale, segments_translated, word_count, glossary_version_used, delivered_at.

sections.name: qa_report
sections.description: Automated QA run: run_at, flag counts by category, false_positive_marked, number_mismatches list, unresolved by severity; may be null.

sections.name: review
sections.description: Bilingual review: reviewer_id, assigned_at, completed_at, signed_off, errors list with severity and status; may be null.

sections.name: history
sections.description: Prior events: revision_rounds, previous rejections with dates, reassignments.

F437.rendering_notes: scope_mismatch shows only by comparing job.source_version, source.version and deliverable.built_from_version, and source.segment_count with deliverable.segments_translated. trivial_count_drift changes word_count by under 1% while segments match; this is a decoy explained by the repetitions breakdown. locale_mismatch appears as job.target_locale differing from deliverable.target_locale. glossary_version_state compares job.glossary_version with deliverable.glossary_version_used; not_recorded sets the latter to null. review_status is rendered through review.completed_at against deliverable.delivered_at, review.signed_off, or review being null; in_progress has assigned_at but completed_at null. open_error_profile is spread across review.errors items with status open/closed and qa_report.unresolved counts; closed critical errors are decoys. When auto_qa_present is false, qa_report is null. qa_false_positive_share inflates qa_report flag totals while false_positive_marked offsets them. number_mismatch_count appears as entries in qa_report.number_mismatches (source value vs target value) and may duplicate open review errors. deadline_slack_hours is implied only by job.due_at against deliverable.delivered_at; there is no lateness field. client_waiver appears as job.terms booleans (variant_accepted, glossary_exception, due_revised_to with a new date), which sometimes cover the exact mismatch present and sometimes an unrelated one. prior_revision_rounds is the length of history.revision_rounds. dtp_step_pending is a job.workflow entry with step 'dtp' and done_at null. No free-text fields. The record never contains fields such as release_ready, severity_overall, recommended_action or scope_ok. All dates are ISO, all counts are numbers, and unknowns are null.

F438.role: Clinical coding auditor reviewing one sampled inpatient episode at a time against its source documentation
F438.setting: A hospital clinical coding department runs a rolling audit. Each sample is a single completed inpatient episode pulled from the coded data. The auditor compares the assigned diagnosis and procedure codes with structured extracts from the clinical documentation, regroups the episode and checks the coder's history. For each sample the auditor decides whether the codes stand, whether anything is missing, how many errors exist, how serious the worst one is, and whether the episode needs correction, regrouping or referral to the coding lead.

primary_supported.instructions: Primary diagnosis code is supported by the clinical documentation.

hrg_shift.instructions: Corrected coding would move the episode into a different HRG.

criteria.true: Regrouped HRG differs from the submitted HRG
criteria.false: Regrouped HRG matches, or regrouping not yet possible

next_step.instructions: What should happen to this audit sample now?

criteria.accept_as_coded: Coding matches documentation; sample closes with no changes.
criteria.request_records: A named document or query answer is needed before deciding.
criteria.amend_codes: Correct codes locally; correction leaves the submitted HRG unchanged.
criteria.amend_and_regroup: Correct codes, regroup and flag the tariff change for resubmission.
criteria.escalate_to_lead: Refer to coding lead for unsupported billable codes or integrity concerns.

error_count.instructions: How many coding errors does this audit sample contain?
criteria: No coding errors found against the documentation
Exactly one coding error found
Two or three coding errors found
Four or more coding errors found

error_severity.instructions: How serious is the most consequential coding error found?
criteria: None: no error alters any assigned code
Cosmetic: sequencing or specificity slip, same clinical meaning
Minor: secondary code wrong or missing, HRG unchanged
Major: primary diagnosis wrong or regrouped HRG differs
Critical: billed code has no supporting documentation entry

factors.name: primary_dx_match
factors.description: How the coded primary diagnosis relates to the documented principal condition: exact match, same category but differing fourth character, or a different condition altogether.

factors.name: secondary_discrepancies
factors.description: Number of secondary diagnosis codes that are missing from, or not supported by, the documented comorbidities and complications list.

factors.name: procedure_mismatch
factors.description: State of the coded procedures against the theatre log: all match, one procedure date or laterality differs, or a documented procedure is not coded.

factors.name: regroup_outcome
factors.description: Result of regrouping with corrected codes: same HRG, different HRG within the same subchapter, different subchapter, or regrouping blocked because a source document is absent.

factors.name: missing_source
factors.description: Which, if any, key source document is absent from the documentation extract, preventing confirmation of some codes.

factors.name: clinician_query
factors.description: Status of any query raised with the responsible clinician about an uncertain diagnosis: none raised, outstanding, answered confirming the code, or answered contradicting it.

factors.name: approved_local_convention
factors.description: Whether an approved local coding convention listed in the audit context covers the apparent primary or secondary discrepancy, making it compliant rather than an error.

factors.name: pre_submission
factors.description: Whether the episode has not yet been submitted to the commissioner, so any correction carries no resubmission or tariff recovery.

factors.name: coder_recent_audit_passed
factors.description: Whether the coder's most recent audit was passed with high accuracy; a mitigating decoy that does not change the facts of this sample.

factors.name: coder_error_rate
factors.description: Coder's historical error rate across prior audits; an alarming-looking decoy that should not on its own change any decision.

factors.name: boundary_case
factors.description: Whether a discrepancy hinges on a classification boundary, such as acute versus chronic or a fourth character that standards leave open, splitting reasonable auditors.

factors.name: unsupported_billable_code
factors.description: Decisive aggravating fact: a coded procedure or complication that raises the tariff has no corresponding entry anywhere in the documentation or theatre log.

sections.name: episode
sections.description: Episode identifiers, admission and discharge dates, specialty, length of stay and admission method.

sections.name: clinical_documentation
sections.description: Structured extract of documented diagnoses, procedures with dates and sides, and document presence flags.

sections.name: coded_record
sections.description: Assigned primary and secondary diagnosis codes and procedure codes with dates and laterality.

sections.name: grouping
sections.description: Submitted HRG, auditor regrouped HRG, tariff values and commissioner submission status.

sections.name: audit_context
sections.description: Sample metadata, approved local coding conventions applied, and clinician query records with status.

sections.name: coder_history
sections.description: Coder pseudonymous id, prior audit count, historical error rate and last audit result.

F438.rendering_notes: No free-text fields; all content is codes, dates, numbers, flags and enumerations. primary_dx_match appears only by comparing coded_record.primary_dx.code with clinical_documentation.principal_condition.code (same three characters with different fourth for specificity_differs). secondary_discrepancies is the count of mismatches between coded_record.secondary_dx[] and clinical_documentation.comorbidities[]; never stated as a count. procedure_mismatch appears as differing date or side between coded_record.procedures[] and clinical_documentation.theatre_log[], or a theatre_log entry with no coded counterpart. regroup_outcome appears as grouping.hrg_submitted versus grouping.hrg_regrouped (hrg_regrouped null and grouping.regroup_status 'blocked_missing_source' when not_regroupable); tariff_submitted and tariff_regrouped follow. missing_source sets clinical_documentation.documents_present.{discharge_summary,operation_note,pathology_report} to false and blanks the corresponding lists. clinician_query appears in audit_context.queries[] with target_code, status ('open','closed') and response ('confirms','contradicts', null). approved_local_convention appears as an entry in audit_context.local_conventions_applied[] whose code_pair matches the discrepancy; when absent the list may hold unrelated decoy conventions. pre_submission appears as grouping.submitted_to_commissioner false with submission_date null. coder_recent_audit_passed and coder_error_rate appear in coder_history.last_audit_result and coder_history.error_rate; both are decoys. boundary_case appears as a code pair where the documented term maps to two adjacent codes, e.g. documentation listing both acute and chronic forms. unsupported_billable_code appears as a coded procedure or complication code in coded_record with no matching entry in any documentation list and a positive tariff difference; it must not be flagged by any field. Never include fields such as error_found, severity, accuracy, outcome or recommended_action; the auditor must derive every answer by comparison.

F439.role: Test centre quality assurance reviewer checking individual practical driving test reports submitted by examiners
F439.setting: A regional driving test centre where every completed practical car test report is sampled or flagged for review. The reviewer reads one submitted report at a time, covering test details, candidate checks, the fault sheet, the recorded outcome, any incident, and the edit trail. They decide whether the result is sound, whether the paperwork is complete, what to do with the report, and how serious the worst issue is.

result_supported.instructions: The recorded result follows from the faults marked on the sheet.

criteria.true: Pass or fail agrees with fault counts and categories.
criteria.false: Result contradicts marked faults, or tallies leave it undecidable.

report_complete.instructions: All mandatory report sections and sign-offs are present and correctly ordered.

criteria.true: Every required field present; sign-offs timestamped after test end.
criteria.false: A required section, field or sign-off missing or misordered.

disposition.instructions: What should the reviewer do with this examiner report?

criteria.accept: No discrepancy or gap; file the report as submitted.
criteria.hold_query: One open point needs examiner confirmation before filing.
criteria.amend_record: Confirmed clerical error fixable from evidence already in the report.
criteria.refer_investigation: Result or conduct issue needs formal investigation; result suspended.

staff_effort.instructions: How much staff time would fully resolving this record require?
criteria: Under one hour of staff time needed
One to eight hours of staff time
One to five working days of staff time
More than five working days of staff time

issue_severity.instructions: How serious is the most significant issue found in this report?
criteria: No discrepancy found between any report sections
Discrepancy present but cannot change result or safety
Discrepancy that could change the recorded pass or fail
Mandatory safety procedure breached during the conducted test

factors.name: fault_profile
factors.description: Underlying pattern of faults on the test: comfortable pass, fail on a serious fault, borderline driving-fault count near the 15-fault limit, or a dangerous fault marked.

factors.name: result_mismatch
factors.description: The recorded outcome contradicts the fault sheet, e.g. pass recorded with a serious fault ticked or with 16 driving faults.

factors.name: tally_error
factors.description: The driving_fault_total field differs from the sum of per-item counts; harmless on clear tests, result-changing on borderline counts.

factors.name: documentation_gap
factors.description: Which required element is absent or out of order: none, debrief record null, licence/ID check null, examiner sign-off missing, or sign-off timestamp earlier than test end time.

factors.name: intervention_recorded
factors.description: Examiner recorded a physical or verbal intervention (dual brake or steering) during the drive; an alarming signal on its own.

factors.name: intervention_explained
factors.description: Intervention is matched by a corresponding serious or dangerous fault on the sheet and a note giving a benign cause; applies independently of whether intervention occurred.

factors.name: continued_after_collision
factors.description: Aggravating: vehicle made contact with a third party or object and the examiner continued the test route instead of terminating it as procedure requires.

factors.name: senior_countersigned
factors.description: A supervising examiner sat in on the test and countersigned the report, lending weight to borderline markings.

factors.name: adverse_conditions
factors.description: Logged weather or road conditions (heavy rain, fog, roadworks diversion) that plausibly explain hesitancy or progress faults.

factors.name: note_alignment
factors.description: How the examiner's free-text note relates to the fault sheet: consistent, vague, or describing an event not marked or marked differently.

factors.name: examiner_complaints_12m
factors.description: Number of upheld candidate complaints against this examiner in the past twelve months; context decoy that never settles a question alone.

factors.name: post_submission_edit
factors.description: Report was edited after initial submission; whether an amendment reason is given varies.

sections.name: test
sections.description: Test reference, date, centre, category, start and end times, route code, conditions logged.

sections.name: candidate
sections.description: Pseudonymous candidate ref, attempt number, licence and ID check fields.

sections.name: fault_sheet
sections.description: List of marked items with driving, serious and dangerous counts, plus driving_fault_total.

sections.name: outcome
sections.description: Recorded result, intervention flag, debrief record, examiner note, sign-off timestamps.

sections.name: incident
sections.description: Null if none; otherwise contact type, time, location, action taken, short description.

sections.name: review_trail
sections.description: Edit history, amendment reason, examiner complaint count, countersignature.

F439.rendering_notes: fault_profile shows only through fault_sheet.items[] (each {item, driving, serious, dangerous}) and driving_fault_total; borderline_count yields totals of 14-16. result_mismatch shows as outcome.result disagreeing with the item counts (pass with any serious/dangerous >0 or >15 driving). tally_error makes driving_fault_total differ from the item sum by 1-3; on borderline counts the true sum and total straddle 15. documentation_gap: debrief_null sets outcome.debrief to null; id_check_null sets candidate.id_check to null; signoff_missing sets outcome.examiner_signoff_at null; signoff_before_end sets examiner_signoff_at earlier than test.end_time. intervention_recorded sets outcome.intervention true with intervention_type; intervention_explained adds a matching serious/dangerous item and a benign cause in outcome.examiner_note (e.g. 'cyclist emerged from blind junction'); without it the note is silent or the sheet has no matching fault. continued_after_collision: incident section populated with contact_type and incident_time, and test.end_time and route_completed true show the route was finished well after incident_time, with incident.action_taken 'continued' or 'noted'; when false and an incident exists, action_taken is 'test_terminated' with end_time shortly after. senior_countersigned fills review_trail.countersigned_by and countersigned_at; adverse_conditions fills test.conditions with a concrete entry. note_alignment drives outcome.examiner_note (one sentence) content. examiner_complaints_12m appears as review_trail.upheld_complaints_12m and is a decoy. post_submission_edit fills review_trail.edits[] with timestamps after submission and amendment_reason text or null. Decoys: high complaint counts on clean reports, adverse conditions on reports without hesitancy faults, attempt_number high, intervention flagged with full explanation. Never include fields such as severity, valid, compliant, recommended_action or review_outcome; the reviewer must derive every answer by comparing sections.

F440.role: Group bookings officer at a regional youth hostel network, checking each school or youth-group booking before it is confirmed
F440.setting: Incoming group bookings for youth hostels arrive as structured records combining the booking request, the submitted group roster, the provisional room allocation, payment status, safeguarding checks for adult leaders and the organiser's booking history. The officer reviews one record at a time and decides whether supervision cover is adequate, whether the deposit position is acceptable, what to do with the booking, how urgent it is and how many unexplained inconsistencies it contains. Policy requires 1 adult per 10 minors aged 13 to 17 and 1 adult per 8 minors under 13 on every night, with ratios computed from roster dates of birth against the arrival date. Female and male minors sleep in separate dorms.

ratio_met.instructions: Supervision ratio meets policy on every night of the stay.

criteria.true: Required adult cover present on all booked nights
criteria.false: At least one night falls below required cover

deposit_covered.instructions: Deposit received covers the amount due under agreed payment terms.

criteria.true: Paid amount meets amount due or approved instalment
criteria.false: Paid amount short with no approved instalment plan

disposition.instructions: What should happen to this group booking next?

criteria.confirm: All checks satisfied; booking released for arrival without conditions.
criteria.confirm_conditional: Confirmable now; one named item must clear before arrival.
criteria.hold: Cannot confirm until one specific missing confirmation is received.
criteria.refer_manager: Several open issues or a policy breach need manager decision.
criteria.decline: Group cannot be accommodated safely; cancel and refund deposit.

urgency.instructions: How soon must this booking be resolved before arrival?
criteria: Routine: arrival more than 30 days away
Soon: arrival between 15 and 30 days away
Pressing: arrival between 4 and 14 days away
Immediate: arrival within 3 days or already today

conflict_count.instructions: How many cross-section conflicts lack a logged amendment explaining them?
criteria: No unexplained conflicts between any sections
Exactly one unexplained conflict between sections
Two or three unexplained conflicts between sections
Four or more unexplained conflicts between sections

factors.name: pax_mismatch
factors.description: Difference between booked headcount and number of people on the roster

factors.name: night_mismatch
factors.description: Booked arrival/departure nights versus nights covered in the room allocation

factors.name: amendment_logged
factors.description: A booking amendment entry exists that accounts for any pax or night mismatch

factors.name: supervision_level
factors.description: Adult cover relative to the age-banded ratio computed from roster dates of birth

factors.name: extra_cover_logged
factors.description: Additional adult cover exists elsewhere (late-joining leader in amendments or hostel warden booked in allocation) that may close a ratio gap

factors.name: deposit_position
factors.description: Deposit paid compared with the deposit due under the booking terms

factors.name: instalment_approved
factors.description: An approved instalment schedule exists whose current due amount is met by the partial payment

factors.name: days_to_arrival
factors.description: Days between the record's review date and the booked arrival date

factors.name: dorm_fit
factors.description: Whether roster sex split fits the allocated single-sex dorm beds

factors.name: leader_checks
factors.description: Status of safeguarding background checks for adults listed on the roster

factors.name: trusted_organiser
factors.description: Organiser holds trusted status from several clean past stays

factors.name: prior_no_shows
factors.description: Count of past bookings by this organiser that ended as no-shows or late cancellations

factors.name: diet_count_drift
factors.description: Decoy: dietary requirement totals in booking versus roster flags differ slightly

sections.name: booking
sections.description: Booking reference, review date, arrival and departure dates, booked pax by age band, dietary totals, amendments list

sections.name: roster
sections.description: List of group members with role, date of birth, sex, dietary flag

sections.name: allocation
sections.description: Provisional rooms with type, sex designation, beds, nights covered, optional warden cover

sections.name: payment
sections.description: Total price, deposit due, amount paid, payment dates, instalment schedule or null

sections.name: safeguarding
sections.description: Per-adult background check status, check date and expiry

sections.name: history
sections.description: Organiser id, trusted flag, past stays count, no-show count, last stay date

F440.rendering_notes: pax_mismatch: booking.pax_by_band totals differ from roster entry count; never stated as a difference. night_mismatch: booking.arrival/departure versus allocation[].nights date lists. amendment_logged: booking.amendments[] entries with type codes (pax_change, date_change), delta and logged_at that exactly account for the mismatch when true; when false amendments is empty or holds an unrelated entry (e.g. diet_change). supervision_level: computed only from roster roles (leader/participant) and dates of birth against arrival; adults leaving early shown by roster[].depart_date, giving one-night shortfall. extra_cover_logged: a leader_add amendment with a new adult or allocation.warden_cover listing nights; when true it may close the gap only for the nights it lists, so sometimes it covers only part. deposit_position and instalment_approved: payment.deposit_due vs payment.paid_total; instalment schedule lists due dates and amounts, and the current due instalment may be met. days_to_arrival: booking.review_date versus booking.arrival. dorm_fit: allocation room sex designation and bed counts versus roster sex counts. leader_checks: safeguarding[] status verified/pending/missing with expiry dates; an expiry before departure counts as pending. trusted_organiser and prior_no_shows: history fields; these are decoys for ratio and deposit questions but bear on disposition in balanced cases. diet_count_drift: booking.diet_totals vs roster diet flags, a trivial conflict that still counts for conflict_count unless amended. No field may state compliance, risk, urgency, conflict counts or a recommended disposition; no status like ratio_ok or deposit_ok. Use null for unknown payment dates or missing check dates. No free-text fields.
